jobs.occupation: Følsgaard is looking for a Customer Relations & Order Manager – MarineTech
jobs.description:
Do you build the kind of customer relationships where trust makes the difference?

At MarineTech, we are looking for a Customer Relations & Order Manager who will take responsibility for a small portfolio of key customers and ensure an excellent customer experience from agreement to delivery.

This is not a traditional sales role focused on hunting for new business. Your success will come from knowing your customers, understanding their needs and business, and building strong, long-term relationships based on trust, reliability and professional advice.

Your role

You will be the customer’s primary point of contact and trusted advisor, working closely with colleagues, suppliers and partners to make sure everything comes together.

You will combine customer relationship management with hands-on responsibility for orders, forecasts and deliveries. This means staying close to your customers, anticipating their needs and ensuring that commitments are followed through.

Your key responsibilities will be to:

• Build, maintain and develop strong relationships with existing customers

• Act as the customer’s primary contact and advise on products, solutions and delivery options

• Manage orders from A to Z, including requirements, prices, terms, documentation and delivery

• Follow up on customer forecasts and coordinate internally to support material and delivery planning

• Coordinate closely with customers, suppliers and internal teams

• Proactively keep customers informed about quotations, orders, deliveries and deviations

• Maintain accurate customer, order and activity data in ERP and CRM

• Identify opportunities to further develop existing customer accounts

• Look forward to 10–15 travel days per year as an opportunity to meet customers, build stronger relationships and get closer to their business.

You probably have experience from B2B customer management, order coordination, sales or customer service. More importantly, you enjoy building relationships and creating a customer experience where people know they can rely on you.

We imagine that you:

• Have experience working with B2B customers and coordinating orders or deliveries

• Have a good commercial understanding and an interest in technical products and solutions

• Are comfortable working with ERP and CRM systems and structured follow-up

• Ideally have experience coordinating with suppliers, carriers and complex deliveries

• Communicate professionally in both Danish and English

As a person

You are outgoing and approachable and naturally create good relationships with customers and colleagues. You are service-minded without losing sight of the commercial perspective.

At the same time, you are structured and proactive. You take ownership, keep an overview when several things are happening at once, and make sure agreements and commitments are followed through to completion.

Why this role?

You will get a role where relationships matter. Rather than constantly chasing the next customer, you will have the opportunity to understand a smaller number of important customers in depth and become a trusted partner in their day-to-day business.

You will be close to both customers and the internal organization, giving you a central role in turning customer needs into reliable solutions and deliveries.

Interested?

If you want to help develop the specialized container and maritime transport industry – while developing yourself professionally and personally – then we look forward to hearing from you.

Send your application and CV as soon as possible. Interviews are held continuously and we will hire once we find the right candidate.

If you have questions, feel free to contact HR Manager Louise Buur at +45 21 20 44 67.

**About Hans Følsgaard (**Hans Følsgaard A/S)

Hans Følsgaard A/S is a global technology company with roots in engineering and a clear ambition to support the green transition through intelligent, reliable solutions. Since 1922, we have provided specialised technology expertise to industry, and our team of more than 120 employees is based across locations in Denmark, Norway, Germany, India and China.

Collaboration, accountability and integrity are at the heart of how we work. We operate with flat organisational structures, take a long-term perspective and value curiosity, professional expertise and initiative.

jobs.employer_name: KU- SCIENCE - CHEM og MATH og NBI-HCØ
jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen

   

  Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applicants for PhD stipends in mathematics.

  The start date is ordinarily September 1, 2027, but can be subject to negotiation.

  There will be PhD stipends available in:

   	
• Algebraic and Arithmetic Geometry, Applied algebra, Combinatorics, Geometric group theory, Geometry and Geometric Analysis, Number Theory, Representation Theory, and Topology as covered by the section Algebra & Geometry and  Copenhagen Center for Geometry & Topology (GeoTop).    	
• Classical Analysis, Descriptive Set Theory, Functional Analysis, Geometric group theory, Harmonic Analysis, History of Mathematics, Mathematical Physics, Operator Algebras, Partial Differential Equations, Quantum Information, Quantum Computation and Quantum Simulation as covered by the section Analysis and Quantum, the Centre for the Mathematics of Quantum Theory  and the Quantum for Life Center.   You are welcome to contact any member of the department to discuss research projects.

   

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the field of Mathematics or nearby fields, whose background and research interests are a strong fit with the areas of mathematics above.

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members; around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics, and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors’ programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website http://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research  conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/.  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  You can find more information about the PhD program on the homepage http://www.math.ku.dk/english/programmes/ph.d/. 

   

  The PhD programme 

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree.

  ********************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. mathematics or closely related. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor’s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled in one of the faculty’s master’s programmes in Mathematics or Quantum Information Science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme  (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional experience, including publications (if any) 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics 	
• Good English skills    

  Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, publications (if any), language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s or Master’s and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Reference letters (if available; letters can be uploaded as part of the application or sent to hr-math@adm.ku.dk by the reference person).   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

   

  Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is 1 November 2026, 23:59 GMT+1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment (shortlisted) by a committee of unbiased experts. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  An assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

To apply, please send a short introduction together with examples of your work, portfolio, Instagram, or any relevant projects to lb@avoniprojects.com

Architect, build, and scale AI systems that hold up in production

Take ownership of how AI is architected, built, and scaled across our products. You will design the agentic systems at the core of our pension and advisory platforms, with a focus on reliable and responsible AI.

About the role

We are looking for a Senior AI Engineer to help lead our newly established AI team, working on our Life product for pension companies. The team is focused on the practical and responsible use of AI and is still in its early stages, so as a senior member you will play a defining role in setting the technical foundation, design patterns, and ways of working that the rest of the team builds on.

You will work closely with the AI Team Lead and Chief Architect, who own the overall architecture, helping shape the design within that direction. You will also be part of an agile team with a flat structure, where collaboration, curiosity, and continuous learning are central to the culture.

This role is primarily about designing and building agentic and LLM systems end to end, with a meaningful share of your time spent owning how we evaluate them and prove they hold up. It suits someone with 5+ years of relevant experience who wants to move beyond implementation into designing AI systems, and who enjoys raising the bar for the engineers around them.

Why this matters

This is core infrastructure, not edge tooling. Our Life product runs policy and capital administration for some of Europe’s largest pension providers, including PensionDanmark and APG, and is on track to support more than 8 million members and over €800bn in retirement assets.

The AI you design must meet that bar: fast and innovative, but also accurate, secure, and reliable enough for systems that people depend on for their financial security in retirement. Building it well and being able to prove it works, are two sides of the same job.

What you’ll do

As a senior member of the AI team, you will help shape how we build with Large Language Models and agentic systems across our products, contributing to high‑level design decisions, turning ambiguous business problems into robust system designs, and ensuring high‑quality coding standards and design. You will be hands‑on, with a real say in the architecture, standards, and technical judgement that guide the team.

In practice, you will:

Help shape the technical direction

• Contribute to the AI tech stack across our products: help define the high‑level system design, reference architectures, and design patterns the team builds on.

• Help shape AI strategy: identify where AI can create genuine value, frame the trade‑offs, and feed into a coherent, prioritised technical roadmap that fits our wider platform.

• Inform major architectural decisions: model and framework selection, build‑versus‑buy, and how AI components fit into our existing Java platform, integrate with surrounding systems, scale, and stay maintainable over time.

• Reason about trade‑offs in the open: weigh latency, cost, accuracy, security, and reliability, and explain and defend those choices to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Architect and build (hands‑on)

• Design LLM systems end to end: from retrieval, agent orchestration, and data pipelines through to deployment and monitoring.

• Design and build agentic systems: single‑ and multi‑agent, covering orchestration, tool use, action groups, knowledge‑base integrations, and patterns such as routing, delegation, parallelisation, and result aggregation for complex, reliable production workflows.

• Engineer RAG pipelines that connect agents to internal structured and unstructured data.

• Drive quality through design: prompt strategy, system prompts, and memory systems that produce hallucination‑resistant outputs with strong relevance and faithfulness.

• Make cost‑aware architectural choices: balancing latency, cost, and quality across model selection and orchestration patterns so what we ship is sustainable at scale.

• Set the standards for prompt strategy, RAG, orchestration, and cost management that the wider team adopts.

Evaluate and prove

• Build evaluation frameworks: eval sets, golden datasets, and LLM‑as‑judge pipelines, with offline regression suites wired into CI and online evaluation on production traces.

• Evaluate the whole agent, not just the answer: task success, trajectory and tool‑use correctness, and RAG faithfulness and grounding, so you know whether failures come from retrieval, reasoning, or generation.

• Measure what gates shipping: relevance, faithfulness, latency, cost, and reliability across repeated runs, turned into quality gates the team ships against.

Collaborate and grow the team

• Collaborate and mentor: work with the AI Team Lead, Chief Architect, senior developers, and product teams to translate business needs into working, well‑tested solutions, and support more junior engineers as the team grows.

What we’re looking for

You bring a strong technical foundation, hands‑on depth with modern AI tooling, and the judgement to design systems that hold up in the real world. You don’t need deep expertise in every area below, but we do expect real depth in agentic systems and AI architecture, backed by a solid grasp of how to evaluate what you build.

Required

• A master’s degree in computer science or a similar field, preferably with an AI focus.

• 5+ years building software, with significant hands‑on work applying Large Language Models.

• Strong proficiency in a statically typed, object‑oriented language, Java or C# (we build in Java). Python is welcome for demos, evaluation tooling, and experiments, but it is not our production language.

• Deep experience designing, building, and operating agent‑based systems, with hands‑on use of one or more orchestration frameworks (e.g. LangChain/LangGraph, Microsoft Agents, Claude Agent SDK, AutoGen, Semantic Kernel).

• A track record of designing and building AI systems, including how the components fit together, scale, and are maintained over time.

• Solid, practical experience with prompt strategy, Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), and the cost considerations of LLM usage and model selection.

• Working knowledge of LLM and agent evaluation: eval sets, LLM‑as‑judge, and the metrics that distinguish a good system from a confident‑but‑wrong one (faithfulness, relevance, task success, latency, and cost).

• Experience designing AI or backend systems that fit into a larger production platform, collaborating with senior engineers and architects to align on a shared technical direction.

• Strong communication skills to explain and defend architectural trade‑offs to both technical and non‑technical stakeholders.

Nice to have

• Experience building automated evaluation pipelines or CI gates for AI systems.

• Familiarity with observability and tracing tooling for LLM applications (e.g. LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix, Braintrust).

• Familiarity with LLM evaluation, automation, and red teaming.

• Broader machine learning experience.

• Hands‑on experience building and integrating MCP servers.

• Experience working in regulated or high‑reliability domains such as finance, insurance, or healthcare.

Who you are

You are a confident, hands‑on engineer who takes ownership of complex and sometimes undefined problems, and who is just as comfortable designing a system as proving it holds up. You think in systems, balance pragmatism with quality, and care about building things that work in production rather than just in a demo. You lift the people around you, stay open to feedback, and bring strong technical judgement of your own. You are curious, persistent, and result‑oriented.

jobs.occupation: Medical Head, Oncology – Denmark – Nordic Marketing Company

AstraZeneca Nordic is a recognized leader in its core therapy areas and aims to improve the lives of millions of people. This is an area where you are free to be more – you are encouraged to challenge traditional ways and test your curiosity. We drive innovative science, deliver key launches, build close collaboration and partnerships within health care.

You will guide a high-performing office- and field-based team, champion responsible AI adoption, and influence decisions across the enterprise while maintaining Medical independence. How will you translate insights from clinicians, payers and patients into an integrated medical plan that changes practice and accelerates impact?

Accountabilities:

Lead Medical Strategy: Own the country Integrated Medical Plan, connecting therapeutic priorities, patient needs and evidence gaps to measurable impact.

• 
Drive Evidence Generation: Shape the country evidence strategy, including real-world evidence, health data and investigator-sponsored research, in collaboration with Nordic, regional and global teams.

• 
Influence Cross-Functional Strategy: Bring medical expertise to Market Access, HTA and business planning while safeguarding Medical independence.

• 
Advance Organizational Excellence: Strengthen performance, operating models and ways of working to increase external impact and reduce internal complexity.

Develop Future-Ready Talent: Build a strong leadership pipeline through workforce planning, succession, coaching and inclusive development.

• 
Connect Nordic and Global Priorities: Contribute to Nordic strategy, share best practices across countries and ensure local needs shape broader decision-making.

• 
Manage Resources Strategically: Own medical budgets and deploy resources to priority activities, launches and patient-impact opportunities.

Build Strategic Partnerships: Develop trusted relationships with clinical experts, patient organizations, payers, HTA bodies and healthcare leaders to advance patient outcomes.

Essential Skills/Experience

Scientific Qualification: Advanced degree in Medicine, Pharmacy, Dentistry, Natural Sciences or a related field.

• 
Medical Affairs Leadership: Significant experience leading Medical Affairs strategy, operations and capabilities across therapeutic areas and product lifecycles.

• 
Launch and Portfolio Expertise: Proven success delivering pre-launch, launch and lifecycle activities for complex portfolios.

• 
Senior Leadership: Experience influencing across cross-functional, matrixed, regional and global environments.

• 
People Leadership: Track record of building high-performing teams through coaching, empowerment and accountability.

• 
Strategic and Business Acumen: Ability to connect medical strategy with brand, value and access priorities while maintaining scientific integrity.

• 
Evidence and Compliance Expertise: Strong understanding of evidence generation, data, responsible AI, regulatory requirements and HTA expectations.

• 
Communication and Influence: Exceptional communication, presentation and stakeholder-management skills; fluent in English and the local language.

• 
Agility and Execution: Strategic, analytical and adaptable, with the ability to prioritize, manage complexity and deliver results at pace.

• 
Industry Knowledge and Integrity: Strong understanding of the pharmaceutical industry, healthcare systems and payer environments, with high ethical standards.

Desirable Skills and Experience

• 
Global or Cross-Cultural Experience: Experience working in global organizations or leading international teams.

• 
Additional Qualification: Physician training, PhD or MBA.

• 
Organizational Leadership: Experience leading leaders and developing high-performing organizations.

• 
R&D Collaboration: Experience partnering with Clinical Research, Medical Development or R&D Strategy.

• 
Project Leadership: Strong experience delivering complex, cross-functional initiatives.

When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility. Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

I&D

We are proud to have a unique workplace culture that inspires innovation and collaboration! Here, employees are empowered to express diverse perspectives - and are made to feel valued, energized and rewarded for their ideas and creativity.

Why AstraZeneca

Here, science and strategy meet to change clinical practice. You will work shoulder to shoulder with unexpected teams in the same room unleashing bold thinking—from data scientists and regulatory experts to field-based medical leaders—to create evidence that directly informs how cancer is treated. We unite around a clear purpose, valuing kindness alongside ambition, and empower leaders to experiment, learn and move at pace. Your decisions will ripple from clinics to national systems, backed by real-world data capabilities, cutting-edge analytics and a culture that shares knowledge across roles and levels to turn a strong pipeline into meaningful outcomes for patients.

So, what is next

If you are ready to lead a country medical organization to generate practice-changing evidence, harness responsible AI and shape cancer care at scale, step forward and make your impact now!

jobs.description:
The opportunity

How could AI help a policy analyst assess a regulatory proposal for global shipping, a researcher make sense of a pile of reports, or a communications colleague turn an idea into a first draft? We’re looking for a curious student who enjoys figuring things out with people and wants to help colleagues use AI in their everyday work.

We’re setting up a new AI team to strengthen how the Center uses AI, and you’ll be one of its first members. You’ll help build the team’s work from the start.

Who we are

We’re the Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller Center for Zero Carbon Shipping, an independent, not-for-profit research and development center working to decarbonize global shipping. Our team unites experts from many fields – engineers, economists, analysts, software developers and more – who share a passion for making a real difference. We’re based in Copenhagen but collaborate globally.

Who you are

You’re enrolled in a higher education program. We’re open to different subjects and care less about your specific education than about your abilities. What we need is:

• An analytical, problem-solving mindset. You break unfamiliar problems down, ask good questions and work out what someone needs before jumping to a solution.

• Hands-on interest in AI. You already use AI in your studies, work or personal projects and enjoy finding new ways to use it.

• Good with people. You listen and explain things clearly in English, both in conversation and in writing.

• Drive to learn and follow through. You pick things up quickly, act on feedback and finish what you start.

You don’t need coding skills, maritime knowledge or previous professional AI experience.

What you’ll do

You’ll join our new AI team and work closely with the people building it. Specifically, you will:

• Find where AI helps: Talk with colleagues to understand their tasks and where AI might help.

• Test on real tasks: Try out tools and approaches on real work, checking whether the results are useful and reliable.

• Help colleagues get started: Support them through one-to-one conversations, drop-in sessions and short guides that you build and keep up to date.

• See work through: Take smaller tasks and projects through to completion and bring recurring problems back to the team.

You’ll learn alongside us and gradually take on more responsibility as your skills grow.

Why join us

You’ll be part of a new team from the start and help shape how it works. You’ll learn from experienced colleagues while helping them solve real problems. You’ll see how different teams work and build your own skills in AI and problem solving.

Practical details

Based in Copenhagen. 15 to 20 hours per week, with flexibility around studies and exams.

Apply

Send your CV and a short note explaining why this role interests you and what you would bring to it. We’re interested in how you approach unfamiliar problems, work with people and use AI. Examples from studies, personal projects or work are all welcome.

We interview candidates on a continuous basis and may close the recruitment process once the right candidate is found, so please apply as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: Senior Scientist, Downstream, Late-Stage Process Development
jobs.description:
Join a fast-paced process development team where scientific expertise, collaboration and practical problem-solving help advance projects. As Senior Scientist, you will lead downstream development activities for mammalian cell culture processes, supporting their progression through late-stage development.

You will work closely with clients, laboratory technicians and colleagues across upstream, downstream and analytical disciplines. The role combines scientific leadership, study design, data interpretation and technical writing. Most hands-on laboratory work will be performed by technicians; you will work closely with them to develop protocols, design experiments and guide execution, ensuring studies are scientifically sound and generate decision-quality data.

**A role with scientific ownership and real project impact

**As a Senior Scientist, you will have the opportunity to take ownership of downstream development activities and contribute directly to the progression of projects. You will combine your scientific expertise with practical problem-solving and collaborate with both internal colleagues and clients.

The role gives you exposure to different projects, technologies and challenges rather than focusing on one narrow area. You will be involved in shaping studies, interpreting data and turning scientific findings into clear recommendations that support project decisions.

Your work will also give you the opportunity to collaborate closely with laboratory technicians and scientists, allowing you to stay connected to the practical side of process development while taking a leading role in the scientific direction.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Lead and coordinate downstream development activities for assigned projects, working with clients and cross-functional teams to align on project needs and deliver outcomes.

• Plan and evaluate downstream processes, including chromatography using ÄKTA systems and filtration operations such as depth filtration, virus filtration and ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF).

• Design studies and author practical protocols in close collaboration with laboratory technicians; provide scientific guidance during experimental execution.

• Interpret study results, apply appropriate statistical approaches—including design of experiments (DoE) where relevant—and communicate findings through clear presentations and reports.

• Contribute to process characterization, including failure mode and risk assessments such as FMEA, and author process characterization (PC) work reports.

• Support investigations and deviation handling by assessing technical causes, interpreting relevant data, and documenting conclusions and follow-up actions.

• Provide scientific and technical input to business activities and support the generation of information for regulatory submissions.

**Required Qualifications And Experience

**

• Education: Master’s or PhD in Biochemistry, Biochemical or Chemical Engineering, Process Technology, or a related discipline.

• Industrial experience: 5+ years with a Master’s degree, or 2+ years with a PhD.

• Downstream development: Demonstrated experience with mammalian cell culture processes.

• Unit operations: Chromatography and filtration; ideally ÄKTA systems and TFF systems.

• Study execution and data: Ability to plan, analyze and report complex development studies, including statistical analysis.

• Project work: Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities with scientific rigour and attention to detail.

• Communication: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to explain technical findings clearly to clients and colleagues.

• Language: Fluent written and spoken English.

**Preferred Qualifications And Experience

**

• Process Characterization and FMEA

• Viral clearance studies or activities.

• Commercial manufacturing requirements and biologics regulatory frameworks, including relevant ICH guidelines and BLA submission requirements.

• Knowledge of Design of Experiments (DoE), including experimental design, data analysis, and evaluation using SAS JMP

• Liquid-handling automation, such as Tecan systems.

**What Will Help You Succeed

**You take ownership, bring a practical can-do attitude and are comfortable working at pace. You collaborate closely with technicians and colleagues, communicate openly, and use data and sound scientific judgement to find a way forward as project needs and priorities evolve.

**What You Can Expect From Us

**We want you to have the opportunity to use your scientific expertise while continuing to develop professionally. In this role, you can expect:

• Scientific ownership: Take responsibility for development activities and influence how studies are designed and executed.

• Variety: Work across different projects, technologies and scientific challenges rather than doing the same thing every day.

• Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with scientists, technicians, upstream and analytical colleagues as well as clients.

• Client exposure: Develop your ability to communicate scientific findings and recommendations directly with clients and contribute to project discussions.

• Professional development: Continue developing your expertise in downstream processing, process characterization, data analysis and late-stage development.

• Impact: See how your scientific work contributes to advancing biopharmaceutical processes towards later-stage development and manufacturing.

**A team where science and collaboration go hand in hand

**You will become part of a team where scientific knowledge, practical experience and collaboration are important to how we work. We value people who share knowledge, ask questions and are willing to challenge and support each other.

You will work closely with experienced colleagues across different disciplines, giving you the opportunity to learn from others while also bringing your own expertise to the team.

We believe that good science is strengthened by open communication, different perspectives and a willingness to find solutions together.

**Ready to make your next move?

**If you are looking for a role where you can combine scientific expertise, project ownership, client interaction and practical problem-solving, we would like to hear from you.

Apply through the AGC Biologics career site by **31 October 2026.

Applications will be reviewed on a continuous basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We may close the position before the application deadline once the right candidate has been identified.

To support an objective recruitment process, please do not include a photo in your application or CV.

From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Complex transactions, new products and changing business needs often raise accounting questions without a standard answer.

As Senior Financial Controller, you’ll combine hands-on financial controlling and Group reporting with IFRS and technical accounting expertise. You’ll assess those questions, establish the accounting treatment and translate your conclusions into clear, practical reporting solutions across the Group.

This is a role for someone who enjoys being close to the numbers while taking ownership of the accounting questions behind them. You’ll have room to apply your expertise across reporting processes, accounting governance and IFRS as the business develops.

DIVE INTO WHAT YOUR DAY-TO-DAY TASKS WILL BE

Your work combines recurring financial controlling and Group reporting with accounting assessments that require deeper analysis.

Your mission is to:

• Support month-end and year-end closing, Group reporting, accounting analyses and quality assurance of financial data

• Provide IFRS and technical accounting expertise on complex accounting matters and contribute to accounting policies, reporting guidance and documentation across the Group

• Analyse new products, contracts, energy trading activities and strategic initiatives to determine their accounting and reporting implications

• Strengthen Group reporting processes, controls and documentation to support consistent and reliable financial reporting

• Work across Financial Controlling, Accounting, Risk, Treasury, Tax, Legal, Trading and Business Development, bringing financial reporting expertise into complex business and accounting decisions

JOIN A TEAM OF MINDFUL ACHIEVERS

You’ll join our Financial Controlling team, where collaboration, learning, high-quality reporting and strong processes are part of everyday work. Curiosity and practical thinking shape how the team approaches financial questions and grows.

Knowledge is shared openly, and colleagues challenge ideas constructively to improve controlling, reporting and compliance. You’ll have room to contribute your expertise from day one while continuing to develop professionally.

This position is based at our Aarhus office, with flexibility to work from home when it fits the work and the team. Expect around 5–10 days of travel each year.

LET'S SWITCH THE FOCUS TO YOU

You enjoy working close to the numbers and digging deeper when an accounting question requires it. You approach complex questions with curiosity and structure, connecting the details to the broader reporting picture and turning your conclusions into something others can use.

We imagine you bring:

• 5+ years of experience in financial controlling, Group reporting, audit, technical accounting or a similar finance position.

• A master’s degree in accounting, auditing, finance or a related field.

• Solid knowledge of IFRS and financial reporting, with an interest in developing further expertise within technical accounting.

• Experience from a Big 4 firm, an international finance function, Group Finance or a similar controlling and accounting environment.

• The ability to communicate complex accounting and reporting matters clearly to finance and non-finance stakeholders.

• Fluency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

You don’t need to tick every box. What matters most is a solid controlling and financial reporting foundation, combined with the curiosity to dig into complex accounting questions.

WE MIGHT BE BIASED, BUT IT IS QUITE AWESOME HERE

People here care about doing things well and creating a place people genuinely enjoy being part of. We like to hack the everyday, from breakfast and lunch made in-house with organic ingredients to in-house massage, something in the freezer when the day runs late and the occasional “Just Because” surprise. You also get five Switch Days, equal to a seventh holiday week, giving you extra flexibility and room to recharge throughout the year.

Through Mind Club, people come together around everything from padel and Football Shirt Fridays to clay pigeon shooting and Christmas afternoons with your family and Santa. And with Mind Academy, you grow alongside sharp and curious colleagues who challenge ideas, share knowledge and help each other level up. These are just some of the things that make us special. It’s easier to experience in person.

We’re mindful achievers. It shapes how we work, think and grow together, while recognising that well-being, care and integrity matter just as much as the results we create. This is a place to focus, grow and achieve more.

LET US GET THIS CONVERSATION STARTED

Upload your CV and tell us a bit about how you approach financial controlling, reporting quality and complex accounting questions in practice.

We’re particularly interested in hearing about:

• A complex accounting or reporting issue you’ve worked with. How did you analyse it, involve relevant stakeholders and translate your conclusion into a practical solution?

• A reporting process or control you’ve improved. What did you change, and what was the result?

Where confidentiality permits, you’re welcome to include an anonymised accounting assessment or reporting example, as well as your university transcript if available.

Application deadline is November 6, 2026.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the process early if we find the right match.

If you have any questions about the role, you're welcome to contact Anton Byg Olesen, Head of Financial Controlling, at anbl@mindenergy.com

For general recruitment matters, contact people@mindenergy.com

Delivering software excellence and pushing the limits of technology to make some of the world’s best hearing aids is what we do in Demant.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer with broad competencies who wants to develop and strengthen our Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL).

You will be deep down the software stack in a crucial and complex part of our software eco system.

Development, defect support and platform improvements

Our HAL platform connects to hearing aids, apps, fitting software and sophisticated internal tools. Seamless Bluetooth solutions and connectivity are crucial for the end-users to have great experience with our hearing aids.

We embrace agile software development and use Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) and releases the HAL platform 2-4 times per year. The backlog of features and enablers are executed by priority.

The features are platform support of audiological or end user features. The enablers are typically platform improvements for the future and general internal improvements that can be either specific or of an exploratory nature.

What you will do

Your job can be divided into these three main areas:

• 
Most of your daily life is analyzing, designing, coding, testing and integrating our platform, always done with a broad mindset. Analyzing logs and unraveling mysteries is a key activity in the role and team.

• 
With an ever-changing Bluetooth environment and incoming defects there will be adjustments, which you must react fast to as part of the team. You will also act as problem solver for other teams consuming HAL.

• 
Lastly, you will be part of simplifying HAL to make the solutions more effective, maintainable and secure. In collaboration with the team, you will identify improvements and come up with suggestions for how these should be implemented.

We need everybody in the team to be on top of technology to keep on improving and providing best-in-class solutions. To support this, we have a monthly learning day for the team to acquire relevant knowledge either individually or on a team base.

We invest in and take advantage of AI, that is part of our development environment and tooling.

Teamwork, teamwork, teamwork

Part of your team consists of six Software Developers, two Test Developers, a Product Owner and a Scrum Master. They are all very experienced and enthusiastic about their jobs.

We encourage and strive for T-shaping, meaning that it is healthy that we share the responsibilities and grow mutual skills between developers and test developers.

Scrum is used as the basic way of working and encourages collaboration, sparring and sharing of thoughts and enables the best possible solutions.

It is important that you can collaborate with others and see the gain of it, rather than just working on your own. We hope that you, with your energy and enthusiasm, will contribute and encourage cooperation.

Your manager is a “servant leader” and will support your needs and development in our trust-based culture.

We believe in the good life

In Demant we trust and value professionalism, experience, and commitment. We recognize that to bring energy and inspiration to work, you need to re-energize and spend time with family, friends, and hobbies in a healthy work life balance.

To ensure the good life we offer good breakfast and lunch in our canteen, free fitness room including weekly spinning and yoga sessions, massage offer, no child’s first sick day meaning you can stay home with your child as long as the child is not feeling well and the possibility to work from home up to two days per week. Just to mention some of the things.

Your profile

• To candidate for this job, you need to be Senior Software Developer with minimum 8 years of experience. You have experience with hardware abstraction layers either as a provider or consumer.

**

Senior Manager, Group Development & Strategy

Help shape Coloplast’s growth agenda by sourcing, evaluating and executing strategic transactions across our global business.

The opportunity

We are looking for a Senior Manager to join Group Development & Strategy at our headquarters in Humlebæk. The role will have a primary focus on M&A while also contributing to selected enterprise strategy projects. You will help develop Coloplast’s M&A agenda, build and maintain a strong pipeline of opportunities across our business segments, support the M&A Director on key priorities and independently lead selected projects.

The transaction scope spans acquisitions, divestments, minority equity investments and strategic partnerships, as well as integration planning. This is a hands-on role with significant exposure to senior leaders, business segments, global functions and external advisers.

Welcome to Group Development & Strategy

You will join a team of five high-performing specialists across strategy, business development and M&A. Together, we work across group strategy, strategic projects, transactions and post-merger integration, collaborating closely with Executive Leadership and teams across the organisation. You will become part of a distinctive performance culture focused on working together to achieve the best results.

Your key responsibilities includes

•    Support the development of the enterprise M&A strategy and strategic priorities across our business units

•    Source opportunities and maintain the pipeline across acquisitions, divestments, equity investments and partnerships

•    Assess potential targets, including strategic fit, value and key risks, in collaboration with internal stakeholders

•    Support the M&A Director on key transactions and independently lead selected processes

•    Prepare financial models, valuations and business cases

•    Coordinate due diligence across relevant functions

•    Manage relationships with targets, owners and external advisers

•    Support integration planning and the handover to the business

•    Prepare proposals and recommendations for senior management and other internal stakeholders

•    Monitor market, competitor and transaction trends relevant to Coloplast

•    Support on selected enterprise strategy and integration projects

What we expect from you:

•    A relevant commercial master’s degree or MBA

•    5–6 years of experience within M&A and ideally with strategic projects

•    Experience from top-tier consulting, investment banking and/or private equity

•    Strong financial and business modelling skills and hands-on M&A execution capabilities

•    Experience across all phases of a transaction

•    Experience managing multiple high-priority projects simultaneously

•    Fluent written and spoken English

•    Experience working in an international environment

•    Experience from healthcare or medical devices industry is an advantage, but not a requirement

How you work

You are intellectually curious and comfortable moving between the big picture and detailed analysis. You create momentum in ambiguous situations, challenge constructively and know when to involve others. You build trust across functions and geographies, remain composed under pressure and balance analytical thoroughness with the pace required in live transactions.

Role details

Location: Humlebæk, Denmark

Team: Group Development & Strategy

Reports to: Group Development & Strategy Director

Travel: Some international travel should be expected, particularly during active transactions.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. Working closely with the Head of HR and key stakeholders, you will play an important role in shaping a modern, efficient, and globally connected function.

Trackman has grown into a global organisation through innovation, strong products and talented people. As we continue to scale, we are investing in the infrastructure, systems and ways of working needed to support our next phase of growth.

Imagine working with cutting-edge machine learning models, crunching high frequency data sets and sparring with exceptional and fun colleagues, all while taking part in scaling our business even further.

Does this sound highly appealing to you? Then you might be our new Machine Learning Researcher at Alipes.

At Alipes, we have been the market leader in automating the financial markets since we started back in 2008, shaping a fully automatic natural language processing system for reading and interpreting financial news.

To accomplish our mission of being the best at what we do, we understand the importance of elevating our predictive modeling standards to the highest levels. Your work will involve leading the efforts in creating a world class modeling workflow, enabling the team to seamlessly turn massive data sets of financial information into mathematical models that accurately predict movements in the financial markets.

In doing so, you will get a chance to tackle a variety of software infrastructure challenges, such as:

• Development and optimization of calibration and benchmarking frameworks

• Building out and implementing best practices for data preparation and dataset generation pipelines

• Prototyping and releasing novel predictive architectures, especially with respect to time-series models.

You will get instant validation of your work and experience short feedback cycles, where going from inception to deployment can be a matter of hours. There will be no red tape to cut and no sales people to consult.

About the team

All of this will happen in an informal atmosphere where technical discussions are valued, and you are encouraged to take ownership of, and pride in, your work. You will impact the direction of the team, prioritize your work and choose the tools that get the job done. We are a tight-knit modeling team with fourteen passionate quantitative researchers covering 6 nationalities – eleven PhD’s and three MSc’s with expertise in statistical analysis, mathematical modeling and machine learning. We enjoy collaboration and are always willing to lend a helping hand. We are working alongside two other teams of software developers and traders that implement and conceive the mathematical models together with us. What makes this constellation work great is that all of the individual team members write code and understand that a seemingly trivial change can actually require a lot of work, and vice versa.

About you

• Fluency within mathematics and statistics.

• Experience working with the full Machine Learning stack from data generation through model calibration and real-life validation and monitoring.

• Programming experience with Python, in particular data-wrangling and numerical programming.

• Proficiency with computer science fundamentals.

• A scientific and inquisitive mind.

Nice to have

• Experience working with ‘out-of-core’ datasets.

• Experience working with tools like PyTorch, Tensorflow, XGBoost and/or Catboost.

• Programming experience with languages like C# and C/C++.

• PhD or MSc degree in engineering, physics, computer science, mathematics or economics.

What we can offer you

• Competitive benefits, including pension, health insurance, and 30 days of vacation.

• A modern, harbour front office in Copenhagen (Nordhavn) with a flexible hybrid work model.

• A flat hierarchy with high levels of trust, autonomy, and freedom to make decisions.

• A valued role with unique responsibilities and plenty of room for creativity.

• Fast feedback and recognition of your contributions in a high-growth company.

• Strong team spirit - successes are celebrated with company events and trips.

Practicalities

To apply, please send us your CV and, in lieu of providing a cover letter, concisely answer the questions on the application. If your profile looks like a good match, we will get in touch to coordinate an online technical test as a first step in the interview process.

Should you have questions about the role that you would like clarified before applying, you're welcome to send an email to quant_jobs@alipescapital.com. Please note that applications should not be sent to the email address but rather via the job link.

A Snapshot of Your Day

Join Siemens Energy as a Technical Project Manager and lead the technical execution of a large-scale high-voltage substation project: a 400 kV AC substation with GIS (Gas Insulated Switchgear), Control & Protection systems, SCADA, telecommunications and auxiliary systems, which will connect future offshore wind. As the technical authority in the project organization, you report to the overall project manager and coordinate all technical disciplines on the Danish part of this flagship infrastructure project in Denmark, which runs until 2034. From design through installation and commissioning, you represent the technical side in meetings with the customer and a large international project organization, making a significant impact on the future of power transmission and the energy transition.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Leading the technical execution of a complex high-voltage substation project from design through installation and commissioning

• Coordinating a multidisciplinary team of 7-10 discipline leads, scope managers and engineering specialists, and ensuring each discipline delivers its commitments on time and to the required quality

• Driving technical planning and engineering schedules with a clear work breakdown, critical path and intermediate milestones, aligning interfaces and dependencies between work packages and monitoring progress against schedules and budgets

• Acting as the primary escalation point for technical challenges, managing technical risks and mitigation plans, and presenting technical solutions to the customer side by side with the overall project manager

• Participating in customer meetings and technical workshops, and collaborating closely with project management, site management, procurement, construction and commissioning teams

• Ensuring compliance with standards, regulations, employer requirements and contractual technical obligations, leading requirement management and traceability, and supporting design reviews

What You Bring

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline

• Minimum 5 years of experience leading technical teams and coordinating engineering disciplines within power transmission, substations or large infrastructure projects, for example as a technical project manager or senior technical lead

• Strong understanding of high-voltage substations, especially GIS and Control and Protection systems, as well as AIS, SCADA, communication and auxiliary systems

• Strong knowledge of engineering standards, specifications and requirement management, and experience working directly with customers, contractors and external stakeholders

• A structured, proactive and results-oriented leader who is confident in large customer-facing meetings and technical negotiations, and builds strong relationships across disciplines and organizations

• Fluent English, Danish is considered an advantage

About the Team

This position is part of our Substation engineering department in Denmark, which consists of four engineering teams and a number of specialists reporting directly to the Head of Engineering. In the project, the Technical Project Manager is supported by work package managers and experts within each technical discipline.

Our Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.

Who is Siemens Energy?

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Learning-Based Multi-Agent Control under Uncertainty
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at the Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a postdoc in learning-based multi-agent control under uncertainty, with applications to autonomous multi-robot systems operating in dynamic and uncertain environments, as per February 1, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is available for a period of 2 years.

Your work tasks   The position focuses on fundamental research in learning-based planning and control of interacting autonomous agents under uncertainty. You will develop new theoretical and algorithmic approaches for distributed and cooperative control, combining learning or online adaptation with principled treatment of safety, robustness, and performance. Research challenges include uncertain dynamics and disturbances, partial or noisy information, changing interactions between agents, and limited or unreliable communication.

A central part of the work will be to formulate rigorous methods and establish their properties, for example concerning stability, safety, constraint satisfaction, robustness, and convergence, where applicable. Depending on the research direction, the work may draw on learning-augmented model predictive control, safe reinforcement learning, data-driven modelling and safety mechanism (e.g. CBF), distributed optimization, or robust and adaptive control. You will develop reproducible numerical studies and simulations to examine the strengths, limitations, and scalability of the proposed methods.

The research will be carried out in the Horizon Europe ROX-6G project, where heterogeneous robot teams provide a compelling application for coordination under uncertain conditions and connectivity constraints. Although the position is primarily theoretical, you will collaborate with colleagues working on robotic implementation and will contribute to experimental validation. You will lead and co-author publications in international journals and conferences, engage with project partners, contribute to research planning and scientific discussions, and support knowledge exchange within the team.

Your competencies

We seek a researcher with a PhD in control engineering, robotics, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, or a closely related field, and a strong background in mathematical modelling, control, optimization, or multi-agent systems.

You should be able to formulate original research problems, develop and analyse rigorous methods, and demonstrate research quality through peer-reviewed scientific publications. Experience in learning-based control, robust or nonlinear control, distributed control, or decision-making under uncertainty is particularly relevant; expertise in every one of these areas is not expected.

You should have good scientific programming skills, for example in Python, MATLAB, or C++, and be able to evaluate algorithms systematically through simulation. We value independent research initiative, clear scientific writing, and the ability to work constructively with researchers from different disciplines and backgrounds. Experience with autonomous robots, ROS/ROS 2, multi-robot simulation, or physical robotic experiments will be considered an advantage, but is not a prerequisite for this primarily theory-oriented position. Excellent written and spoken English is required.

Who we are

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

The position is hosted in the Automation and Control Section, within a collaborative robotics research environment combining fundamental research with real-world applications.

In addition, you will work with an international team and research partners in ROX-6G, a European collaboration addressing autonomous robotic operations in demanding underground environments. Our research interests span safe and resilient decision-making, learning-enabled control, distributed multi-robot coordination, and validation in simulation and on robotic platforms. We encourage scientific independence, close exchange of ideas, and publication of high-quality research. More information: www.es.aau.dk.

Qualification requirements Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications if relevant.

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Postdoc”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

Enduro Sense is used for cell-based expression systems and production strains to deliver higher titer, rate and yields, making biomanufacturing more efficient and scalable.

jobs.occupation: Better Nitrogen efficiency by improving Cow Resilience, Eating Dynamics, Breeding and Lifetime Efficiency
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Quantitative Genetics and Genomics programme. The position is available from 1 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Better Nitrogen efficiency by improving Cow Resilience, Eating Dynamics, Breeding and Lifetime Efficiency

Research area and project description
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) holds a leading position in cattle breeding research, particularly in genetic studies on data generated by advanced phenotyping technologies such as the CFIT 3D camera system through industry collaboration with VikingGenetics. This state-of-the-art system enables large-scale, non-invasive measurement of feed intake, body weight, and milk production data in over 30,000 cows directly in their production environment. This PhD project will leverage this extensive phenotypic dataset generated by CFIT, in combination with feeding parameters and other phenotypes from the Danish Cattle Database, to develop genetic tools aimed at enhancing nitrogen efficiency, resilience, eating dynamics and feed efficiency. The goal is to develop novel genomic breeding values for nitrogen efficiency, while considering other important breeding goal traits (e.g., productivity, health, fertility) and other traits, such as resilience, eating dynamics and feed efficiency. The project will apply advanced statistical methods, artificial intelligence, and cutting-edge genetic models to support and enhance management and breeding decision-making by dairy farmers. This project offers a unique opportunity to contribute to the green transition in agriculture by breeding cows that are both more sustainable and economically viable for the future of Danish dairy farming. We encourage candidates finishing their MSc in summer 2027 also to apply.

Qualifications and specific competences
A relevant master’s degree (120 ECTS) in Animal Breeding
Experience with data handling softwares (e.g., R, SAS, Python, Unix Shell) and genetic softwares (e.g., DMU, BLUPF90, AIREML).
Background in working with Livestock data is an advantage.
Can speak and write English fluently is a prerequisite.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C., Denmark.

Contacts
Applicants seeking further information regarding the PhD position are invited to contact:
• Associate Professor Bingjie Li, e-mail: bingjie.li@qgg.au.dk (main supervisor)
• Tenure Track Assistant Professor Rasmus Bak Stephansen, e-mail: rasmus.stephansen@qgg.au.dk (co-supervisor)For information about application requirements and mandatory attachments, please see our application guide. If answers cannot be found there, please contact:
• admission.gradschool.tech@au.dk 
How to apply
Please follow this link to submit your application.

Application deadline is 29 November 2026 23:59 CET.

Preferred starting date is 01 March 2027.

For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Please note:
• Only documents received prior to the application deadline will be evaluated. Thus, documents sent after deadline will not be considered.
• The programme committee may request further information or invite the applicant to attend an interview.
• Shortlisting will be used, which means that the evaluation committee only will evaluate the most relevant applications.
Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions. You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. As a PhD fellow you will also receive a monthly non-pensionable allowance.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via the online recruitment system, which can be accessed under ‘How to apply’.

jobs.occupation: Two 3-year Postdoc positions in Leadership Studies
jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for two vacant 3-year Postdoc positions in Leadership Studies, both based on a broad understanding of leadership as studies of both governance, organising and management. One Postdoc position will be affiliated with Department of Management, Society and Communication and the other with Department of Organisation. For more information about the two departments, please follow the links.

The two positions form part of CBS Executive Education’s Talent Programme (ETP). The ETP sets out to strengthen CBS’ leadership related research and education capacity within executive education and life-long learning. Expected starting date is 15 February 2027.

Examples of research areas that the Postdocs might cover:

• Leadership Studies with a particular focus on leadership practices and developments in the Nordic context
• Leadership Studies with a particular focus on life-long learning for working professions
The Postdoc positions are non-tenured positions, each for a three-year period with both research and teaching obligations.

To fulfill the research requirements of the positions, the applicants chosen are expected to be physically present on a regular basis and actively participate in the teaching and research activities of their respective Departments.

Qualifications

Applicants must hold a PhD or the equivalent. In assessing applications, particular emphasis will be placed on

• Research potential within different aspects of leadership studies in a Nordic context and within life-long learning for working professionals.
• Demonstrable experience with executive education and external engagement based on direct participation in executive education activities, including development and teaching of high-quality offerings in the executive education area.
• Demonstrable interest in developing and co-creating new educational formats that address changing learning and competence needs of relevance for life-long learning, in part by further developing CBS Executive Education’s collaboration with external partners and the CBS Executive Education Foundation.
• Professional proficiency in both Danish and English (written and spoken).
Copenhagen Business School has a broad commitment to the excellence, distinctiveness and relevance of its teaching and research programmes. Candidates who wish to join us should demonstrate enthusiasm for working in an organisation of this type.

The application must include:

• A summary of the candidate’s key abilities and qualifications.
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Information indicating experience in research management, teaching incl executive education, industry co-operation and international co-operation.
• Documentation of relevant, significant, original research at an international level.
• Transcript(s) and a full CV
Recruitment procedure

The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants; when possible five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. 

The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment.

Once the recruitment process has been completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

For further information please contact: Head of Department MSC Dorte Salskov-Iversen tel.: +45 3815 3181, e-mail dsi.msc@cbs.dk.

For information on the recruitment process, please contact: jobcall.msc@cbs.dk

Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Finance’s agreement with the Central Academic Organisation.

Application: Application must be sent via the electronic recruitment system.

Application deadline: 19 November 2026

Copenhagen Business School must receive all application material, including all appendices (see items above), by the application deadline.

WE TRANSFORM SOCIETY WITH BUSINESS

CBS is a globally recognised business school with deep roots in the Nordic socio-economic model. Our faculty has a broad focus on societal challenges, and we have earned a reputation for high-quality disciplinary and interdisciplinary research and education.
We are located at Frederiksberg and have approximately 20,000 full and part-time students, 800 full-time faculty members, 200 PhD students and 700 administrative staff, and a full portfolio of bachelor, master, MBA/EMBA, PhD and executive programmes taught in English and Danish.
Our global profile carries the obligation to address critical challenges in our research and to develop the transformational capabilities of students, graduates and business leaders via our educational activities and opportunities for lifelong learning. Complex challenges call for joint action, and therefore our strategy focuses on strengthening current and starting new partnerships with other sciences, the business community, authorities and civil society.
