jobs.occupation: 171626 Associate professor in Clinical Proteomics and Data-Driven Biomarker Discovery for Neurodegenerative Disease (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

   

  The University seeks to appoint an time limited associate professor at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology to commence March 1st 2025 or as soon as possible thereafter

  Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology is committed to advancing human health through discovery, design, and evaluation of safe and effective medical treatments. To achieve this, we work in a dynamic and committed academic community, that bridges health science and life science in a translational and innovative approach from molecule to patient. We value interdisciplinary research and education, development of individual competences, and finding solutions to todays and tomorrows challenges in society. The department furthermore prioritizes sustainability in all aspects of research and education.

  The department is organized in six research sections and furthermore houses Center for Pharmaceutical Data Science Education and Center for Protein Design. Further information on the Department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk/

  Job description 

  We seek an established researcher to lead an independent research programme at the interface of clinical proteomics, molecular neuropathology, and translational neuroscience. The successful candidate will drive biofluid biomarker discovery and drug-target identification in Huntington’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders, contributing to the department’s data-driven target and drug discovery activities and to its concerted effort to integrate data science and AI into research and teaching. Using state-of-the-art mass spectrometry-based proteomics, multi-omics, and machine learning, the candidate will connect mechanistic insight to clinical application through disease-relevant models and human sample cohorts, supporting AI-powered translational prediction and clinical decision support for personalized treatment.

  Responsibilities

  The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination of results to the scientific community and attraction of external funding 	
• Develop, organize, and conduct research-based teaching, including associated examination. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of students and researchers 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments 	
• Engage in outreach and/or innovation activities both within the Department and towards academia, the clinic, and industry in general.   Qualifications of the applicant

  When evaluating applicants, primary emphasis will be placed on the applicant's ability to document original scientific work of the highest international standard, an innovative mindset, and strong ambitions for advancing teaching within the fields of biochemistry and pharmacology, with particular focus on teaching on compulsory courses at the BSc and MSc levels.

  Applicants already having sustainability integrated in all aspects of their research and teaching, or a clear plan for doing so, will have preference. Likewise, a clear and structured plan for internal and external collaborations will be given positive consideration.

  Overall criteria for the position: 

  To be qualified for an associate professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as an assistant professor/postdoc, but may also be obtained in other ways 	
• Teaching qualifications and pedagogical competencies 	
• Research-based teaching   The associate professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Desired qualifications: 

   	
• Strong, independent research record in neurodegenerative disease, with expertise in mass spectrometry-based proteomics and biofluid biomarker discovery. 	
• Experience integrating multi-omics data with machine learning and AI, and working with preclinical models and cell-type-resolved approaches. 	
• A track record of securing competitive external funding and of research leadership. 	
• Teaching experience and formal teaching qualifications (e.g. Universitetspædagogikum), together with supervision experience. 	
• Ability to bridge discovery and translation (from molecule to patient) and to collaborate across academia, clinic, and industry, including innovation and spin-out activity   Terms of employment
 The position is a time limited position for 5 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). 

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.
 
 Questions
 For further information, please contact Head of Department Dan Stærk, ds@sund.ku.dk. For information about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology and the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND), please see www.drug.ku.dk and https://sund.ku.dk/.

  
 Foreign applicants may find this link useful: https://www.ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility).
 
 Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application, including motivations for applying for the position (maximum 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including information about external funding 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD, and other relevant certificates) 	
• A complete list of publications 	
• Research plan (3-5 pages) 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 (associate professors) publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/job-application-portfolio)   Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at The university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. The closing date for applications is 23.59 CET on 20 November 2026.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) engineering: internalization and lysosomal delivery
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC) / Finsen Laboratory, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

  A 3-year PhD fellowship is available in the research group of Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm. Expected start: 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

   

  The project

  Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) depend on efficient internalization and lysosomal processing to release their cytotoxic payload. Inefficient trafficking limits potency and restricts current ADCs to targets with very high receptor density. The PhD project will engineer and test next-generation ADCs with improved internalization and lysosomal routing. This includes bispecific constructs that combine our established ADC targets (uPAR, MMP14, uPARAP and the Mannose Receptor) with receptors that drive lysosomal delivery, such as IGF2R. Lead candidates will be evaluated in cancer cell models and in vivo, including models of sarcoma and glioblastoma.

  The project is part of the Novo Nordisk Foundation Distinguished Innovator project "Breaking Barriers: Engineering ADCs for Efficient BBB Transport and Lysosomal Targeting", in collaboration with Professor Matthias Herth (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, UCPH) and Professor Katrine Qvortrup (Department of Chemistry, DTU).

   

  Main tasks

   	
•  	Production, purification and validation of recombinant and bispecific antibodies

 	 	
•  	Conjugation of antibodies to cytotoxic payloads and characterization of the resulting ADCs

 	 	
•  	Cell-based assays: antibody uptake and internalization, flow cytometry, drug screening and cytotoxicity/cell viability assays

 	 	
•  	In vivo efficacy studies of ADC candidates in tumor models

 	 	
•  	Writing scientific publications and presenting at international conferences

 	    

   

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
•  	Carrying through an independent research project under supervision. 

 	 	
•  	Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points.

 	 	
•  	Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team.

 	 	
•  	Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project

 	 	
•  	Teaching and disseminating your knowledge.

 	 	
•  	Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project

 	    

  PhD Programme Description:
 The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., [relevant degrees]).

   

  Qualifications

  We are looking for a candidate with a strong, hands-on background in ADC research. Applicants must have:

   	
•  	An MSc degree (120 ECTS, or equivalent) in pharmaceutical biotechnology, biotechnology or a closely related field, with an excellent academic record

 	 	
•  	An MSc thesis or equivalent research project on antibody-drug conjugates or antibody-based cancer therapeutics

 	 	
•  	Documented hands-on experience with production, validation and payload conjugation of recombinant antibodies

 	 	
•  	Experience with cytotoxicity, cell viability and drug screening assays in mammalian cancer cell lines

 	 	
•  	Experience with flow cytometry

 	 	
•  	Experience with laboratory animal work

 	 	
•  	Experience from an international research laboratory and excellent written and spoken English

 	   Experience with functional genomics (e.g. CRISPR-Cas9 screening) and with sarcoma models is an advantage.

     Place of employment

  The place of employment is BRIC, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. 

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is 15 January 2027 or after agreement.

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2013) and the Faculty’s rules on achieving the degree. 

  Salary, pension and terms of employment are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,800 DKK/Roughly 4,200 EUR (August 2026 level) plus pension.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

   

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm, lhe@finsenlab.dk.

  General information about PhD studies at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences is available at the Graduate School’s website: https://healthsciences.ku.dk/phd/guidelines/

   

  Application procedure
 Your application must be submitted electronically by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. The application must include the following documents in PDF format: 

  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page)

  2. CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

  3. Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufm.dk/en/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science

  4. Publication list (if possible)

   

  Application deadline: 6 November 2026, 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor.

  The assessor makes a non-prioritized assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement.

  Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You find information about the recruitment process at: http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicants will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  Interviews are expected to be held in week 49

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

**

CANNORDIC is looking for a self-driven sales professional to accelerate our international growth. We are a MedTech scale-up with a proven track record of more than one million units sold since launch.

Application:

About CANNORDIC:

CANNORDIC A/S is a Danish MedTech company developing, manufacturing and commercialising over-the-counter products under pharmaceutical legislation. We combine science, nature and cannabinoid technology to create innovative products with a focus on efficacy and bioavailability.

Our portfolio comprises 21 cannabidiol-based products, including 11 patent-pending products. Learn more about CANNORDIC and the CANNASEN® brand at www.cannordic.com.

As our new Laboratory Technician, you will become part of our Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory, where we support products and processes throughout their lifecycle. You will work with ongoing production, helping ensure that our products meet the required quality standards.

If you are motivated by laboratory work, quality assurance, data evaluation, and close collaboration with colleagues across different functions, we offer you an interesting permanent position in a laboratory with a broad range of tasks and stakeholders.

“This is an opportunity to work with quality assurance at different stages of a product’s lifecycle. Your laboratory work and attention to detail will contribute directly to ensuring high-quality products for people with intimate healthcare needs,” says Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory.

Join a skilled and collaborative laboratory team

At our Coloplast Mørdrup site, you will join the Quality Assurance Lifecycle Laboratory. The team consists of 10 laboratory technicians and 2 test method specialists who work closely together to support ongoing production, process development, quality investigations, and test method activities.

You will become part of an engaged and supportive team with a strong team spirit and a valuable mix of practical laboratory experience and specialist knowledge. We place great emphasis on engagement, collaboration, and creating a working environment where people feel included, support one another, and share knowledge across tasks and responsibilities. In our daily work, we collaborate closely with colleagues across Quality Assurance, Research and Development, and Operations, and we value curiosity, flexibility, and a continuous improvement mindset.

**Laboratory work across the product lifecycle

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• 
Planning and performing laboratory tests according to approved procedures, instructions, and test methods

• 
Documenting test activities and results accurately and in accordance with quality requirements

• 
Reviewing and evaluating test results, including basic statistical analysis and interpretation of data

• 
Supporting ongoing production with laboratory testing

• 
Contributing to investigations related to unexpected or non-conforming test results

• 
Supporting test verification and transfer activities

• 
Participating in equipment-related activities, including maintenance, calibration, qualification, and troubleshooting

• 
Writing, reviewing, and updating laboratory procedures, test methods, and work instructions

• 
Supporting change control, corrective and preventive actions, and audit activities

• 
Participating in daily stand-up meetings and contributing to task prioritization and workflow

• 
Ensuring that laboratory activities are carried out in compliance with environmental, health, and safety requirements

• 
Contributing to continuous improvement of laboratory processes, workflows, and ways of working

You can expect a role with both routine and non-routine laboratory activities. You will have the opportunity to build a broad network across the organization and gain experience with quality assurance at several stages of a product’s lifecycle.

**Bring quality and reliability to every laboratory task

**To succeed in this position, you work carefully and systematically and understand the importance of accurate documentation and data integrity. You take responsibility for your tasks, follow established procedures, and

communicate clearly if you identify unexpected results, quality risks or challenges.

You enjoy working both independently and as part of a team. As priorities may change depending on production and project needs, you are flexible and able to organize your work accordingly.

We imagine that you:

• 
Are a qualified Laboratory Technician or have a comparable laboratory education

• 
Have experience with practical laboratory work, preferably within quality control, quality assurance, production, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or another regulated industry

• 
Have a strong quality mindset and a structured approach to documentation

• 
Have knowledge of basic statistics and experience evaluating and presenting laboratory data

• 
Are able to write and maintain procedures, test methods, and work instructions

• 
Are comfortable working according to procedures, test methods, and quality requirements

• 
Have experience with laboratory equipment and general laboratory practices

• 
Are curious, solution-oriented, and willing to learn new methods and technologies

• 
Work well with colleagues from different professional backgrounds

• 
Communicate clearly and professionally

• 
Are comfortable using digital systems for laboratory documentation and data handling

• 
Are fluent in Danish and able to communicate in English

Experience from the medical device industry, working under Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements, or using a Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) is an advantage, but not a requirement.

**Interested?

**If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Lotte Stoklund, Team Manager, QA Lifecycle Laboratory, at dklst@coloplast.com

We will invite candidates for interviews continuously, so we encourage you to submit your CV with a short description of your motivation for applying as soon as possible. The position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship - New-Generation Control of Hybrid Wind, Solar and Battery Power Plants - DTU Wind
jobs.description:
European Doctoral Network – WindConnect | DTU Wind and Energy Systems | Fully funded · 36 months.

Shape the future of hybrid renewable power plants
Join the Renewable Power Plants (RPP) section at DTU Wind and Energy Systems and help shape the next generation of control systems for hybrid wind, solar, and battery power plants. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in power systems and renewable energy integration, who are motivated by developing technical, practical solutions to complex real-world challenges and thrive in a highly international and collaborative research environment.

In this fully funded three-year PhD project, you will develop an innovative, technology-agnostic control architecture for hybrid power plants, combining advanced modelling with opportunities for experimental validation in collaboration with European Energy.

The position is part of the WindConnect European Doctoral Network, bringing together 15 PhD researchers across leading European universities and industry partners to advance the next generation of wind energy technology.

Why choose this PhD?

• Unique experimental infrastructure. In close collaboration with European Energy, you will gain hands-on exposure to DTU's MW-scale hybrid power plant research facility, one of only a few such testbeds worldwide. The facility offers opportunities to explore your control concepts in a realistic operational environment, subject to feasibility and access.
• European research community. As part of WindConnect, you will join a vibrant network of 15 doctoral researchers, collaborate with leading academic and industry partners across Europe, and undertake 6-9 months of research stays at partner institutions.
• High-impact research. Your work will help hybrid renewable power plants provide reliable grid services and support the transition to power systems with higher shares of wind and solar energy, with potential implications for grid operators, plant developers, and energy policy.
• Broad career development. Benefit from technical and transferable-skills training, industrial secondments, international conference participation, peer-reviewed publications, and a strong professional network across academia and industry.
About the project
Hybrid Power Plants (HPPs), combining wind, solar PV, and battery energy storage behind a single grid connection point, are emerging as a cornerstone of future power systems. While they can provide grid services beyond the capabilities of individual technologies, coordinating assets from different vendors with varying response times and communication protocols remains a major challenge. Traditional control architectures struggle to reconcile fast local asset responses with slower plant-level actions, while communication delays and interoperability issues add further complexity.

This PhD project addresses these challenges by developing a two-layer, technology-agnostic control architecture for utility-scale HPPs. The architecture is designed to improve interoperability, reduce communication overhead, and enhance the reliability and performance of hybrid power plants.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your research will focus on developing a two-layer, technology-agnostic control architecture for utility-scale hybrid power plants (HPPs) integrating wind, solar PV, and battery storage. The architecture will enable direct communication between the HPP controller and individual asset controllers while addressing interoperability challenges across technologies and vendors. You will design control solutions that coordinate fast local responses with plant-level objectives. The work will combine controller design, high-fidelity modelling and simulation, and, where feasible, experimental evaluation in collaboration with European Energy.

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Model and benchmark state-of-the-art HPP control architectures, including dynamic behaviour and grid-service performance.
• Identify interoperability, communication, and coordination challenges across assets, vendors, and control layers.
• Design and implement a two-layer controller that connects fast local responses with plant-wide coordination.
• Evaluate the proposed architecture using high-fidelity modelling and simulation (e.g. MATLAB/Simulink and Python) and, where feasible, explore experimental testing at DTU's hybrid power plant facility.
• Publish findings in peer-reviewed journals, present at international conferences, and contribute to IEA Wind Task 50 on Hybrid Power Plants.
• Participate in WindConnect training activities and provide limited support for MSc supervision and teaching at DTU.
What we are looking for

Essential qualifications

• MSc degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) in electrical engineering, power system engineering, control engineering, or a related field.
• Sound fundamentals in power-system dynamics and control, with an understanding of converter-interfaced generation and storage.
• Experience with dynamic modelling and simulation using tools such as MATLAB/Simulink, Python, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, PSCAD or comparable software.
• Strong analytical and research skills, with the ability to conduct independent research
Advantageous (nice to have qualifications)

• Familiarity with grid integration requirements, ancillary service provision, and/or multi-vendor renewable power plant control.
• Experience in international or cross-disciplinary research collaborations.
• Strong English communication and interpersonal skills for effective collaboration in international and multidisciplinary teams.
What we offer

• A fully funded 3-year PhD position at DTU, offering co-supervision by experienced researchers and close collaboration with European Energy and leading industry partners in an internationally recognised research environment.
• A collegial, diverse, and inclusive research environment that invests in your development, well-being, and career growth through international networking, multidisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and partnerships with leading universities and industry across Europe.
• Diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are committed to an equitable and inclusive research environment and strongly encourage applications from women and candidates from groups underrepresented in engineering and energy research. We value curiosity, motivation, and collaboration and welcome diverse career paths and backgrounds. 
MSCA eligibility – please check before applying

This position is funded through the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) European Doctoral Network. To be eligible, applicants must:

• Not hold a doctoral degree at the time of recruitment.
• Have less than four years of full-time equivalent research experience after obtaining the degree that qualifies them for PhD studies.
• Not have resided or carried out their main activity (work or studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date.
Please note: Applicants who do not meet these MSCA eligibility criteria cannot be considered for the position, regardless of their qualifications. Please verify your eligibility before applying. 

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

What we offer

• A fully funded 3-year PhD position at DTU, offering co-supervision by experienced researchers and close collaboration with European Energy and leading industry partners in an internationally recognised research environment.
• A collegial, diverse, and inclusive research environment that invests in your development, well-being, and career growth through international networking, multidisciplinary collaboration, leadership training, and partnerships with leading universities and industry across Europe.
• Diversity, equity, and inclusion. We are committed to an equitable and inclusive research environment and strongly encourage applications from women and candidates from groups underrepresented in engineering and energy research. We value curiosity, motivation, and collaboration and welcome diverse career paths and backgrounds.
Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Anca D. Hansen (anca@dtu.dk), Associate Professor Kaushik Das (kdas@dtu.dk) and Head of Section Gregor Giebel (grgi@dtu.dk). 

You can read more at wind.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 22 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A 1-page research statement, including figures and references if deemed necessary (max 500 words). Research achievements (if any), methodological approaches and research objectives relevant to the framework of the PhD study are recommended elements to be included. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Wind and Energy Systems has led wind energy research, teaching, and commercial activities since the 1970s. With approximately 400 staff, it is the world's largest public research institute dedicated to wind and energy systems transition. Internationally recognized for pioneering wind technology and smart energy systems, the department is structured into four divisions: Materials and Components, Wind Turbine Technology, Wind Energy Systems, and Power and Energy Systems. In close collaboration with industry and public authorities, DTU Wind and Energy Systems develops cutting-edge solutions for a sustainable energy future and trains the next generation of engineers. 

About the Division: The Wind Energy Systems division focuses the development of a chain of systems that connects Atmosphere-Plant-Grid-Society. The division is home to several large software projects and datasets that help to disseminate this research to the industry and public.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Manager, Downstream Microbial Manufacturing

Manager, Downstream Microbial Manufacturing – Senior Production Leadership (Leaders of leaders)

A senior production leadership role with responsibility for leading Shift

Supervisors and their teams

Our purpose is to bring hope to life by enabling life-changing therapies for patients around the globe, creating a healthier and happier tomorrow. Our mission is to work side by side with our customers to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

**Lead leaders in complex GMP manufacturing

**At AGC Biologics, your leadership will directly influence how biologic medicines are produced and delivered to patients worldwide.

As Manager within Downstream Microbial Manufacturing, you will take responsibility for a production area operating across multiple shifts. Your direct leadership focus will be the Shift Supervisors who lead the operational teams.

This is a senior manufacturing leadership role for someone who combines a strong technical understanding of biologics production with substantial experience in developing leaders and managing complex GMP operations.

You will create direction and alignment across shifts, ensure reliable production performance and develop the leadership capabilities needed to build a stable and continuously improving manufacturing organisation.

**Full ownership of production performance

**You will take overall ownership of your production area, ensuring that safety, quality, compliance, delivery and performance are managed consistently across all shifts.

Your role connects strategic priorities with daily execution. You will move between the shop floor, leadership discussions and cross-functional decision-making, maintaining a clear understanding of operational performance while ensuring that longer-term improvements remain on track.

Working closely with your Shift Supervisors, you will support them in leading their teams, managing performance and handling both operational and people-related challenges. You will set direction, establish clear expectations and ensure consistency across the leadership team.

You will also collaborate closely with Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain and other internal stakeholders to:

• 
Maintain production readiness and reliable execution

• 
Anticipate and address operational risks

• 
Resolve complex production challenges

• 
Support audits and regulatory inspections

• 
Strengthen processes and operational performance

jobs.occupation: One or more Professors in Cyber Security
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for one or more professors in the field of Cyber Security as per March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The positions are permanent.

**Who we are

**In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems is ranked among the top 50 in the world in the Shanghai Ranking (GRAS). The department employs more than 200 people, of whom approximately 90 are PhD students, and around 40% of all employees are international. In total, the department has more than 800 students enrolled in its BSc and MSc programmes, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and laboratory facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and research results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department here www.es.aau.dk.

The Cyber Security Research Group at Aalborg University (Cyber Security Research Group) is a young and growing research group within the Department of Electronic Systems, focusing on cyber security from various perspectives. Its core research areas are network security, IoT/OT security, applied cryptography, and privacy and security in machine learning. The Cyber Security Research Group consists of 16 members and offers a young, international research environment. The group is responsible for teaching activities in the Master’s programme in Cyber Security, which is taught in English and has more than 100 active Danish and international students. Moreover, the group is strongly engaged in community-building activities, with the AAU Copenhagen campus serving as a hub for weekly CTFs and ethical hacking activities involving dozens of participants.

Your work tasks

You will lead the academic direction of cyber security research and education. The role combines independent academic leadership with close collaboration across the department, within the section, with other research environments, external organisations, and international partners.

Your research and teaching will address one or more areas within applied cryptography, IoT and/or cloud security, security and privacy for big data and machine learning, risk management and threat modelling, mobile security, secure software development, and systems security and privacy. You will initiate and lead research projects, secure and manage external research funding, publish research at an international level, and develop collaborations with industry, public-sector organisations, and universities in Denmark and abroad.

You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral levels, develop courses and teaching materials, and contribute to the planning and coordination of programmes built on problem-based learning. You will also supervise doctoral researchers and early-career colleagues, contribute to relevant committees and academic activities, and take part in developing the department’s research and educational priorities. International collaboration, including participation in networks, conferences, and joint research activities, forms an integral part of the position.

Your competencies

You hold a doctoral degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related field. You have documented original research contributions at an international level within cyber security and a strong publication record in recognised journals and conferences. You can demonstrate a proven track record of attracting, establishing, and managing externally funded research activities, and you have the academic judgement required to develop a coherent research agenda with clear societal and technological relevance.

You bring substantial experience in university teaching, supervision, course development, examination activities, and the development of educational programmes. Familiarity with problem-based learning is relevant, particularly because the role includes contributing to programmes in which students work collaboratively on complex and practice-oriented challenges. You communicate confidently in English, both orally and in writing, and you are willing to develop Danish language skills over time.

You set a clear academic direction while creating constructive working relationships with students, colleagues, and collaborators. You contribute with sound judgement, curiosity, and an ability to turn research ideas into well-organised projects and partnerships. You support the development of early-career researchers, engage openly across disciplines, and help maintain a respectful and collaborative research culture.

**Qualification requirements

**Applicants must be able to document a high degree of original academic production at an international level and experience from teaching at different levels. Including tests/exams, course/study programme management as well as contributions to the development of teaching activities and teaching material.

Emphasis is placed on the extent, to which the applicant, has developed the academic discipline from a research and teaching perspective.

Emphasis may moreover be placed on the applicant’s ability to carry out and develop research-based public-sector consultancy. Also, emphasis will be placed on an assessment of the applicant’s ability to perform research and teaching management tasks and possibly fulfil other functions, for example in relation to the university’s external cooperation.

Emphasis will also be placed on the applicant's ability to undertake pedagogical supervision, supervision and academic assessment work.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of ten publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this .

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. The successful applicant is expected, with support from the university, to acquire Danish language skills over time and to be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 2–5 years of employment, including grading and supervising students, at a level corresponding to the teaching undertaken.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Professor”.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

Contacts

• Mads Græsbøll Christensen: mgc@es.aau.dk

We are seeking an experienced Senior Authorised Person (SAP) / Switching Leader (Koblingsleder) to support electrical operations on a major engineering project in Denmark.

The successful candidate will be responsible for coordinating safe switching operations, electrical isolations and safety procedures across high-voltage (HV) and low-voltage (LV) electrical systems.

The position operates within an established electrical safety management structure, under the designated Operation Manager (Driftsansvarlig Person), and in accordance with applicable Danish electrical safety regulations and EN 50110-1.

Key Responsibilities

• 
Plan, coordinate and oversee HV and LV switching operations.

• 
Prepare and review switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Coordinate electrical isolations, earthing and safe access procedures.

• 
Prepare, issue and cancel safety documents within the scope of assigned authorisation.

• 
Coordinate with Control Engineers and electrical work teams during operational activities.

• 
Ensure appropriate safety precautions are implemented before electrical work begins.

• 
Supervise and coordinate personnel involved in electrical operational activities.

• 
Support commissioning, energisation and electrical system handover.

• 
Maintain accurate switching records, operational logs and safety documentation.

• 
Participate in safety audits, risk assessments and toolbox talks.

• 
Ensure compliance with site-specific electrical safety procedures and applicable Danish regulations.

Qualifications and Experience

• 
Relevant qualification in electrical engineering or equivalent professional experience.

• 
Extensive experience working with HV and LV electrical systems.

• 
Previous experience as a Senior Authorised Person, Switching Leader, Control Engineer or equivalent.

• 
Strong understanding of electrical switching, isolation, earthing and safe working procedures.

• 
Knowledge of EN 50110-1 and electrical safety management systems.

• 
Experience preparing switching schedules and electrical safety documentation.

• 
Demonstrated ability to coordinate electrical work teams and operational activities.

• 
Strong communication, organisational and safety leadership skills.

• 
Good command of English.

Electrical Safety Requirements

The successful candidate will undergo a competence assessment and receive the necessary written operational appointment and authorisation under the project's Danish electrical safety management arrangements (KLS-D) before undertaking regulated electrical activities.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering?

Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells, a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data.

In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners.

Successful candidates must document:

• Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE)
• Python programming skills
• Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar)
• Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Catalytic CO₂ Conversion to Carbon Nanotubes - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Can we transform greenhouse gases into some of the world's most valuable advanced materials? 
At DTU Physics, we are looking for a talented and ambitious PhD candidate to help pioneer a completely new route for carbon utilization. The project aims to discover catalytic materials capable of converting CO₂ directly into carbon nanotubes (CNTs), combining climate-change mitigation with the sustainable production of next-generation functional materials. 

Carbon nanotubes are among the most sought-after nanomaterials due to their exceptional strength, low weight, electrical conductivity, and thermal stability. They are key components in future energy technologies, electronics, and lightweight structural materials. Yet, conventional CNT production relies on fossil-derived feedstocks and carries a substantial carbon footprint. This PhD project seeks to establish an entirely new catalytic paradigm in which captured CO₂ becomes the raw material for producing high-value carbon nanomaterials. 

You will join the Catalysis and Operando Characterization (CATOC) group at DTU, an international research environment at the forefront of catalyst development and operando characterization. Working in close collaboration with Leipzig University, you will combine catalyst synthesis, catalytic testing, advanced electron microscopy, and operando X-ray characterization to reveal how catalysts form, evolve, and produce CNTs under realistic reaction conditions.

As a PhD student, you will have access to world-leading infrastructure, including advanced electron microscopy, in situ and operando characterization tools, and state-of-the-art facilities for catalyst development and testing.

If you are excited by tackling fundamental scientific questions while contributing to sustainable technologies, we encourage you to apply.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall goal will be to discover and develop novel catalytic materials that enable the conversion of CO₂ into carbon nanotubes.

The project will include:

• Development of mono- and multimetallic catalyst materials based on metal silicates.
• Catalytic testing and performance evaluation under realistic reaction conditions.
• Investigation of CNT growth, harvesting, and catalyst regeneration strategies.
• Advanced in situ and operando characterization using electron microscopy and X-ray based methods.
• Establishing structure-activity relationships that guide the design of next-generation catalysts.
You have a strong background in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, physics, nanotechnology, or a related field. Experience with catalysis, materials synthesis, electron microscopy, or characterization techniques is an advantage.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in the use of SWOT for small-scale ocean processes - DTU Space
jobs.description:
Small-scale ocean processes play an important role in shaping ocean circulation and freshwater distribution in the Arctic. Yet, they remain difficult to observe and represent in numerical models. This limits our ability to understand and predict the ocean and its response to a changing climate. SWOT (Surface Water and Ocean Topography) provides high-resolution observations of sea-surface height that can be used to better constrain these processes and the ocean state. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
This PhD will focus on assimilating SWOT observations into a high-resolution ocean model with a focus on the Polar Regions. An emphasis will be on developing surrogate models using Scientific Machine learning to reduce the computational cost of simulations and enable efficient prediction and exploration of ocean processes.

The candidate is expected to have a background in ocean modelling and remote sensing, preferably with experience in satellite altimetry and ocean modelling using the MITgcm (MIT’s General Circulation modelling framework). 

The candidate will work in a stimulating environment at DTU Space, with close collaboration with SWOT researchers, other DTU departments, and international partners. The candidate should be motivated to work in an international environment and participate in relevant research travel.

 Niels Bohr Institute

  The Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in spectral modelling of nuclear restframe UV-optical emission from Active Galactic Nuclei.

  Start date is expected to be February 1, 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

  The project
 The project involves developing software algorithms and pipelines for robust, reproducible, and efficient spectral modelling and analysis of observations from large spectral surveys.
 
 The PhD project includes (a) developing modern and efficient software code to perform analysis of AGN spectral data with the aim to robustly perform reliable spectral decomposition of the AGN emission at restframe UV, optical and infrared wavelengths; (b) applying said spectral decomposition algorithm to large databases of AGN Sky Surveys for subsequent analysis; (c) development of algorithms that utilizes Neural Networks to assist in analysis of the large spectral databases of existing and new large sky surveys.
 
 Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field of active galactic nuclei with significant expertise in developing modern software code for spectral modelling of observations of the nuclear UV-optical emission.
 
 Candidates with a background in AGN physics, AGN spectral analysis and spectral decomposition are strongly encouraged to apply. Experience in handling large datasets from large Astronomical Sky Surveys, such as Sloan Digital Sky Survey, is a strong asset (i.e., advantage). A background in or experience (whole or in part) with Deep Learning, various neural network architectures and auto-encoders are strong assets. Specific experience with use of high-performance computing, advanced statistics, optimization and performance testing of software algorithms and with scientific software development in Python are all favorable assets.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?
 Vestergaard’s group is part of DARK, Niels Bohr Institute, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. DARK’s areas of research include, but are not limited to, observations, simulations and theory of astrophysical transients and cosmic explosions (including gravitational waves, tidal disruption events and supernovae), neutrino astrophysics, high-redshift galaxies, fundamental cosmology, dark matter, black holes and AGN, and cosmic dust. DARK scientists reside in the new Niels Bohr Building at the North Campus in Copenhagen, sharing space with the other astrophysics sections (Stars & Planetary Sciences, Cosmic DAWN center) and the rest of the Niels Bohr Institute.

  DARK is committed to excellence through diversity and strives to establish a working climate that welcomes, celebrates, and promotes respect for the contributions of all students and employees.  To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. physics or astronomy. jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Crop root development, and its effects on root zone water and nitrogen dynamics
jobs.description:
Department of Plant and Environmental Science, Faculty of Science at University of Copenhagen is offering a 34-months Postdoc position in Crop root development, and its effects on root zone water and nitrogen dynamics commencing February 1st 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Further information on the Department is linked at https://plen.ku.dk/english/.  Inquiries about the position can be made to Professor Kristian Thorup-Kristensen, email: ktk@plen.ku.dk.

  Job description
 The postdoc will be working on crop root and root zone research in our newly established root research facility RootAccess (https://plen.ku.dk/english/research/crop_sciences/cpps/rootaccess/). The facility is equipped to allow the study of crop root growth to 3 meters depth and to follow the dynamic effects on soil water and nitrogen (uptake, leaching and denitrification) to the same depth. During the project, a number of common crops will be grown in rotation in the facility, allowing the study of their different exploitation of the root zone for water and nitrogen, both during the crop growth seasons as well as during periods without crops, to cover rotational effects over the years. Studies will be based on soil water sensors, minirhizotrons, soil water suction cells, and soil gas samplers, all installed at several depths in the soil profile. Furthermore, we use isotopic tracers to follow root uptake. The postdoc will be part of the team working on the project and facility, and co-responsible for running the experiments in the facility. Apart from the experimental work and contribution to publishing the results, a main task for the postdoc will be to produce well organized datasets and clear result presentation, continuously updated during the project.

  Description of the scientific environment
 The postdoc will be hosted in the Crop Physiology and Production Systems research group (https://plen.ku.dk/english/research/crop_sciences/cpps/), which focuses on crop growth and quality at the crop, crop rotation, and cropping system level. The group has a specific focus on crop root research, using field-scale root research facilities, including the RadiMax root phenotyping facility as well as the newly developed RootAccess facility.

  Required qualifications
 The applicants should hold professional and personal skills and qualifications as stated below:

   	
• A PhD degree in agricultural science, or related disciplines. 	
• Solid knowledge of whole plant and crop physiology, including plant and soil water and nutrient relations. 	
• Good technical skills and practical experimental experience with whole plant or preferably field crop experiments, as well as modern plant analyses and monitoring techniques. 	
• Competent on data management and statistical analysis, etc. 	
• Good record, considering your early career stage, of peer-reviewed scientific publications

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Soft Robotic Applications - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in developing innovative robotic systems that can adapt their mechanical properties to interact safely and effectively with their environment? Do you have a background in robotics, mechatronics, and control, and enjoy combining mechanical design with hands-on experimental research? 

At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to develop and validate novel robotic technologies integrating compliant mechanisms, variable stiffness, and advanced control strategies. Your research will contribute to the development of adaptable robotic systems capable of performing complex physical operations in challenging and uncertain environments.

The PhD position is part of RESSORT, a European research project aimed at advancing soft and adaptive robotics through the integration of innovative materials, compliant structures, sensing, and intelligent control. The project addresses the limitations of conventional rigid robotic systems by developing solutions capable of adapting their mechanical behaviour to different tasks and operating conditions.

Your research will focus on the design, modelling, and control of robotic systems incorporating soft and variable-stiffness mechanisms. Particular attention will be given to the integration of mechanical adaptability and control to improve physical interaction, operational stability, and performance. The developed methods will be implemented and experimentally validated on robotic platforms, including adaptive and morphing aerial systems.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your main responsibility will be to investigate and develop mechatronic and control solutions for soft and adaptive robotic systems. The research will combine mechanical design, dynamic modelling, control development, and experimental validation, addressing the challenges associated with integrating compliant structures into robotic platforms.

Your primary tasks will include:

• Design and develop compliant and variable-stiffness mechanisms for robotic applications.
• Develop mathematical and dynamic models of robotic systems incorporating flexible and adaptive mechanical structures.
• Investigate control strategies to manage changes in mechanical configuration, stiffness, and interaction forces.
• Integrate actuators, sensors, and embedded control systems into experimental robotic platforms.
• Develop methods for stable and efficient robotic operation under varying mechanical and environmental conditions.
• Implement and validate the developed technologies through simulations and experiments on real robotic systems.
• Collaborate with international research and industrial partners and disseminate research results through scientific publications and conferences.
We expect you to have a strong background in mechatronics, robotics, mechanical engineering, control engineering, or a closely related field. Solid competences in mechanical design, dynamic modelling, and control of robotic systems are particularly important.

Experience with CAD tools, actuators, embedded systems, and experimental prototyping will be considered an advantage. Good programming skills in MATLAB/Simulink, C++, and/or Python are expected. Familiarity with compliant mechanisms, soft robotics, variable-stiffness systems, or aerial robotics will be beneficial.

We are particularly interested in candidates who enjoy combining theoretical developments with practical implementation and experimental work. You should be motivated to develop innovative solutions, work independently, and contribute actively to a multidisciplinary and international research environment.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of applicants will be based on their academic qualifications, research potential, and relevance of their technical background to the proposed PhD project. Particular emphasis will be placed on competences in mechatronic design, dynamic modelling, and control, as well as demonstrated experience in the development and experimental validation of robotic systems.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Matteo Fumagalli, mafum@dtu.dk.

You can read more about the department at www.electro.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 5 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A brief description (maximum one page) of relevant technical or research projects, highlighting the applicant's individual contributions to mechanical design, modelling, control development, and experimental validation of robotic systems
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.
