jobs.occupation: Global Assoc Commercial Competitive Intelligence Director
jobs.description:
**Your impact begins here

**As Global Associate Commercial Competitive Intelligence Director, you will help shape the strategies behind Novo’s projects and future commercial brands in diabetes, obesity, Liver and Cardiovascular disease. You will monitor the commercial competitive landscape, competitor strategies and turn what you find into data-driven insights that sharpen decisions at project, product and portfolio level. By elevating and challenging our approach, you will help Novo stay ahead – and strengthen the commercial strategies that bring treatments to people living with diabetes, obesity, Liver and Cardiovascular disease.

**What You’ll Bring

**You think independently, set the agenda before you are asked and bring people together across functions to influence decisions. You are comfortable in an expert role and confident managing stakeholders at every level. We are open to candidates at different career stages, so the depth of experience we look for will vary with your background:

• An M.Sc. in Business, Medicine or Life/Pharmaceutical Sciences.

• Relevant experience in similar roles.

• Experience within the pharmaceutical industry is highly preferred.

• Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret complex data and translate it into actionable intelligence.

• The ability – or a proven track record – to communicate scientific, medical and commercial information clearly to diverse audiences, including senior management.

• An understanding of drug development, commercial strategy and pharmaceutical value chains, with depth matching your seniority.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Experience in social media monitoring.

**What You’ll Do

**You will provide high-quality monitoring and insight generation on the commercial competitive landscape and competitor strategies, helping commercial teams act on what is happening in the market today.

• Deliver high-quality, data-driven insights on the commercial competitive landscape across diabetes, obesity, Liver and Cardiovascular disease.

• Drive strong commercial competitive insights that improve decision-making at project, product and portfolio level.

• Lead assessments of key intelligence topics of strategic interest, working with cross-functional stakeholders.

• Act as a strategic partner to Commercial teams, making sure real-time insights are translated into competitive counter-strategies.

• Contribute to building and developing the Commercial Competitive Intelligence function.

• Encourage collaboration and knowledge sharing across the organisation.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join the Commercial Competitive Intelligence team, which monitors, assesses and activates commercial competitive intelligence within core strategic areas in diabetes, obesity, Liver and CVD. The team is part of Strategic Insights, where you will work alongside colleagues in Customer & Consumer Insights and in Data, Analytics & AI Strategy.

Strategic Insights sits within Product & Portfolio Strategy, which drives commercial strategy, medical affairs and business development across all therapy areas. The area acts as a connector and compass – guiding the portfolio for sustained competitiveness upstream and maximising its potential through strong commercial strategies and competitive launches downstream.

Your closest partners will be Commercial teams, and you will engage with stakeholders across the value chain. Bringing these perspectives together – and creating clarity on what competitor moves mean for Novo – is how your insights will turn into action.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will take on an expert role with real influence: your insights will feed directly into decisions on projects, products and the wider portfolio. You will be trusted to set the agenda, make your voice heard and challenge established thinking when the evidence calls for it.

You will also help develop the Commercial Competitive Intelligence function itself, giving you the chance to shape how the work is done, not just deliver it. Working across commercial, medical and data-focused colleagues, you will broaden your perspective and build new skills on the job. Because we are open to different career stages, your responsibilities and salary will be tailored to your experience.

At Novo Nordisk, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 847,000.00 to 1,245,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn competitive intelligence into decisions that keep Novo ahead in diabetes and obesity, apply for the Global Assoc Competitive Intelligence Director role by 29 October 2026.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Analog IC Design Lead – Power Management
jobs.description:
Analog IC Design Lead – Power Management

Lotus Microsystems is looking for a motivated and experienced Analog IC Design Lead – Power Management to join our team at our headquarters in Copenhagen. Join a DeepTech company at the forefront of innovation, where ideas move quickly from concept to reality in a collaborative startup environment.

Position Summary

We are looking for an experienced Analog IC Design Lead – Power Management to join our Engineering team. You will lead and contribute to the development of next-generation power converters for a wide range of applications.

You will work on state-of-the-art power management technology alongside a team with hands-on expertise in power electronics, IC design, and semiconductor process development. The role combines technical leadership with hands-on circuit design and close collaboration across disciplines.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide technical leadership for IC development projects and design activities.

• Design integrated power converters and monitoring circuits.

• Design analog and mixed-signal circuit blocks.

• Drive and coordinate IC design and layout activities, working closely with design and layout engineers.

• Simulate and verify circuits using transistor-level and system-level simulation tools.

• Contribute to silicon validation, characterization, and troubleshooting.

• Collaborate with engineers across IC design, power electronics, semiconductor processes, and system development.

Qualifications

• Master’s degree (or higher) in Electrical Engineering or a related field.

• At least 10 years of relevant IC design experience.

• Strong understanding of and hands-on experience with power converters, such as linear regulators, switched-inductor DC-DC converters, and switched-capacitor DC-DC converters.

• In-depth knowledge and hands-on experience in designing integrated power converters, gate drivers, and PWM control circuits.

• In-depth knowledge and hands-on experience in designing analog circuits, including comparators, amplifiers, current sensors, temperature sensors, bandgap references, and related building blocks.

• Experience with IC design environments and EDA tools, such as Cadence (preferred), Synopsys, and/or Mentor Graphics.

• Experience with technical leadership, project leadership, and/or technology leadership in previous IC development projects is a plus.

• Experience with power management ICs (PMICs) and DC-DC converter applications is a plus.

• Experience with PCB design, assembly, and experimental/silicon validation is a plus.

Personal Competencies

• Based in Copenhagen or within reasonable commuting distance. Lotus Microsystems will support relocation for the right candidate, where needed.

• Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary and international team.

• A creative, curious, and innovative mindset, with a passion for solving complex technical challenges.

• Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain and champion new ideas, actively contribute to brainstorming, and present technical concepts clearly.

• Strong planning and time-management skills, with the ability to adapt to changing priorities in a fast-paced startup environment.

Additional Information

For more information about the position, please contact Martin Lantz, IC Design Manager, at mlantz@lotus-microsystems.com.

We will process candidates on a running basis.

About Us

Lotus Microsystems creates advanced power solutions that transform power and thermal management, unlocking the full potential of AI and advanced computing. Our patented power silicon interposer technology enables miniaturized power delivery systems with exceptional power density and thermal performance.

At Lotus Microsystems in Copenhagen, you will experience an informal, collaborative, and hands-on work environment. Our open office setup fosters strong teamwork and close interaction among colleagues.

Although we are a small team, we are truly international, with colleagues from diverse professional and cultural backgrounds. This diversity enriches our work and gives us a global perspective that resonates with our international customers and partners.

Join Lotus Microsystems and help us develop cutting-edge power technology that can make a meaningful impact on the future of AI and advanced computing.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in sustainable cropping systems
jobs.description:
The department of Plant and Environmental Sciences invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in faba bean/cereal intercropping. The project is part of the research centre “N2CROP”, which is a centre for legume innovation funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The centre is a partnership between Aarhus University, the Technical University of Denmark, University of Copenhagen, the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, and La Trobe University

Start date is (expected to be) 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Intercropping is considered a potential more sustainable cropping system reducing fertilizer and pesticide inputs. Despite the well-known effects of intercropping there is still a knowledge gap considering belowground interactions. The project will focus on intercropping of faba bean and cereals, and the potential benefits of the fun mutant (fixation under nitrate). Above- as well as belowground complementarity and competition between crops will be examined with focus on nitrogen dynamics. The project will also focus on biological nitrogen fixation, transfer of nitrogen between species and effect of specific rhizobium strains on fixation. Experiments will be conducted in field trials and in rhizotubes, and the field experiments will be done in close collaboration with SLU in Uppsala where similar experiments will be carried out. Results from the experiments will feed into development of an intercropping crop modelling part.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of agronomy, biology and/or root science. Applicants can have a background with specific knowledge on root development and function, grain legume production, intercropping, crop competition and biological nitrogen fixation. Experience with greenhouse and/or field studies in combination with one or more of the abovementioned topics is an advantage.

Our group and research- and what do we offer?

The PhD position is placed in the Belowground Crop Ecology research group headed by Associate professor Dorte Bodin Dresbøll. Focus of the research group is on resilient and sustainable cropping systems with special emphasis on belowground interactions, root development and function. We are working with grain legumes, forage legumes and cereals for food and feed. Main topics of the group are drought tolerance, nutrient acquisition and root exudation.

The group is a part of the Agricultural Section of Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We are located at the Taastrup Campus outside Copenhagen.

We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include field and greenhouse facilities, modern laboratories and specialized root research facilities.

Principal supervisor is Associate professor Dorte Bodin Dresbøll, Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, dbdr@plen.ku.dk, +4535333452

The PhD programme

Qualifications needed for the regular programme

To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. [relevant educations]. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

Terms of employment in the regular programme

Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the SCIENCE faculty, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

• Carry through an independent research project under supervision

• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE

• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad

• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities

• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals

• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project

We are looking for the following qualifications:

• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project

• Relevant publications

• Relevant work experience

• Other relevant professional activities

• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in agronomy and specifically grain legumes, root physiology, and intercropping systems

• Good language skills

Application and Assessment Procedure

Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

Please include:

• Motivated letter for applying for the specific PhD project (max. one page)

• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

• Publication list (if possible)

• Reference letters (if available)

Application deadline:

The deadline for applications is 1 November 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

The further process

After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in week 47.

Questions

For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor.

Materials send directly to the principal supervisor will not be considered.

General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Part of the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU), and among Europe’s top-ranking universities, the University of Copenhagen promotes research and teaching of the highest international standard. Rich in tradition and modern in outlook, the University gives students and staff the opportunity to cultivate their talent in an ambitious and informal environment. An effective organisation – with good working conditions and a collaborative work culture – creates the ideal framework for a successful academic career.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Soft Matter physics and Food Science
jobs.description:
The Department of Food Science and the Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in colloidal research in food science. The PhD project has the overall goal of describing the molecular structure of casein micelles through computational and experimental investigations, with focus on the role of κ caseins. The candidate will be part of the CaIFF center for the use of neutrons for the investigation of colloids and interfaces in food science and pharmacy (https://pharmacy.ku.dk/research/caiff/).

Expected start date is 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Background. Casein micelles (CMs) are the main protein constituent of milk (80% of protein) and defining for dairy product taste and structure. CMs are 100-200 nm globular particles, formed by a hydrated network of disordered casein proteins, named αS1, αSs, β, and κ casein. The caseins are cross-linked through binding to ionic calcium and colloidal calcium phosphate, and through hydrophobic interactions. Post-translational modifications play an important role in this, as the ionic interactions are largely mediated by casein phosphorylation sites. The CMs are stabilized by κ caseins that are believed to form a hairy layer on the CM surface. Therefore, κ casein are particularly important for CM stability. κ caseins moreover contain a rennet cleavage site, separating its anchoring para κ casein domain from the water-soluble caseinomacropeptide, the primary component of the stabilizing hairy layer. Enzymatic cleavage of this site promotes coagulation and curd formation.

Goal. Despite decades of research, central questions remain regarding the CM structure, their molecular organization, and dynamic behaviour. The goal of the PhD project is to answer fundamental questions like: are all caseins needed for CM formation? What is the role of post-translational modifications in the casein-calcium network formation, and in the κ casein hairy layer? How extended is the stabilizing hairy layer, and how does it depend on for example pH or solvent? What is the dynamic exchange of caseins between soluble caseins or other CMs? In other words, the PhD project’s aim is to understand the molecular interactions in CM which are central to the unique food properties of dairy products like milk, cream, and cheese, with a particular focus of κ casein.

How. Methodological strategy involves state-of-the-art molecular dynamics simulations for building a molecular model of casein micelles. Advanced x-ray and neutron scattering experiments, will be used to validate the model. Scattering experiments provide information of the hierarchical structure of CMs, whereas molecular simulations model the molecules and their interactions. The combination of simulations and scattering data is particularly strong, as the simulated molecular predictions can be validated experimentally. The project thus involves preparing samples, collecting and analysing scattering data and complementary data when needed, and running MD simulations and comparing these to the experimental data. [AL1]

Societal impact. By understanding casein micelles better, the project supports the development of more sustainable dairy products based on plant-based or precision fermented proteins. Such approaches could remedy the green house gas emissions and adverse effect on biodiversity and animal welfare in traditional dairy production.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for applicants with a strong background in molecular modelling, for example applied to food or structural biology. Experience with any of the following is an advantages:

• Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations; coarse-grained force fields, for example Martini.

• Small-angle x-ray scattering (SAXS), small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) or other x-ray or neutron scattering experiments.

• Programming, for example use of Python and GitHub.

• Data analysis, inverse problems and statistical analysis.

• Mathematical understanding, knowledge of integration, Fourier transformation etc.

• Wet lab experience; protein purification, experience with with colloidal and self-assembled systems.

Finally, the candidate needs to posses good written and oral communication skills.

Our group and research – and what we offer?

You will be part of a very strong cross-institutional and international research environment through the CaIFF center (https://pharmacy.ku.dk/research/caiff/). This means that other PhD students will start approximately at the same time, and you will be part of a unique network of young researchers in the center. You will be supervised by newly appointed tenure track assistant professor Andreas Larsen as well as associate professor Jacob Kirkensgaard (https://www.erda.dk/vgrid/JJKK/), who are affiliated with the Department of Food science and the Niels Bohr Institute at University of Copenhagen. Thus, you will be in a research environment focusing on self-assembly, dynamic structure formation within food science, but also have colleques in the related field of polymer science and soft matter. You will get regular supervision and be part of a lively research group with students at all level from BSc to PhDs and postdocs. A strong methodological focus core technique in the group is on the use of x-ray and neutron scattering experiments to probe structure and molecular self-assembly at the nanometer-scale.

The Departments offers unique facilities. Department of Food science have state-of-the art laboratory facilities for sample preparation and characterization. Computational resources are available through national and European supercomputer facilities LUMI and Computerome, along with local small-scale GPU resources at the Niels Bohr Institute. Local SAXS instrument are available at both institutes, and managed through the cross-disciplinary X-ray center (CXC), and thereby readily available for the project. Only one hour from the University of Copenhangen, in Lund in Sweden, there is access to the world-class x-ray synchrotron MAX-IV, and the project involves SAXS experiments there. Moreover, the group regularly visits neutron facilities in Europe, and will be frequent users of the neutron facility European Spallation Source (ESS) also in Lund, which is expected to open for users during 2027.

Principal supervisor is associate professor Jacob Kirkensgaard, Niels Bohr Institute and the Department of Food Science, University of Copenhagen, jjkk@food.ku.

Co-supervisor is tenure-track assistant professor Andreas Larsen, Niels Bohr Institute and the Department of Food Science, University of Copenhagen, andreas.larsen@food.ku.dk.

The PhD programme

Qualifications needed for the regular programme

To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. [relevant educations]. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

Terms of employment in the regular programme

Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD  programme

• Carry through an independent research project under supervision

• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad

• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities

We are looking for the following qualifications:

Application and Assessment Procedure

If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

Application deadline:

The further process

After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in sustainable cropping systems
jobs.description:
The department of Plant and Environmental Sciences invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in faba bean/cereal intercropping. The project is part of the research centre “N2CROP”, which is a centre for legume innovation funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The centre is a partnership between Aarhus University, the Technical University of Denmark, University of Copenhagen, the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, and La Trobe University

Start date is (expected to be) 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project

Intercropping is considered a potential more sustainable cropping system reducing fertilizer and pesticide inputs. Despite the well-known effects of intercropping there is still a knowledge gap considering belowground interactions. The project will focus on intercropping of faba bean and cereals, and the potential benefits of the fun mutant (fixation under nitrate). Above- as well as belowground complementarity and competition between crops will be examined with focus on nitrogen dynamics. The project will also focus on biological nitrogen fixation, transfer of nitrogen between species and effect of specific rhizobium strains on fixation. Experiments will be conducted in field trials and in rhizotubes, and the field experiments will be done in close collaboration with SLU in Uppsala where similar experiments will be carried out. Results from the experiments will feed into development of an intercropping crop modelling part.

Who are we looking for?

We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of agronomy, biology and/or root science. Applicants can have a background with specific knowledge on root development and function, grain legume production, intercropping, crop competition and biological nitrogen fixation. Experience with greenhouse and/or field studies in combination with one or more of the abovementioned topics is an advantage.

Our group and research- and what do we offer?

The PhD position is placed in the Belowground Crop Ecology research group headed by Associate professor Dorte Bodin Dresbøll. Focus of the research group is on resilient and sustainable cropping systems with special emphasis on belowground interactions, root development and function. We are working with grain legumes, forage legumes and cereals for food and feed. Main topics of the group are drought tolerance, nutrient acquisition and root exudation.

The group is a part of the Agricultural Section of Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We are located at the Taastrup Campus outside Copenhagen.

We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include field and greenhouse facilities, modern laboratories and specialized root research facilities.

jobs.occupation: Tenure Track Assistant Professor in Infectious Animal Disease Modelling for Sustainable One Health Actions
jobs.description:
The University seeks to appoint a tenure track assistant professor to commence 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Information on the department can be found at: https://www.sund.ku.dk/.

Subject area: Infectious disease epidemiology, modelling, animal health, One Health, and sustainable health systems

The Tenure-Track Assistant Professor will lead research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, with particular emphasis on how changes in environmental conditions, animal populations, production systems, and management practices influence disease emergence, transmission, and control. The position will combine infectious disease epidemiology, mathematical and statistical modelling, data science, and economic analysis to generate evidence supporting disease preparedness, prevention, and control.

The successful candidate will:

• Lead independent research on the dynamics of infectious disease spread in health systems, including the influence of environmental and production system changes.

• Develop and apply simulation, epidemiological, and statistical models to assess disease and spillover risks, evaluate mitigation and control strategies, and quantify their economic implications.

• Demonstrate strong programming skills in R and other relevant programming languages, including experience in managing, processing, and analysing large and complex datasets.

• Have experience in developing and applying epidemiological disease-spread models, including model calibration, validation, parameter estimation, and calculation of epidemiological indicators such as the basic reproduction number (R₀) across different animal species and production systems.

• Design and implement epidemiological modelling frameworks.

• Validate and calibrate models using large-scale national datasets, ensuring scientific robustness, methodological validity, and relevance for policy and decision-making.

• Translate research findings into evidence supporting risk-based disease prevention, preparedness, and control.

• Establish and maintain collaborations with key stakeholders, including the Danish Veterinary and Food Administration, industry partners such as SEGES and Landbrug & Fødevarer (L&F), and international organisations such as the FAO.

• Lead and secure independent research funding through competitive national and international funding calls. The position requires demonstrated experience in securing external funding, as well as the ambition to develop research ideas into externally funded projects and provide scientific leadership for such projects within the TIPTON Research Group.

• Contribute to the development and delivery of One Health and sustainability teaching, with a particular focus on infectious diseases, disease preparedness, and the interactions between animal, human, and environmental health.

• Contribute to teaching in data science, including data management, dataset preparation and handling, statistical analysis, programming, and the analysis of large-scale and complex datasets.

• Supervise students and contribute to research capacity building within infectious disease epidemiology, disease modelling, data science, and One Health.

• Contribute to the delivery of government services undertaken by the Department, including research-based advice, preparedness activities, risk assessments, and other activities relevant to infectious disease modelling and control.

The position is expected to combine methodological excellence in infectious disease modelling and data science with applied epidemiological research, generating evidence that is directly relevant to disease preparedness, private and public bodies, sustainable production systems, animal health and resilient health systems.

The tenure track assistant professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

• research, including publication/academic dissemination

• research-based teaching

• sharing knowledge with society

• participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors

The tenure track assistant professor’s performance will be evaluated through annual evaluations. Furthermore, the tenure track assistant professor will be evaluated in a mid-track appraisal.

After no more than six years of employment and on condition of a positive final appraisal, the tenure track assistant professor will be employed as associate professor. Find more information about tenure track at the University of Copenhagen.

Required qualifications

To be qualified for an assistant professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

• a PhD degree or similar qualifications within the subject area

• research experience within the field of the position

The tenure track assistant professor must have an academic standing showing internationally competitive research, and/or have internationally recognized high potential to make a future impact.

The assistant professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

Salary and employment conditions

The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

The position is permanent.

Employment is as Tenure Track Assistant Professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector at www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

Questions

For further information, please contact Research Group Leader: Professor Beate Conrady, bcon@sund.ku.dk

Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

Application

The application must be submitted in English, and must include the following documents:

• Application (Including motivation for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages))

• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding)

• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD and other relevant diplomas)

• A complete list of publications

• Research plan (2-4 pages)

• Teaching plan

• Uploads of maximum 5 publications to be considered in the assessment

• Teaching portfolio, if applicable (Guidelines)

Please note: It is mandatory to upload a teaching plan in the online application form. Should you not be able to produce a teaching plan, please upload a blank document in this box instead.

Application procedure

After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

The application will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested in this post to apply.

Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, 18 November 2026.

Interviews for this position are likely to be held on 7 April 2027.

We are looking for one or two highly motivated researcher interested in transcription regulation at the DNRF Center of Excellence, Center for Gene Expression (CGEN), within the Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM), at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Starting date: 1st of January 2027 or after agreement.

Information on the department can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/

Our research

CGEN is an interdisciplinary research center consisting of 6 research groups located in modern laboratories in the Mærsk Tower at the Panum Institute. Our mission is to use a cutting-edge ensemble of genetic, cell biological, biochemical, organismal, and modern ‘omic’-approaches to achieve a comprehensive understanding of the process of gene expression.

CGEN performs ground-breaking research in a collaborative and ambitious environment, where young researchers are offered the best conditions to engage in bold and imaginative research. CGEN is also a center of learning, where PhDs and postdocs receive comprehensive insights in the cellular processes underlying gene expression, as well as a clear view of their medical importance and potential for a future research career.

Information on CGEN and its individual groups can be found at: https://cgen.ku.dk/ and on ICMM at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/

Your job

The researcher’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

• research, including publication/academic dissemination duties

• research-based teaching and mentorship, primarily in a laboratory setting.

The project will be decided in consultation with the selected candidate(s) in accordance with ongoing research programmes within the individual groups. Broadly projects are focused on understanding the various aspects of the process of gene expression, ranging from the mechanisms of 3D chromatin organisation to transcription, mRNA processing, translation, and protein turnover. CGEN addresses fundamental questions in this broad field at the leading edge of science and aims to dramatically expand our knowledge of the processes, signals and factors allowing a gene to be transcribed while integrating with protein synthesis and protein turnover, so that the overall integrity of gene expression is maintained.

jobs.occupation: Are you a Flight Instructor? Explore Multiple Career Paths at Greybird, no matter your level.
jobs.description:

jobs.occupation: 170026 Clinical Professor of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Clinical Professor of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology 
 (Fixed-Term, 5 Years)

  Department of Clinical Medicine
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

  The University seeks to appoint a clinical professor of Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology to commence as soon as possible. The externally funded professorship is combined with a consultancy at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet, Department of ORL, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology in the Capital Region.

  It is a requirement for appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the professorship and the consultancy. In order to be considered for the position, the applicant must send two applications: one to the Faculty (the professorship) and one to the hospital (the consultancy) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the consultancy. This also applies to applicants who are already employed as consultants at the Hospital. Please find the advertisement for the consultancy at www.sundhedsjobs.dk/

  Both the professorship and the consultancy will be financed by Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

  Find information about the department.

  Job description
 In the consideration of applications for the professorship, the main emphasis will be on the applicant's ability to document a high level of original scientific work at an international level within the area of Otorhinolaryngology.

  The professor's responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination – The professor is expected to conduct and lead high-quality clinical and translational research within otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery and audiology. Relevant research areas that are prioritized will be head and neck surgical oncology and biomarker development. The professor is furthermore expected to contribute to the development and implementation of new diagnostic and treatment approaches within the field. 	
• Research-based teaching, including associated examination – The professor will contribute actively to undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education through research-based teaching. In particular, the professor is expected to contribute to teaching and examination within the Clinical Course in Otorhinolaryngology and the Medical Specialty Focused Course and Exam in Otorhinolaryngology, and to supervise medical students, PhD candidates, and clinical researchers. The professor will contribute to the integration of current research findings into clinical teaching, curriculum development, and specialist training. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of researchers – The professor is expected to play a central role in the development and strategic direction of the research environment within otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery and audiologThe professor is expected to contribute to innovation and societal impact through the development, evaluation, and implementation of new knowledge, technologies, and clinical practices. 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments   Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for a clinical professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution, and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to:

   	
• Document a high degree of original academic production at an international level, including considerable contributions to the development of the academic discipline 	
• Manage research and other management functions, e.g. engage in the university’s external academic activities, as well as knowledge and technology transfer 	
• Provide research-based teaching   The professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Terms of employment 
 The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of five years. Extension is possible if the employed candidate performs well in the position.

  For the professorship the appointee will receive a pensionable annual honorarium of 219.882,33 DKK (1 August 2026 level).

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Questions
 For further information please contact Head of Department Nicolai W. Albrechtsen, nicolai.albrechtsen@regionh.dk.

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application (Including motivations for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD and other relevant certificates) 	
• Uploads of maximum 10 publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Self-declaration form (Template under Nyttige links - Upload the completed and mandatory form as “Other relevant material”) 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines / Template for inspiration under Nyttige links) 	
• Research plan (3‐5 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• A complete list of publications   Application procedure 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee. When the assessment work is completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59 p.m. CET, Sunday, 8 November 2026.

  Interviews for this position are likely to be held in the month of March 2027.

jobs.occupation: ASIYE GROUP ApS søger nye kollegaer: Koordinator/Chauffør & Chauffør (Kørekort B) / ASIYE GROUP ApS is hiring: Coordinator/Driver & Driver (Driver's License B)
jobs.description:

Dine primære opgaver:

Planlægning og koordinering: Daglig ruteplanlægning og opgavestyring for selskabets ansatte chauffører.

Kvalitetssikring i marken: Køre periodisk med chaufførerne for at evaluere, vejlede og sikre vores høje kvalitetsstandarder.

Vores forventninger til dig:

Sprogkundskaber: Du skal kunne kommunikere flydende på tyrkisk og engelsk i både skrift og tale af hensyn til vores interne koordinering og samarbejdspartnere.

• 
Erfaring med logistik, koordinering eller teamledelse (erfaring fra transportbranchen er en stor fordel).

Struktureret, løsningsorienteret og i stand til at bevare overblikket i pressede situationer.

Gyldigt kørekort (B) og erfaring som aktiv, rutineret bilist.

PROFIL 2: Chauffør (Kørekort B)

Vi søger en stabil og serviceminded chauffør, der vil være virksomhedens ansigt udadtil over for vores kunder. Du bliver en vigtig del af vores daglige leveringsteam.

Transport og levering: Sikker og effektiv afvikling af de planlagte ruter i selskabets biler (Kategori B).

Vores forventninger til dig:

• 
Gyldigt kørekort (B) og solid erfaring med kørsel i varebil eller lignende.

• 
Mødestabil, fleksibel og ansvarsfuld omkring dine arbejdstider og opgaver.

• 
Præsentabel, høflig og serviceminded over for kunder og kollegaer.

Hvad tilbyder ASIYE GROUP ApS?

• 
En stabil arbejdsplads med gode, engagerede kollegaer.

• 
Gode og professionelle rammer for udførelsen af dit arbejde.

• 
Mulighed for personlig og faglig udvikling (særligt i koordinatorrollen).

• 
Løn efter kvalifikationer.

Ansøgning og kontakt

Er du vores nye koordinator eller chauffør? Send din ansøgning og dit CV hurtigst muligt til zekeriya-eker@hotmail.com. Marker venligst din ansøgning med enten "Ansøgning: Koordinator" eller "Ansøgning: Chauffør".

Har du spørgsmål til stillingerne, er du velkommen til at kontakte os via ovenstående e-mail, hvorefter vi vil vende tilbage til dig.

jobs.occupation: 2-year Postdoctoral Researcher in Abstractions for Quantum Software
jobs.description:
The Quantum Hub at University of Southern Denmark is seeking a postdoctoral researcher for a two-year post to conduct research on abstractions for quantum software. As quantum computing advances towards large-scale fault-tolerant devices, robust hardware-independent software abstractions are becoming increasingly important for bridging the gap between quantum algorithms and physical implementations, and for making quantum computing accessible to software developers. We welcome applicants strongly motivated to contribute to this growing field with expertise in one or more of the following areas:

* Quantum algorithms

* Quantum circuit synthesis and optimisation

* Gaussian boson sampling

* Topological quantum computing

* Quantum error correction

* Fault-tolerant quantum computing

* Quantum programming languages and programming abstractions, including LLM-assisted quantum programming

* Quantum intermediate representations

* Quantum compilation, including AI/ML-assisted compilation techniques

* Quantum software engineering

* Quantum software design and testing

* Developer tools and usability in quantum software

The targeted starting date of the position is 1 January, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Note: We are not permitted to directly contact your academic references, so please ensure their letters have reached us by the deadline.  The application requirements are detailed at the end of this advertisement.  

Requirements
The candidate must have a PhD degree in mathematics, physics or computer science. 

Situation of the position
The position at the SDU Quantum Hub, will be situated at the Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, Faculty of Science on the international campus in Odense, Denmark. SDU Quantum Hub is established with the ambition to create a highly international and interdisciplinary group within a broad spectrum of quantum research. Odense is a fast-growing international community with an open Scandinavian culture, affordable housing and living costs. 

Assessment
Shortlisting may be used. Shortlisted applicants will be assessed by an assessment committee. Applicants will be informed of their assessment by the faculty. As part of the overall assessment, the applicant may be called for interview.

Conditions of employment
The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. 

Information of salary rates can be found at: https://www.sdu.dk/en/om-sdu/job-sdu/international-staff

For non-Danish candidates there is an optional researcher taxation scheme (see the link above).

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor in Public Health: Children and Young People
jobs.description:
At the National Institute of Public Health (NIPH), University of Southern Denmark (SDU), a position as Associate Professor in Public Health is hereby advertised with a focus on interdisciplinary, qualitative studies of children’s and young people’s health and well-being, commencing on 15 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

About your future research environment  

The National Institute of Public Health (NIPH) is part of the University of Southern Denmark and is located in Copenhagen. As a national public health institute, we conduct research to improve public health in Denmark and Greenland. At the same time, we contribute internationally to the development of knowledge, theories and methods in the field of public health.

We offer an inspiring research environment in the heart of Copenhagen with skilled and dedicated colleagues from diverse research and educational backgrounds. Here, you will have the opportunity for academic exchange and further development of your own research areas, as well as participation in national and international networks. The position is anchored in the research group Health Promotion and Interventions, which conducts research on interventions addressing public health issues and works with methodological and theoretical challenges related to the design and evaluation of intervention and implementation studies. Our research concerns children, young people and families, as well as vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, and takes place in a range of settings, including daycare institutions, primary and lower secondary schools, upper secondary education, the healthcare system, municipal services, supermarkets and local communities.  
You will actively participate in the daily activities of the research group and work closely with other researchers at NIPH.  

The duties include research, teaching and dissemination within the institute’s areas of expertise, including:  
- Children’s and young people’s health, well-being and everyday life
- The significance of digital media for children’s and young people’s lives and health
- Health promotion and implementation research in daycare institutions, schools and upper secondary education
- Interdisciplinary, practice-oriented research and development projects, including process evaluation
- Advanced qualitative methods, including ethnography, interviews, focus groups and child-centred approaches
- Teaching and supervision at bachelor’s and master’s level, including qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and implementation
- Preparation of applications for external funding as well as project management and coordination
- Contributions to the further development of the research environment, including method development and research group activities
 
The following qualifications are highly valued:  
You have established yourself as a qualified researcher within qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and intervention and implementation research, and you possess strong research and teaching qualifications at a high level. You have a relevant publication profile and extensive experience in disseminating research to researchers, practitioners, and other target groups. You have broad collaborative networks and experience in research collaboration with practitioners. As a person, you are dedicated and possess strong communication skills. You are able to build trusting relationships with students, colleagues, and external partners alike. As a teacher, you communicate up-to-date, relevant knowledge in an engaging, clear and understandable way, and as a supervisor you are skilled, inspiring, and supportive.  

Qualifications  
- A PhD degree in Public Health, Education, Sociology, Anthropology or a related field
- Experience with intervention and implementation research
- Documented experience in research on children’s and young people’s health
- A strong profile within qualitative research
- Experience in collaborating with practitioners, exchanging knowledge and disseminating research
- Experience in national and international research collaboration
- Documented teaching experience at university level and experience supervising students (e.g. bachelor’s or master's students)
- Proficiency in Danish and English at a high level, both orally and in writing
- Documented experience with scientific publications within relevant research areas
 

Further information regarding the position can be obtained from:  
Research Leader Susan Andersen,  mailto:suan@sdu.dk

Terms and conditions of employment  
Appointment as an Associate Professor is for a fixed term of three years, commencing on 15 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Appointment to the position will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state with the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for associate professor as described herein. Please check links for more information on salary (only available in Danish) and taxation.

The person employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a self-organiser.

The assessment and evaluation process
Shortlisting may be used in the assessment process. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will receive an assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU. 
Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee and the shortlisted applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicants to provide the necessary material. Interviews and tests may form part of the overall assessment carried out by the appointment committee.  
Based on information from the entire recruitment process, the Head of Institute will decide which applicant is offered the position. 

The application

Applicants are encouraged to read the information "How to apply" before applying. 

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include:

• 
Motivated application

• 
Curriculum vitae

• 
Master’s degree and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (copy of original + verified English translation)

• 
Teaching portfolio

• 
Research plan, including an account of your own research and preferably a vision for future research 

• 
A complete list of publications

• 
Up to six of the most relevant publications. Please attach one PDF file per publication. In cases of co-authorship, a co-author declaration must be submitted as part of the PDF file.

• 
Reference letters/references may also be included

jobs.occupation: Part-time Lecturer in Responsible Business Governance and Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence
jobs.description:
A position as Part-time Lecturer in Responsible Business Governance and Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence is available at the Department of Management, Society and Communication for appointment on 01 January 2027.

As part-time lecturer you will have the opportunity to apply your knowledge to educate young people and to provide them with insight into your practical experience. At CBS, part-time lecturers represent an important supplement to the teaching done by researchers. Your role as part-time lecturer will also provide you with opportunities to update your theoretical knowledge, to share in discussions with engaged students and to be part of an international academic environment.

The position is on a temporary part-time basis, which can be extended within the framework of the Danish Fixed-Term Employment Act (Lov om tidsbegrænset ansættelse).

MSC’s research and teaching addresses the dynamic relations between business and society and the responsible management thereof. To this end, MSC mobilises a wide range of knowledge within management and business disciplines as well as the broader social and human sciences, organized in three interconnected research environments: CBS Sustainability; Centre for Business and Development Studies; the Communication, Organisation and Governance Research Cluster.

The position includes 

• 
Planning and conducting teaching on responsible business governance and corporate responsibility due diligence, with a particular focus on risk management, reporting and finance between sustainability expectations and compliance. The part-time lecturer is expected to have solid knowledge of sustainability (risk-based) due diligence, international governance frameworks on responsible business conduct, EU law and policy on corporate sustainability, demands on companies, social expectations of responsible business conduct, and business uptake, responses and challenges in the interface of management and growing public regulation of responsible business and corporate sustainability.

• 
Online teaching—blended learning

• 
Student supervision

• 
Preparing teaching materials and exam questions

• 
Conducting exams and other evaluations

Qualifications

To fill this position, you have a master’s degree and:

• 
High-level practical experience at a high level, which has not been gained through academic employment with a university, or

• 
Employment in an academic principal position with another university (e.g. as assistant professor/researcher, associate professor/senior researcher, or professor/professor with special responsibilities).

• 
A part-time lecturer who is employed on the merits based on their relevant practical experience must possess in-depth, up-to-date knowledge of the possible applications of the subject/academic discipline. This knowledge is/has been acquired through employment within the subject/academic discipline.

• 
Employment as part-time lecturer presupposes that teaching qualifications are included in the assessment of applicants for an external professor.

Other skills

• 
In addition to having a relevant master’s degree, emphasis is placed on your specialization and professional skills within the content of the respective courses.

• 
Good interpersonal and collaboration skills and the ability to contribute to a good working environment

• 
Teaching is mainly done in English. Proficiency in Danish will be helpful as some supervision opportunities may be in Danish. The conditions of employment and the qualification requirements are described further in the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Terms of employment

Salary and employment will be in accordance with the Cirkulære om aftale om Eksterne lektorer ved universiteter m.fl. under Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet. The maximum number of working hours per academic year is 500 and may vary as needed in individual semesters. Remuneration is based on the number of hours, which is determined twice a year.

When employed as a part-time lecturer you must take an introductory course on university teaching organised by CBS.

You will be assigned a researcher at the department as your professional contact person. You are expected to participate in professional events relevant to your teaching and you will also be part of the department’s network of part-time lecturers.

The recruitment process

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply for the position. An appointment committee will review the applications and invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview.

One of CBS’ strategic goals is the promotion of diversity, which is why every effort has been made to ensure a recruitment process that reduces potential bias. Applicants are therefore encouraged not to include a photo or unnecessary personal information in their application.

Further information

If you would like to know more about the position, please do not hesitate to contact Professor Karin Buhmann, email kbu.msc@cbs.dk.

Your application

To apply, click on the link “Apply online”, fill out the application form and attach the following documentation:

• 
Letter of motivation

• 
CV

• 
Diploma(s)

• 
Teaching Portfolio

• 
Publication list, if relevant for the position

Additional information about CBS and the department is available at www.cbs.dk.

Application due 11/3/2026

jobs.occupation: Research Assistant (Staff Scientist) in Cancer Bioinformatics and Molecular Oncology
jobs.description:
The Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a Research Assistant (Staff Scientist) position in the research group of Professor Paolo Ceppi.

The successful candidate will contribute to ongoing research activities focused on understanding the molecular and metabolic mechanisms underlying cancer development and progression, with a particular emphasis on bioinformatics and computational approaches in oncology.

The position aims to strengthen and further develop bioinformatics research within the group, facilitating the integration of computational analyses with experimental cancer biology and supporting the development of new research directions.

Main Responsibilities

The successful candidate will be expected to:

• 
Conduct independent and collaborative research in cancer biology, with particular attention to metabolic regulation and molecular mechanisms of tumor progression.

• 
Develop and apply bioinformatics and computational approaches for the analysis of complex biological datasets, including transcriptomic and other omics data.

• 
Support the integration of bioinformatics analyses with experimental research activities within the laboratory.

• 
Contribute to identifying molecular pathways and regulatory networks involved in cancer progression and cellular plasticity.

• 
Participate in the preparation of scientific publications, research proposals, and future grant applications.

• 
Contribute to teaching activities at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, including the BMB835 course.

• 
Collaborate with researchers within the department and contribute to the scientific development of the research group.

Qualifications

Applicants should have:

• 
A PhD degree in molecular biology, biochemistry, bioinformatics, cancer biology, or a related field.

• 
Documented postdoctoral research experience in molecular oncology or cancer-related research.

• 
Strong expertise in bioinformatics and computational analysis of biological datasets.

• 
Experience with transcriptomic data analysis and the interpretation of molecular pathways and regulatory networks.

• 
Knowledge of cancer metabolism and molecular mechanisms involved in cancer progression.

• 
A demonstrated ability to conduct research independently and collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary research teams.

• 
A strong scientific publication record.

• 
Good communication skills and an interest in contributing to teaching activities.

Research Environment

The successful candidate will join the research group led by Professor Paolo Ceppi at the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark.

The group investigates molecular mechanisms regulating cancer progression, with particular interests in cancer metabolism, cellular plasticity, and molecular regulatory networks. The position will play an important role in strengthening the computational and bioinformatics capabilities of the laboratory and supporting the development of innovative research projects and future funding applications.

Employment Details

• 
Position: Research Assistant (Staff Scientist)

• 
Workplace: Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, University of Southern Denmark, Odense

• 
Starting date: 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter

• 
Duration: 1 year

• 
Application deadline: 27 October 2026

We are looking for a Finance Manager who will be instrumental in establishing and developing a robust, scalable finance function that enables Quantum Foundry Copenhagen to achieve its strategic ambitions.

Strong culinary expertise with a background in developing seasonal menus, sharing concepts, and modern dining experiences.

Solid grasp of kitchen administration, including staff scheduling, purchasing, stock management, and food cost control.

Staff prices in all chain restaurants and hotels (Strawberry).

Join our High-Performance Development team in Denmark in a role focused on Improving and maintaining our power plant control software solution that is deployed to SGRE wind farms all over the world.

• Ongoing optimisation of graphic workflows, including through the use of AI and new technical tools to strengthen efficiency and quality

• Ad hoc graphical tasks of a smaller nature, e.g. related to the publisher’s social media presence, attendance at book fairs and similar

We therefore envision that you…

• Are an Adobe suite power user and are familiar with other relevant graphic design programs

• Have experience with and an interest in new AI tools, both for use in the graphic work itself and for optimising graphic workflows

• Have a strong eye for composition, aesthetics, typography, contrast, imagery and more

• Are structured and detail-oriented, and thrive when working independently

• Can plan and prioritise your tasks and are able to both set and meet deadlines

• Ideally have at least 1–2 years of experience as a graphic designer

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Senior Business Process consultant - Viby DK
jobs.description:
Would you like to turn complex procurement processes into practical digital solutions that create measurable business value? And are you motivated by working at the intersection of business, process improvement and technology?

“As our new Senior Business Process Consultant, you will connect business needs with digital opportunities within Procurement. You will join our Digital S2C Excellence team, part of Procurement Data and Digital Excellence, where you will work across Procurement, business functions and digital teams to improve the way we work and help translate business requirements into effective processes and solutions”, says Anette Falk Bøgebjerg, Head of Data & Digital Excellence for Procurement.

How you will make an impact

Reporting to the Head of Digital S2C Excellence, you will play an important role in developing and improving Arla's source-to-contract and procure-to-pay processes. Combining process knowledge, data and stakeholder insights, you will identify improvement opportunities, help design solutions and support their implementation across the organisation.

Your key responsibilities will be to

• Facilitate business process improvements and collaborate with stakeholders to define and document clear objectives, requirements and opportunities for improvement.

• Analyse process and performance data to identify trends, challenge existing ways of working and recommend improvements.

• Design process and digital solutions that support business priorities, working closely with Digital Business Consultants and relevant Procurement and business teams.

• Maintain high-quality process documentation, define and monitor performance metrics and ensure alignment with Arla's process framework.

• Support change management, stakeholder training and the successful handover of improved processes to operational teams.

What will make you successful

For this role, we are looking for someone with 2-3 years of Procurement category knowledge and preferably an understanding of Source-to-Pay processes.

You have a Master’s degree in Economics, Supply Chain, or a related field, are interested in how digital solutions and data can enable better ways of working, and you are comfortable turning business requirements and analysis into practical recommendations. LEAN background would be an advantage.

You do not need to know everything from day one. What matters is that you bring solid knowledge about source to contract processes and are motivated to develop your expertise further in a complex, international Procurement environment.

To succeed in the role, you

• Approach complex challenges with curiosity and use data and critical thinking to understand problems and identify practical solutions.

• Build constructive relationships across functions and can communicate requirements and ideas clearly to different stakeholders.

• Take ownership of your work while actively collaborating with others to create improvements that work in practice.

As Arla is an international organisation, professional proficiency in English is required.

What do we offer?

You will become part of Digital S2C Excellence within Procurement Data and Digital Excellence in Aarhus. The team has adopted agile ways of working and you will work in an  environment where business expertise, data and digital capabilities come together to improve the way Procurement operates.

The position offers an opportunity to build your expertise in business process management and digital transformation while working with colleagues across functions and geographies. You will have the opportunity to contribute to meaningful improvements while developing your professional capabilities within a global organisation.

We are committed to professional development and creating a collaborative environment where colleagues share knowledge and support each other in delivering results. You will join a global, farmer-owned dairy cooperative working to create value for our customers, our farmer owners and the wider world.

Would you like to join us?

If you would like to combine your category experience and business process skills with data and digital solutions to help shape the future of Procurement at Arla, we would be pleased to hear from you. Please apply as soon as possible, as we will process applications on a continuous basis and close the recruitment once the right candidate is found.

For additional information about the position, please contact Head of Data & Digital Excellence, Anette Falk Bøgebjerg at anefb@arlafoods.com

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.
