**Team & Role Overview

**We are looking for a systems-minded Senior ML Data Engineer to own the offline-to-online feature infrastructure that powers our real-time recommendation and search engines at scale. You will be building the low-latency data syncs and feature-serving layers that bridge our analytical warehouses with operational databases, caches, and Feature Stores. This is a role for a performance-driven engineer who excels at pipeline orchestration (Airflow, dbt), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Docker), and database tuning, ensuring our recommendation systems receive reliable data under strict low-latency SLAs. If you thrive on solving complex data synchronization challenges, scaling operational storage for millions of users, and acting as the operational bridge between Data Science and Backend Engineering - you will play a critical role in powering our product's core ML capabilities.

**What You'll Do

**

• Offline-to-Online Feature Pipelines: Build and operate resilient feature pipelines syncing transformed data from analytical warehouses (e.g., BigQuery) into operational storage layers (e.g., AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models at scale.

• Pipeline Orchestration and Transformations: Design, test, and maintain robust Apache Airflow DAGs and modular dbt transformations to automate end-to-end data ingestion and feature generation under strict low-latency SLAs.

• Infrastructure as Code and Reliability: Provision, scale, and automate cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and CI/CD pipelines, implementing automated data quality testing and monitoring across all feature syncs.

• Cross-Functional System Design: Partner directly with Data Scientists and Backend Engineers to define online/offline feature contracts, optimize database schemas for sub-second queries, and eliminate training-serving skew for millions of active users.

**What we’re looking for 🌟

****We Imagine That You Have

**

• 4+ years of experience

• Operational Data Pipelines: Proven experience moving batch features from analytical warehouses (BigQuery, Snowflake) into low-latency online stores (AlloyDB, Redis, Feature Stores) to serve real-time ML recommendation models.

• Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Deep hands-on experience provisioning, scaling, and managing cloud data infrastructure using Terraform, Docker, and modern CI/CD automation pipelines.

• Pipeline Orchestration & Transformations: Strong track record building, scheduling, and maintaining workflow orchestrations (e.g., Airflow, Dagster) and modular data transformation frameworks (e.g., dbt).

• Database Performance Tuning: Advanced SQL skills across both OLAP and OLTP systems. Ability to optimize schemas, indexing, partitioning, and queries.

It is further seen as an advantage to have experience with:

• Production Feature Management: Experience managing Feature Stores (e.g., Feast, Tecton) or low-latency key-value stores (e.g., Redis) to serve online ML features with zero training-serving skew.

• Real-Time OLA): Experience with ClickHouse, Pinot, Druid or others for ultra-fast aggregations over live event streams.

• Event Streaming: Hands-on experience with streaming tools like GCP Pub/Sub, Kafka, or Flink for real-time feature updates.

Why GoWish should sit at top of your career wish list 💙

At GoWish, we believe great work comes from people who feel energized, supported, and excited to show up every day. That’s why we’ve built a workplace where celebration, growth, and genuine enjoyment are part of the journey - not perks on the side.

Take your birthday off with Happy Birthday Leave, enjoy 30 days of vacation to fully recharge, and join a team that fills the year with events and playful happenings. We invest in your future with pension and insurance, fuel your days with a weekly lunch scheme, and keep you going with unlimited snacks and sodas - because work should feel good.

At GoWish, you don’t just build great products. You build a great work life.

**We collaborate in a flexible hybrid setup, with most of our magic happening at our bright, modern office in Østerbro - perfectly placed between Nordhavn and Østerport Station. We’re ready for you to join us as soon as you are.

The Senior AI Adoption Lead takes ownership of ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, turning enthusiasm into real, safe, everyday value from the AI tools available to ALK employees. This role continues the adoption efforts from 2025 (over 1,000 employees trained in GenAI usage) and 2026 (more tailored training on ALK's AI solutions) and is key to achieving ALK's AI ambition within the Allergy+ strategy.

This role requires genuine enthusiasm for enabling people, facilitating great learning experiences, and driving change. The Senior AI Adoption Lead must work closely with people across all business areas, be proactive, reach out to employees, and drive AI adoption across the entire organization so that the change is permanent and sticks with employees.

This role owns ALK's continuous AI adoption programme, covering general enablement on GenAI, tailored upskilling for all employees, and engagement activities that drive adoption. This includes preparing and hosting AI training (both general-purpose and tool-specific), the training calendar, micro-learning, maintaining AI at ALK intranet site. The role also owns measuring GenAI usage across the organization, providing the data needed to support informed decisions in AI strategy implementation.

This is not an engineering role – the person does not need to build or configure AI solutions. It does, however, require basic understanding of both business and IT, so the Senior AI Adoption Lead can act as an effective bridge between the two. Genuine enthusiasm for new technologies, especially generative AI, is required. Experience with usage of those technologies in daily life and enterprise scenario is vital.

The Senior AI Adoption Lead acts as a proxy between business and IT: translating technical concepts into everyday business language, aligning business demand with IT delivery, triaging common issues, and accelerating adoption before escalation to IT.

This role is based in Denmark, where ALK has its headquarters and the majority of AI users. It also requires occasional business travel to conduct in-person workshops and training.

Major fields of responsibility:

• 
Communicate the need for AI adoption through meetings, newsletters, MS Teams, and Intranet; share success stories, best practices, and enthusiasm for upcoming initiatives.

• 
Foster engagement through targeted workshops for departments and business units, regular manager briefings, tailored communications, and a visible emphasis on the benefits of AI in daily work.

• 
Map use cases and design training courses (e.g. Foundations, Advanced Prompting, Leading with GenAI) and micro-learning, and activate and coordinate a network of AI Champions to extend reach.

• 
Provide accessible, tiered learning resources through the AI community and Learning Hub (Teams channel, SharePoint) — videos, live webinars, in-person workshops, quick-start guides, FAQs, and playbooks.

• 
Support enterprise-AI pilots with onboarding, enablement and value evaluation; collect feedback and resolve common non-technical issues; and maintain a tight feedback loop with IT on platform updates, governance, and support to keep adoption aligned and safe.

• 
Work side by side with the technical teams (programmers, architects, data and platform specialists): take part in solution and roadmap discussions, learn how the solutions work, ask questions from the end-user perspective, challenge and advise on usability, and translate the outcome into layman terms for the business.

• 
Define and measure adoption rates and satisfaction (usage, surveys, focus groups) and report impact to leadership; run iterative cycles to refine training content based on user feedback and business priorities; and recognize high adopters through awards and acknowledgment.

Qualifications:

• 
Minimum 10 years' experience in change management, IT systems adoption, and training management and delivery

• 
Proven facilitation, training and change-management experience

• 
Outstanding communication and stakeholder skills across all levels

• 
Fluent in English.

• 
Hands-on curiosity about generative AI

• 
Practical experience with creation of AI assistants (e.g. custom skills in Anthropic Claude or custom agents in M365 Copilot).

• 
Analytical mindset able to translate adoption data into actionable insights.

• 
Self-driven, organized and creative, comfortable working across business and IT**.**

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Financial Analyst, you'll own the day-to-day financial planning and analysis (FP&A) across clinical programmes, research and corporate functions. You'll turn financial data and input from colleagues into reliable forecasts, useful insights and clear reporting that helps Hemab make informed decisions.

Working closely with the FP&A Director, you'll take ownership of recurring financial activities while helping build practical ways of working as Hemab grows. Your work will give our teams greater financial clarity and help us make thoughtful decisions about the resources behind our science.

What you'll do

• Own monthly FP&A activities across assigned clinical studies, research projects and functions, keeping forecasts accurate and up to date.

• Partner with functional leads and project teams to understand spending, challenge assumptions and identify financial risks and opportunities early.

• Coordinate quarterly forecasts and contribute to the annual Investment Plan and Long-Range Plan.

• Analyse actuals against forecasts, explain variances and turn financial information into clear, useful insights.

• Prepare management reporting, financial commentary and decision materials for review by the FP&A Director.

• Maintain and improve Power BI reporting, ensuring reliable data and consistent financial information.

• Manage routine financial follow-up with CROs and vendors, including invoice reviews, change orders and financial input to negotiations.

• Build straightforward financial frameworks and reporting practices that help teams work efficiently as Hemab grows.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Experience in FP&A, forecasting, management reporting and financial business partnering.

• Strong financial analysis skills, with the ability to turn complex information into practical recommendations.

• Advanced Excel skills and hands-on experience with Power BI.

• Experience managing forecasts independently, identifying material changes and knowing when to escalate.

• Ability to work effectively with finance and non-finance colleagues, communicate clearly and challenge assumptions constructively.

• Professional fluency in English.

Nice to have

• Experience in biotech, pharma, clinical development, CROs or another project-driven environment.

• Familiarity with clinical study budgets, vendor financial management or financial planning systems.

• Experience improving financial reporting or building ways of working in a growing organisation.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

We value people who take ownership, solve problems, ask for help when needed and work without ego. At our size, how you work matters as much as your CV. Good structure should help people move faster and trust the numbers, not slow them down.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Hemab Therapeutics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

Your role

Your work will cover areas such consolidation including eliminations of P&L, balance sheet, cashflow, investments and KPI´s, securing data quality, development of our consolidation platform along with the master data to secure the foundation for high-quality reporting - giving management a more precise basis for taking decisions.

What you bring:

Head of Compliance – help us build a bank Europe can trust

We are looking for a Head of Compliance who sees regulation as part of how a bank is built, and part of its culture.

As a senior professional you are to become our Head of Compliance and Data Protection Responsible. Someone who knows the craft inside out, and would - if faced with a choice - choose to shape a smarter, leaner and specific compliance function over a more broad based big-bank machine.

As part of our second line of defence, you lead the Compliance function with overall responsibility for identifying, assessing, monitoring, advising on and reporting on compliance and data risks.

This is a rare opportunity to shape the governance and compliance culture of a fast-growing bank at an early stage. You work closely with Executive Management and the Board of Directors, and your judgement directly influences how we grow across Denmark, and the rest of the EU. If you pair deep regulatory expertise with integrity and a commercial mindset, this is a place where you can make a real difference.

What you will be doing

Compliance framework & monitoring

• You run and ensure timely development of our effective compliance framework (incl. Compliance AI) based on the bank’s business model and risk appetite, including the annual compliance risk assessment, the multi-year compliance review plan and the Compliance Procedure.

• You review and monitor the effectiveness of the bank’s methods and procedures across all areas relevant to financial regulation – including financial crime prevention (AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC), credit, DORA, GDPR, solvency and capital (CRR/CRD), PSD2/PSD3 and MiCA.

• You report regularly to Executive Management and the Board of Directors, and escalate significant findings, warnings or concerns when compliance risks or incidents arise.

Regulation & business development

• You monitor new and updated regulation, assess its impact on the bank and advise on implementation together with Legal.

• You take part in our business development process: reviewing new products, assessing new outsourcing and overseeing product governance.

• You take part in meetings with the Danish FSA and other supervisory authorities, and follow up on any remediation.

Data protection

• You take on the role as kompasbank’s Data Protection Responsible: the contact point for data protection authorities and data subjects, handling breach reporting and access requests, and advising on data processing agreements, transfer impact assessments and DPIAs.

Governance & culture

• You own our whistleblower scheme and case handling.

• You advise on the Remuneration Policy and supporting Executive Management on investor relations and equity and debt financing.

• You build a strong risk and compliance culture through training and awareness, and making sure the Compliance function has the resources it needs.

• Working closely with Risk Management to coordinate second-line reviews and risk assessments.

What we expect from you

• Legal background: A law degree (cand.jur., cand.merc.jur. or equivalent) and 10+ years of experience in financial services, with solid experience from a bank, a law firm, a fintech or a supervisory authority.

• Compliance expertise: Proven experience leading or holding a senior role in a compliance function in a regulated financial institution.

• Regulatory knowledge: Strong analytical capability within Danish and EU financial regulation, procedures and products; knowledge of the Danish Financial Business Act and Executive Order on Management and Control of Banks, etc., AML/CTF, DORA and MiCA is a strong plus.

• Data protection: Knowledge of GDPR and data protection practice in a regulated environment; experience from a data protection role is a strong plus.

• Collaboration and communication: You build strong relationships across the bank and explain complex regulation clearly to colleagues, management and regulators.

As Head of Compliance is a key function, the position is subject to a fit & proper assessment by kompasbank and the Danish FSA. You must therefore be able to document sufficient knowledge, experience and a good reputation, and have no criminal record or ongoing insolvency proceedings that could affect your suitability.

What we offer

• A key leadership role with real influence and a direct line to Executive Management and the Board.

• A high-energy, collaborative work culture built on trust, humor, ambition, and innovation.

• Competitive salary, attractive pension scheme, six weeks of paid holiday, and comprehensive health insurance.

• 60+ skilled, ambitious, and friendly colleagues.

• A modern office in beautiful green surroundings in Vedbæk, north of Copenhagen.

• Ongoing learning and development opportunities.

About kompasbank

Europe runs on small and medium-sized businesses. SMEs make up 99% of all EU companies, employ around 100 million people and generate more than half of Europe’s GDP. Yet they are the part of the economy that the financial system serves worst: too complex for automated retail credit, too small to be worth a traditional corporate bank’s attention. The Draghi report on European competitiveness was blunt. Europe is falling behind the US and China in growth, productivity and technology, and fragmented, slow-moving capital is a central reason why. Europe will not become relevant again through a handful of champions alone. It needs thousands of ambitious mid-sized companies that can get financing, move money domestically and internationally, and scale across borders as easily as their American competitors. That is where kompasbank stands. Built on a full EU banking licence, we bank European SMEs properly, with serious service, data excellence and the regulatory rigour that lets us say yes where others say no.

We’re a cloud-native neobank with no legacy systems and no silos. Since opening our doors in August 2021, we’ve grown fast, expanding across Denmark, Germany and Spain, with a growth rate of more than 1,150% and top rankings on the Sifted lists – and we were named Best Bank for SMEs – Denmark 2024 by FDI Insider.

We are looking for a motivated and structured student assistant who wants to learn how crisis readiness is built in practice. You will support both the day-to-day maintenance of our Crisis Management framework and the continued development of the Crisis Management Team. The role combines practical coordination, document and data management, analysis, communication and continuous improvement work.

You will receive clear priorities and guidance, but you will also be trusted to be responsible for defined tasks and follow them through. Your work will contribute directly to making plans easier to use, training more effective, and improvement actions more visible.

Purpose of the role

Your purpose is to help keep our crisis-management setup current, organised and ready for use. You will support documents, exercises, readiness activities, reporting and follow-up, while learning how operational resilience and executive crisis management work in a large infrastructure company.

Key responsibilities

• Maintain and improve crisis plans, appendices, role descriptions, quick guides, checklists and templates.

• Coordinate practical preparation for workshops, activation drills and crisis exercises, including invitations, rooms, Teams setup, materials and participant data.

• Collect and structure data from training, activations and exercises, and prepare clear overviews and PowerPoint material.

• Maintain action and improvement trackers, follow up with owners and prepare concise status updates.

• Support stronger decision logging, situation reporting, briefing flows and role-ready crisis-room materials.

• Carry out desk research on crisis management, operational resilience, emerging risks and best practice.

• Help explore, test and responsibly apply AI to improve crisis preparedness, response, recovery, decision and action logging, situation reporting and post-incident learning.

What you will work on from the start

Recent exercises have identified practical opportunities to make activation faster, clarify interfaces, improve decision and situation reporting. We also want to explore how responsible use of AI can improve crisis preparedness, response, recovery, reporting and continuous learning. You will help turn these lessons into updated tools, training material, trackers and follow-up activities. You will support the work, while decisions and formal ownership remain with the relevant specialists and leaders.

Your first months

During your first months, you will learn the Crisis Management framework, key roles, exercise cycle and improvement backlog. With support from the team, you will gradually take ownership of recurring practical tasks, selected improvement actions and clearly defined deliverables. You will be expected to keep overviews current, flag issues early, and ask for guidance when decisions or sensitive information are involved.

The role is designed to combine learning with real responsibility. You will work close to both operational specialists and senior stakeholders, but you will not make crisis decisions or replace specialist role holders. Your contribution is to make the process, tools, information and follow-up more reliable and easier to use.

jobs.occupation: Research Assistants in the Svejstrup group at Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine
jobs.description:
We are looking for one or two highly motivated research assistants for 4-month period to investigate how a long non-coding RNA (lncRNA) variant of ASCC3 regulates transcriptional recovery following DNA damage, in the Svejstrup lab, DNRF Center of Excellence, Center for Gene Expression (CGEN), Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM), Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Staring date: January 1, 2027

  Previous work from the Svejstrup group identified two gene products of ASCC3 implicated in this response: a protein, encoded by the long mRNA transcript, that suppresses transcription during the late stages of the UV-induced global shutdown; and a short mRNA transcript that acts as a regulatory lncRNA, suppressing the ASCC3 protein's function and enabling transcriptional recovery.

  The project will be focused on understanding how the ASCC3 lncRNA regulates RNAPII-mediated transcription and its recovery after DNA damage, using CRISPR/Cas9 technologies to generate and manipulate ASCC3 transcript variants, combined with state-of-the-art transcription profiling approaches such as TTchem-seq and RNA-seq.

  Information on the Department can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/ 

   

  Our Center and Research
 CGEN is an interdisciplinary research center consisting of 6 research groups located in modern laboratories in the Mærsk Tower at the Panum Institute. Our mission is to use a cutting-edge ensemble of genetic, cell biological, biochemical, organismal, and modern ‘omic’-approaches to achieve a comprehensive understanding of the process of gene expression.

  CGEN performs ground-breaking research in a collaborative and ambitious environment, where young researchers are offered the best conditions to engage in bold and imaginative research. CGEN is also a center of learning, where PhDs and postdocs receive comprehensive insights in the cellular processes underlying gene expression, as well as a clear view of their medical importance and potential for a future research carreer.

  Information on the Svejstrup Group can be found at: https://icmm.ku.dk/english/research-groups/svejstrup-group/

   

  Your job
 The role of the candidate will primarily be to perform experiments in the laboratory, analyse and interpret data, scientific publication, and undertake training, as well as attend scientific seminars.

   

  Profile 
 We are looking for highly motivated and enthusiastic scientists with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• You have a master’s degree in biology, biochemistry, molecular biomedicine or similar 	
• You are highly experienced in mammalian cell culture and molecular biology techniques, including CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing, generation of stable cell lines, and transient transfections 	
• You are highly experienced in working with long, non-coding RNAs and their effect in the DNA damage response 	
• Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams 	
• Excellent English skills written and spoken   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• You have experience with genome-wide sequencing approaches and bioinformatic analysis 	
• Experience with protein-based methods, including immunoprecipitation, western blotting, and microscopy    

  Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine, Panum, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and with access to state-of-the-art facilities for cell engineering, next-generation sequencing, flow cytometry, and mass spectrometry

   

  Scientific environment

  The Department of Cellular and Molecular Medicine (ICMM) offers an ambitious scientific environment, with many different nationalities represented. ICMM aims to produce research with high international impact focusing on the functional cell, its genetic components and molecular cellular mechanisms in a medical context. ICMM currently comprises five research programmes, three high profile Research Centers as well as a number of international research groups. The scientists at ICMM are involved in high quality research based undergraduate and graduate teaching programs at the University of Copenhagen. You can read more at www.icmm.ku.dk

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The positions are fixed-term positions limited to a period of 4 months. While funding is currently secured for the first 4 months, the possibility of extending the position to 11 months is expected to be clarified during the recruitment process.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 34.211,01 DKK/approx. 4.576,89  EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

   

  Questions
 For further information please contact Jesper Svejstrup, jsvejstrup@sund.ku.dk www.sund.ku.dk 

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

  Motivated letter of application (max. one page).

  CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position.

  A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do.

  List of publications.

   

  Deadline for applications:  29 October 2026 at 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

   

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD position in adult clinical psychology/psychotherapy research: Treatments for Complex PTSD
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (UCPH), invites applications for a fully funded 3-year PhD-position from 1 May 2027 or after agreement.  
 
 The position and the project
 The successful candidate will work on the project Treatments for Complex PTSD (RECONNECT-trial), a randomized controlled trial conducted in the Mental Health Services. The project has a strong focus on patient involvement and investigating mechanisms of change within the three intervention arms (Prolonged Exposure, Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing and Enhanced Emotional and Interpersonal Skills Training). The project is conducted in collaboration between researchers in psychology and psychiatry.
 
 Duties and responsibilities
 The PhD student will be central in the research project, being involved in and responsible for large parts of the data collection. Most importantly, the PhD-student will be responsible for conceptualizing and conducting a subset of studies. As such, data management and data analyses, as well as manuscript preparation and communication of research results to the scientific community as well as to relevant stakeholders will be central.

  The PhD-student will be responsible for the assessment of the participants with the International Trauma Interview in Danish, overseeing recruitment progress, and conducting quantitative and qualitative research based on survey and interview data. Experience with quantitative and qualitative data analysis is a must. The candidate must have strong clinical skills and preferably with trauma populations. The candidate must be able to work independently under supervision. Collaborative skills and team spirit are in high regard. For the right candidate, there will be ample possibilities to influence the project and develop new project ideas within the project frame.
 
 Supervision and research group
 The PhD-student will be part of a research group at the Department of Psychology conducting psychological and psychiatric research on psychotherapy and trauma.
 
 Qualification requirements
 Applicants must have qualifications corresponding to master’s level related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Psychology. If you have completed your education in Denmark, you must have a master’s degree covered by the collective agreement for academics in the state sector.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, you must either have a master’s degree equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (two years) or as minimum a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree (three years) and be assessed as having professional qualifications at master's level.

  If you have completed your education outside of Denmark, we may obtain an assessment of your education from the Danish Research Agency.
 
 Place of employment
 The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Social Sciences, University of Copenhagen (https://psychology.ku.dk/) is a vibrant, inclusive workplace hosting a large group of faculty, post docs and PhD-students. The research of the department covers a wide range of topics and methodologies and has an international work environment.

  Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

   	
• Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change. 	
• Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competence to change society for the better. 	
• Energizing global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact   For more on the faculty strategy, see: https://socialsciences.ku.dk/.
 
 The recruitment process
 Further information on the recruitment process at University of Copenhagen can be found here:  https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. For more on the diverse working place environment at the University and the University’s participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, see https://employment.ku.dk/working-at-ucph/eu-charter-for-researchers/
 
 International applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about these services as well as information on entering and working in Denmark here: https://ism.ku.dk/
 
 Contact information
 We encourage you to first consult our website, where most questions concerning the recruitment process as well as the academic content and structure of the PhD programme are answered:

  Structure of the PhD programme

  How to obtain a PhD scholarship.

  For information about the project and the position, please contact PI Assistant Professor Sara Kerstine Kaya Nielsen, sara.nielsen@psy.ku.dk. Information about the recruitment process is available from HR, e-mail: HR-SOENDRE@adm.ku.dk Please refer to ID number: 211-2569/26-2H
 
 How to apply
 Submit a complete application at our online portal. Click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of the page to apply. The documents must be in Adobe PDF or Word.  

  Your application must be written in English and include the following documents:

   	
• Motivated application 	
• Curriculum vitae 	
• Diploma (master and bachelor) 	
• Other relevant material   
 The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026.
 Applications or enclosures received thereafter will not be considered.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in environmental microbial ecology
jobs.description:
The Department of Biology, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a two-year, fixed-term postdoctoral position in environmental microbial ecology, starting 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is part of a project funded by the Villum Foundation's Villum Experiment programme.

The project
Electrically conductive iron minerals are widespread in anoxic aquatic sediments, yet we know little about the microorganisms that live on them. The project aims to characterize the phylogenetic identity and ecophysiology of microorganisms associated with these minerals. We hypothesize that, by facilitating extracellular electron transfer, the minerals provide a distinct niche that selectively enriches electroactive microorganisms relative to the surrounding sediment.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two–year position from 1 February, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 
This is a fixed-term position to end on 31 January, 2029.

Job description
You will identify, visualize and characterize bacterial and archaeal cells associated with iron minerals by combining fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) and correlative imaging, DNA- and/or RNA-based omics, and stable isotope incubation experiments. You will have considerable freedom to shape the methodological approach and to develop your own ideas within the project framework. Project collaborators in Germany will contribute chemical characterization of the minerals, giving you the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary team. Participation in supervision of BSc., MSc. and PhD students and possibly some classroom teaching is also expected.

Your profile
You hold a PhD in biology, earth and environmental science, biotechnology or a related field (or expect to complete it before the start date), and you have a research background in microbiology or microbial ecology.

Essentials:

• Experience with advanced microscopy and/or molecular microbial ecology methods.
• Interest in microbial physiology and electromicrobiology.
• A systematic approach to method development and testing.
• A publication record in international peer-reviewed journals, relative to your career stage.
• Very good written and oral communication skills in English.
Desirable:

• Experience with FISH, correlative microscopy, stable isotope probing, or omics data analysis.
• Experience working with sediment or other environmental samples.
• Experience with microbial physiology and/or electromicrobiology.
• If you are excited about the project but your experience does not match every point, we still encourage you to apply.
At the Department of Biology, we value a collegial and inclusive working environment and place strong emphasis on good relationships among colleagues and students. We welcome colleagues who bring an open, constructive and collaborative approach.

Who we are
The Department of Biology (Aarhus University) provides a framework for research and teaching in all major biological subdisciplines. The department currently encompasses approximately 200 academic and technical staff and 45 PhD students while 400 students follow the BSc and MSc programs offered by the department. The Section for Microbiology (https://bio.au.dk/en/about-biology/sections/microbiology) employs 12 associate and full professors and offers a vibrant, international research environment for studying microbial physiology, evolution, ecology, and biogeochemistry. The section integrates basic and applied research, addressing the functions, eco-physiology, and evolution of microorganisms in natural and biotechnological systems. The section has well-equipped laboratories, a permanent support staff of highly skilled laboratory technicians, and access to advanced imaging facilities on the AU campus.

What we offer
• A two-year position in a stimulating, international research environment
• Access to state-of-the-art laboratories and imaging facilities.
• A work environment encouraging lively, open and critical discussion.
• A work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities.
• A workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Aarhus University, and the place of employment is Section for Microbiology within the Department of Biology (https://bio.au.dk/en/), Aarhus University, Ny Munkegade 114, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contact information
Applicants seeking further information are invited to contact Assoc. Prof. Kasper Urup Kjeldsen at AU (kasperuk@bio.au.dk).

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 29 November, 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. _**Join Pandora’s Global Strategy & Business Development Team as Senior Consultant, Strategy Delivery Office

**_Do you enjoy seeing the bigger picture, finding the signal in complexity and turning insight into action? Do you want to work at the heart of Pandora’s strategic agenda and help senior leaders understand where our most important initiatives are progressing, where they are connected and where attention is needed? Join us at Pandora’s Global Office in Copenhagen and help create the portfolio intelligence and organisational momentum that turn strategy into sustained business impact.

**About The Team

**Pandora’s Strategy Delivery Office is part of our Global Strategy & Business Development team, which reports directly to Pandora’s CEO. We connect Pandora’s ambition, portfolio choices and organisational mobilisation to create confidence that our most important initiatives are focused on the right outcomes, progressing with sufficient pace and realising the value behind our strategy. We partner closely with senior leaders across functions and markets to strengthen delivery and resolve risks and dependencies that cut across the organisation. We combine a collaborative spirit with sharp problem-solving skills and offer a supportive and fun team environment.

**What You’ll Do

**As (Senior) Consultant, Strategy Delivery Office, you will create an integrated view of Pandora’s strategic initiative portfolio, turning complex information into insights and recommendations that help leaders understand progress, anticipate issues and make better decisions.

**Your Key Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Create portfolio insight: Bring together delivery, value and adoption information from across strategic initiatives to provide a clear and integrated view of portfolio health.

• Identify what matters: Analyse patterns, trends and connections across the portfolio, highlighting emerging risks, dependencies, value gaps and opportunities that require attention.

• Turn insight into leadership action: Translate complex portfolio information into clear narratives, recommendations and executive materials that enable focused discussions and decisions.

• Connect strategy and execution: Trace how initiatives contribute to Pandora’s strategic ambition. Help ensure that portfolio reporting remains focused on outcomes and impact and links to Pandora’s growth model.

• Drive the portfolio rhythm: Coordinate the preparation and follow-through of portfolio reviews and decision forums, ensuring that the right questions, evidence and stakeholders come together at the right time.

• Strengthen portfolio transparency: Establish a consistent and reliable foundation for understanding initiative progress, value realisation and adoption readiness across the organisation.

• Improve the strategy-to-execution system: Identify opportunities to simplify portfolio processes, strengthen common practices and use technology and artificial intelligence to improve the quality and efficiency of the SDO’s work.

**Who We Are Looking For

**We are looking for a structured and curious problem-solver who can connect detail with the wider strategic picture and turn complex information into clear, commercially relevant insights that drive real business outcomes.

**To Succeed In This Role, You Ideally Bring

**

• 3-5 years of experience in strategy, transformation, portfolio management, business analysis, top-tier consulting or a comparable role.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to connect information from multiple sources and identify the implications for the wider business.

• Experience in creating executive-level insights and materials, including constructively testing evidence and turning complex information into clear narratives, recommendations and decisions.

• Strong orchestration skills, with the ability to bring together inputs, evidence and decision requirements across initiatives and functions.

• A commercial mindset and an interest in how strategic choices translate into customer, operational and financial impact.

• Strong capability in data analysis and visualisation, supported by an interest in using digital tools and artificial intelligence to improve decision-making and ways of working.

• Fluency in English. Additional languages relevant to Pandora’s key markets are an advantage.

• A master’s degree in business, strategy, finance, economics or a related field.

• Experience in retail, consumer goods or omnichannel environments is an advantage.

Did we get your attention?   If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake  You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

jobs.occupation: Group Vice President, Portfolio Strategy, Insights & Access
jobs.description:
Department: Portfolio Strategy, Insights & Access (PSIA), Product & Portfolio Strategy

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark – global scope

Your impact begins here

As GVP, Portfolio Strategy, Insights & Access, you will lead the team that shapes where Novo invests across its portfolio. You will turn market, customer, competitor and access insights into clear recommendations for Executive Management, guiding choices on pipeline, lifecycle management, launches and business development. Working from Denmark with a global scope, you will make sure every portfolio decision balances patient impact, access feasibility and financial value, so the right treatments reach the people who need them.

What you’ll bring

This is a senior leadership role for someone who combines strategic depth with the confidence to guide decisions at the highest level. You will bring:

• An advanced degree, such as an MBA, MSc, PhD, PharmD or MD, or a degree in Economics, Public Health or an equivalent field.

• 15–20+ years of experience in strategy, consulting, pharmaceuticals, market access, forecasting, commercial excellence or portfolio management.

• Experience presenting to executive leadership and governance boards, with strong executive-ready storytelling for decision forums.

• Proven people leadership and stakeholder management experience, including leading large, diverse, cross-functional teams.

• Strong strategic, commercial and analytical capabilities – you are data-driven and able to make decisions under uncertainty.

• A proven ability to balance patient impact, access considerations and financial outcomes.

• The confidence to challenge and influence C-suite and SVP-level stakeholders.

Useful, but not essential:

Experience developing innovative payment models or working with access partners, such as telehealth providers.

What you’ll do

You will lead the strategic engine behind Novo’s portfolio decisions – connecting strategy, evidence, forecasting and access into recommendations that senior leaders can act on.

• Define and drive long-term portfolio strategies across therapy areas, assessing pipeline, lifecycle management and business development opportunities.

• Lead strategic evaluations of portfolio investments and prioritisation and bring clear recommendations to Executive Management and governance committees, such as the Portfolio Committee.

• Translate market, customer (healthcare professionals, patients and consumers), competitor and healthcare system insights into actionable direction, supported by ongoing competitive intelligence and horizon scanning.

• Shape long-range forecast assumptions, scenario planning and business cases for pipeline assets, launches and strategic investments to support resource allocation.

• Integrate payer, reimbursement and health technology assessment (HTA) considerations into portfolio decisions and make sure access strategies are reflected in development and commercialisation plans.

• Raise the quality and speed of decision support by improving scenario planning methods, competitive assessment approaches and shared decision frameworks.

• Provide strategic leadership across NPP, Early Pipeline & Exploratory, helping shape the future portfolio and translate early opportunities into clear strategic choices. You will work closely with R&D and other key functions to bring patient, market and commercial perspectives into early asset and indication strategies, while driving senior-level alignment on portfolio priorities and investment decisions.

Who you’ll work with

You will lead Portfolio Strategy, Insights & Access, a team of around 140 colleagues, through four direct reports, and report to the Executive Vice President of Product & Portfolio Strategy. In Product & Portfolio Strategy, colleagues connect commercial strategy, medical affairs and business development across therapy areas, helping guide the Novo portfolio and strengthen competitiveness.

You will partner with Executive Management and governance committees, Commercial, Medical, Development, Finance and Operations leadership, global and affiliate Market Access teams, and Corporate Strategy, Business Development and Portfolio Management. You will also work with regional leadership teams to align assumptions, access strategy and launch planning.

Externally, you will engage health economics and market access advisors, HTA bodies, payers and insurers, industry consortia, academic experts and channel partners. Across all these relationships, your role is to create clarity, build alignment without direct authority and keep decisions moving at pace.

What you can expect here

You will hold a position where your voice directly shapes decisions on investment, prioritisation and commercialisation across therapy areas. You will be trusted to own the recommendations you bring, to challenge with honest, evidence-based perspectives and, once a decision is made, to commit and move forward together.

You will lead a large, multidisciplinary organisation and build new skills through work that spans the value chain – from development and access to launch and lifecycle management. You will help set the standard for strategic analytics, forecasting and business case development across Novo.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead the decisions that shape Novo’s portfolio and help more people live healthier lives, apply for the GVP, Portfolio Strategy, Insights & Access role by 28 October 2026

**

Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

**

We are looking for a Senior Cost Manager to enhance our cost management capabilities within the Client Consultancy team. **Join Denmark’s Largest Client Advisory Environment

Reporting directly to the Head of Discipline, your primary focus will be project-based, collaborating closely with project teams, clients, and partners. **A place to work and so much more

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

**Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to our Head of Discipline for Project Management Office, Jesper Ege Krog at jeee@cowi.com.

**Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key.

We aim to create a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

Senior Vice President, Corporate Strategy & Business Development

Job title: Senior Vice President, Corporate Strategy & Business Development

Reporting to: Chief Executive Officer

Department: Corporate Strategy & Business Development

Location: Bagsværd, Denmark. Some travel is expected.

The position

Novo Nordisk is seeking a Senior Vice President to lead Corporate Strategy & Business Development, a newly established organisation that brings together two critical capabilities shaping the company's long-term strategic direction and growth.

Reporting directly to the CEO and serving as a member of Executive Management, you will hold an enterprise-wide mandate to shape corporate strategy, inform strategic choices, and identify and execute external opportunities that strengthen Novo Nordisk's future position.

The role requires a senior executive who combines strategic perspective, deep business understanding and sound judgement with the ability to translate strategic priorities into decisions, partnerships and transactions that deliver long-term value.

Key responsibilities

As Senior Vice President, Corporate Strategy & Business Development, you will lead a global organisation of approximately 60 employees across Corporate Strategy and Business Development. You will work closely with the CEO, Executive Management and senior leaders across Novo Nordisk.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead the development and regular review of Novo Nordisk's corporate strategy in close collaboration with the CEO and Executive Management.

• Shape strategic choices on where to compete, how to win and which capabilities to build to support the company's long-term ambitions.

• Lead the full business development value chain, including opportunity identification, due diligence, valuation, transaction execution, contracting, post-deal integration and alliance management.

• Connect internal capabilities and portfolio priorities with external opportunities, including strategic partnerships, collaborations and acquisitions.

• Ensure rigorous strategic and financial assessment, effective governance and clear accountability for value creation across business development activities.

• Build trusted relationships with key internal and external stakeholders and represent Novo Nordisk in strategic partnerships and transactions.

• Lead and develop a high-performing global organisation across Corporate Strategy and Business Development, fostering collaboration and strong leadership.

Your experience and leadership profile

We are seeking an accomplished senior executive with a demonstrated ability to shape enterprise strategy, lead complex business development activities and influence decision-making at the highest organisational levels.

The successful candidate will bring:

• Substantial senior leadership experience in corporate strategy, business development or related disciplines, gained within the pharmaceutical or life sciences industry, investment banking, management consulting or a comparable global environment.

• A strong track record of shaping enterprise strategy and leading complex strategic partnerships, transactions or acquisitions.

• Broad scientific and commercial understanding, combined with strong financial acumen and the ability to assess strategic opportunities and risks.

• The credibility and judgement to advise and constructively challenge the CEO and Executive Management, and to build alignment among senior leaders across a complex global organisation.

• Demonstrated people leadership, with the ability to develop strong leadership teams and build diverse, inclusive and high-performing organisations.

• Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills, together with the integrity and external credibility required to represent Novo Nordisk in significant partnerships and transactions.

You are a collaborative and decisive leader who combines long-term strategic thinking with the ability to deliver results. You exercise sound judgement in complex situations, challenge established thinking when necessary and build trust across different perspectives and interests.

Application and further information

jobs.description:
The Department of Chemistry invites applicants for a 2-year postdoc position within Theoretical Catalysis under the ERC-SyG DEMI, starting from 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

  DEMI (Directed Evolution of Metastable Electrocatalyst Interfaces for Energy Conversion) is an ERC Synergy Grant funded by the European Research Council Executive Agency.

  In the Theoretical Catalysis group, we aim to provide a deeper understanding of catalytic processes and catalytic materials by atomic scale simulations. We have a special interest in electrocatalytic reactions and high entropy materials, and the methods include DFT-simulations, machine learning potentials, Monte Carlo simulations and statistical analysis. We enjoy a close collaboration with experimental groups, both at the department and other universities in Denmark and abroad. The DEMI project is a collaboration with research groups from University of Bern, Ruhr University Bochum and Helmholtz-Institute Erlangen-Nürnberg.

  The Theoretical Catalysis group is part of Center for High Entropy Alloy Catalysis.

  The successful candidate holds a Ph.D. in computational chemistry, DFT-simulations, physical modelling or a similar background. Experience with theoretical catalysis or electrocatalysis is a benefit.

  The postdoc’s duty is primarily research within Theoretical Catalysis but may include performance of other duties.

jobs.occupation: Consultancy in Otorhinolaryngology, head and neck surgery combined with a clinical professorship in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology
jobs.description:
A clinical position as consultant of Otorhinolaryngology at the Department of ORL, Head and neck surgery and audiology at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet is open for appointment from as soon as possible.

The position is combined with a 5-year externally funded position as clinical professor in Otorhinolaryngology and Head and Neck Oncology at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

It is a requirement that the applicant is accepted for appointment of both the professorship and the consultancy.

The advertisement for the professorship is available from the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

About the department

The Department of Otorhinolaryngology and Audiology is responsible for the full spectrum of diagnostics and treatment within the ENT and audiological fields, encompassing both general patient care and highly specialized services. A total of more than 100 clinically active physicians is employed within the department. In addition, there is a high level of research activity, including among the clinical staff. The department currently has five formally affiliated professors, three of whom are clinical professors in otorhinolaryngology. As a university hospital department, it also has teaching obligations at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels, including for healthcare professionals beyond the medical field of both the primary and secondary health sector.

Clinical functions and focus areas of the department

The consultant position in head and neck surgery requires a strong interest and proven surgical expertise within malignant head and neck surgery. The ideal candidate will demonstrate solid experience in teaching and research, including involvement in undergraduate and postgraduate education, as well as supervision of PhD students. Emphasis is placed on candidates with a robust, long-standing, and continuous research background. The candidate is expected to have extensive knowledge and research experience with head and neck cancer epidemiology and documented experience with national registries and particularly with HPV-driven head and neck cancer. A broad knowledge of benign ENT conditions is also expected. Further the candidate should be active and involved in thyroid cancer research.

The position offers significant opportunities for further specialization and skill development within advanced surgical techniques, including the potential for training in robotic surgery. The consultant will also be expected to take on administrative responsibilities such as patient triage and task coordination.

As the department provides highly specialized ENT services at a university level, applicants must have documented surgical experience and a demonstrated research interest.

Applicants must submit documentation of board certification in Otorhinolaryngology. According to the regulations of the Capital Region of Denmark, applicants must have held a specialist certification for at least five years to be appointed as a consultant at Rigshospitalet, unless an exemption is granted. Furthermore, applicants must provide evidence of clinical experience within head and neck surgery, as well as documentation of scientific and educational activities.

Strong collaboration skills are essential, including the ability to work professionally and constructively in interdisciplinary teams.

Organizationally, the consultant will report to the Head of Department. For professional matters related specifically to head and neck surgery, reference will be made to the lead consultant in that subspecialty.

We offer a dynamic and rewarding position in a busy and active department housed in brand-new, state-of-the-art facilities. The position includes excellent opportunities for involvement in research and clinical development.

Work Schedule: The position includes on-call duty (approximately every 14 days), shared equally among the department’s consultants.

Salary and terms of employment will follow the applicable collective agreement.

Please note: The position is subject to regulations requiring a child protection certificate ("børneattest"). Employment is contingent upon the ability to present a clean certificate.

Research and teaching

With the establishment of the new position as Consultant in Otorhinolaryngology and Clinical Professor in Oto-rhino-laryngology with special focus on Head & Neck Surgery, the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery and Audiology seek to significantly strengthen leadership and strategic development within clinical research and teaching. The professorship is conceived as a pivotal academic and clinical role that will unify and advance research activities across the specialty, with a particular emphasis on translational and interdisciplinary head and neck research.

The position will serve as an academic anchor not only for Rigshospitalet but also for Nordsjællands Hospital and, more broadly, for Region Østdanmark (RØST), with the explicit ambition of fostering coordinated research efforts across Eastern Denmark. The clinical professor is expected to provide academic leadership, facilitate collaboration between hospital departments and regional research environments, and contribute to the development of shared research strategies and priorities across institutions.

In research, the position entails responsibility for initiating, leading, and consolidating high-quality clinical and translational research programmes within head and neck surgery and related disciplines. This includes strengthening existing research groups, promoting multicentre and cross-regional studies, supporting early-career researchers, and ensuring integration of research activities across hospitals within RØST. The professor will play a key role in attracting external funding, enhancing national and international visibility, and embedding research as a core component of clinical practice throughout Eastern Denmark.

In teaching, the position carries responsibility for academic leadership in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing medical education within otorhinolaryngology and head and neck surgery. The professor will contribute to curriculum development, pedagogical innovation, and supervision at all levels, ensuring alignment between clinical training, academic standards, and regional workforce needs. Teaching activities will be coordinated across clinical sites, thereby supporting a unified and high-quality educational environment for medical students, residents, and fellows within RØST.

Overall, the position is designed to function as a unifying professorship that integrates research, teaching, and clinical excellence across Nordsjællands Hospital, the wider hospital network in RØST, and academic partners, thereby strengthening the academic foundation and future development of the specialty across Eastern Denmark.

Qualifications

Applicants must be board-certified specialist in Oto-rhino-laryngology.

Conditions

In order to be considered, the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the professorship) and to the hospital (the consultancy) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the professorship. Appointment is conditioned by the fact that the applicant obtains both positions. This also applies to the applicants who are already employed as consultants at Copenhagen University Hospital - Rigshospitalet.

Salary and Employment Conditions

The position is subject to the Collective Agreement for Specialist Doctors and Consultant Physicians (Overlæger) and the applicable Working Time Agreement between the Danish Regions and the relevant medical professional organization.

Detailed information on employment conditions, collective agreements, and salary levels can be found here:

• Collective Agreement: https://laeger.dk/foreninger/overlaegeforeningen/ok26-overlaegeforeningen

• Collective Agreement (PDF): https://laeger.dk/media/15odzzl1/overenskomst-for-speciallaeger-og-overlaeger-2026.pdf

• Salary information: https://www.regionh.dk/om-region-hovedstaden/fakta/arbejdsplads/sider/startloen.aspx

As clinical professor at least 50 % of the working time will be allocated to academic tasks (e.g., research, teaching, evaluation tasks and communication with the public) in agreement with the Head of Department of Department of Clinical Medicine at the University of Copenhagen. The remaining time will be allocated for clinical work in agreement with the head of Department of ORL, Head and neck surgery and audiology, Rigshospitalet. Additional support and details on the working conditions must be negotiated with the head of the Department of ORL, Head and neck sugery and audiology,Rigshospitalet.

Application procedure

The application must include the following:

• 
Curriculum Vitae and a complete list of publications

• 
Copy of the authorization certificate for specialist in Otorhinolaryngology.

• 
A description of how the applicant is qualified as

• 
Clinical expert

• 
Communicator

• 
Collaborator

• 
Manager/administrator/organizer

• 
Health advocate

• 
Scholar/researcher/teacher

• 
Professional

For more information, please refer to Sundhedsstyrelsen: The Seven Roles of Physicians.

The closing date for applications is 8. November 2026.

Further information

For further information please contact Head of Department Mads Klokker tel. + 45 3545 6033, or email: mads.klokker@regionh.dk
