• Proactively help control risk and compliance and lead by example.

Do you have what it takes?

We need a new colleague, who takes ownership as an individual, but also one who teams up. You need to be curious about learning new technology, and we need a person who is not afraid of challenging status quo or taking personal initiative to help us drive superior solutions for the benefit of the Bank and its customers.

We would like to see the following core skills:

• Have some experience of installing, maintaining, and supporting database systems and related software products.

• Feel comfortable working with critical data on several platforms.

• Strong analytical mind and a determination to help drive/facilitate complex problems to resolution.

• Experience with design, configuration, and support of systems in an environment running mission critical 24*7*365 workload.

• Experience working with Public Cloud.

• Have an open mind and an inherent curiosity that can be a constant drive in your professional development.

Additional Preferred Skills

• Degree related to Computer Science or IT

• Equivalent education with required experience

What can we offer?

We are a leading technology team with a global international and modern scene. We have global colleagues and workdays can easily be a flexible mix of physical and virtual presence. We will offer you many opportunities to grow your career and develop your competencies. We have inspirational leaders, who will support you to succeed, and we offer you great flexibility and autonomy.

Interested?

Does this sound like you? Then we look forward to hearing from you. We screen the applications on an ongoing basis, and we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. For questions, please contact Jesper Hollitsch Poulsen on JHP@danskebank.dk.

Kassow Robots is a Danish company that develops and manufactures unique 7-axis collaborative robots for a wide range of industrial applications. Since 2022, we have been part of Bosch Rexroth, a leading global automation company within the Bosch Group.

Are you passionate about cutting-edge technology and hands-on problem solving? In our Assembly and Repair Department, you will take on an important role, working with colleagues to assemble, repair, and improve complete robot systems.

At our young technology company, you will join a diverse and dedicated team of passionate colleagues who make a real difference every day. You’ll experience a dynamic work environment where collaboration, innovation, and quality are at the heart of everything we do.

Your Primary Responsibilities

• Inspect, analyze, and troubleshoot robotic systems and equipment

• Read repair manuals and collaborate with engineers and other specialists

• Run tests, interpret results, and provide effective recommendations

• Write reports, safety regulations, and preventative maintenance plans

• Source and replace faulty parts and components

• Perform both mechanical and electrical assembly of robot systems

• Support manufacturing and development engineers in ongoing projects

• Handle service requests via our support system

• Stay up to date with advancements in the field and attend workshops as needed

What We’re Looking For

• Practical experience with installation, repair, and troubleshooting of complex systems, ideally including electronics and cabling

• Strong problem-solving skills and ability to learn quickly

• A quality-conscious, systematic, and hands-on approach to work

• Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and thrive in a dynamic environment

• Excellent team player with strong communication skills

• A customer-oriented mindset with a focus on delivering reliable solutions

What We Offer

• Comprehensive training in our robot systems and installations

• A collaborative and innovative work environment in a growing tech company

• Opportunity to work with state-of-the-art robotics

• Personal and professional development through workshops and knowledge sharing

• A role where your contributions directly impact the company’s success

📍 Workplace: All work takes place at our company headquarters in Kastrup.

Shape the future of education technology

At IST, we're building the cloud platform that powers educational solutions used by more than five million users across Europe. Unlike most cloud teams, we run our own cloud — on our own hardware, in our own data center. That means the abstraction stops with us: when a node misbehaves, there's no support ticket to a hyperscaler.

There's a rack, and someone who knows it.

We're looking for a Cloud Engineer who finds that appealing rather than daunting.

About the role

As a Cloud Engineer, you'll help design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform — from the automation and orchestration layers our developers build on, all the way down to the switches, servers and cabling that carry it. You'll do this together with our Cloud Engineering team, architects, developers and stakeholders, whether the work happens at a keyboard or in a rack.

In practice, around a quarter of your time will be spent physically on site in the data center. Not as a separate duty, but as a natural part of the work: expanding capacity for a new cluster the team has just automated, replacing a switch that's been throwing errors in your own monitoring, tracing a network issue that turns out to be a cable rather than a config. Owning the platform end to end is what makes this role different from a pure cloud position.

The role is based at our office in Roskilde, Denmark, with the primary data center within reach. Some travel is required, primarily to our office in Växjö, Sweden.

Key responsibilities

• Design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform across the full stack — from physical hardware to the self-service tooling our developers use

• Automate VMs, containers, storage and networking using Ansible, Terraform, Puppet and PowerShell DSC

• Plan and carry out capacity expansions: from sizing and procurement to racking, cabling, provisioning and putting the capacity into production

• Diagnose and resolve issues wherever they originate — including replacing switches, disks and other failed components on site, and handling firmware, BIOS and driver lifecycle across the fleet

• Support reliable, scalable developer platforms, CI/CD pipelines, orchestration and self-service tools

• Manage databases, object storage and monitoring/logging stacks, with observability that spans both the platform and the hardware underneath it

• Contribute to access, identity and compliance work in line with ISO, PCI and internal policies, including physical access and site security

• Ensure robust backup and disaster recovery plans are in place, tested against real hardware failure scenarios

• Coordinate with hardware vendors and support partners (Dell, Cisco and similar) on spare parts, RMAs and escalations

Your profile

You have a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, network engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, along with solid experience in cloud engineering, infrastructure automation and DevOps practices.

Just as importantly, you're comfortable at both ends of the stack. You can discuss platform architecture with our developers in the morning and spend the afternoon in the rack with a screwdriver, and you see those as the same job rather than two different ones. Working in a data center environment — noisy, cold, occasionally at short notice — is something you take in stride.

We also look for:

• Hands-on experience with server, storage and network hardware — Cisco, Dell, KVM, VMware or similar

• Practical understanding of data center fundamentals: power, cooling, rack design, structured cabling

• Strong knowledge of security, compliance and governance in cloud environments

• Strategic thinking and the ability to translate business needs into technical solutions

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English

• A collaborative, decisive and pragmatic approach to problem-solving

• A valid driver's license and the ability to reach the data center when needed

What we offer

This is a full-time, permanent position. We apply an office-first policy, and given the hands-on nature of this role, regular physical presence at the office and in the datacenter is part of the job. Within that framework, there's room for flexibility on the days where your work doesn't require you on site.

You'll join an international and collaborative environment where you'll have real ownership, influence over strategic technology decisions, and the chance to help shape the future of learning.

Apply

Applications are reviewed continuously. For questions, contact Bengt Welin bengt.welin@ist.com or HR@ist.com. Please note that a background check is part of the recruitment process.

Welcome to apply!

jobs.occupation: Special Consultant for HealthTech Innovation and Venture Development – DTU Entrepreneurship
jobs.description:
DTU is strengthening its collaboration with Rigshospitalet in the Technical University Hospital (TUH). We aim to create a coherent innovation pathway from identification of unmet clinical needs through exploration, prototyping and validation to startup formation and commercialisation.

DTU Entrepreneurship is looking for an experienced Special Consultant to coordinate and further develop this HealthTech innovation pipeline.

You will work at the intersection of technology, healthcare, education, entrepreneurship and commercialisation. A central part of the role will be to connect existing DTU and hospital activities into a functioning pathway. We will ensure that promising HealthTech opportunities can progress between educational programmes, clinical environments, prototyping activities and venture development.

You will collaborate closely with DTU Entrepreneurship, TUH, Rigshospitalet, DTU Skylab and TUH Skylab, relevant DTU departments, clinicians, course responsibles, students and external ecosystem partners.

The job
You will coordinate DTU Entrepreneurship's contribution to the TUH HealthTech innovation initiative. Further contribute hands-on to the development and maturation of selected HealthTech opportunities.

Your primary tasks will include:

• Coordinating the HealthTech innovation initiative across DTU, hospitals and other key stakeholders.
• Developing and maintaining a HealthTech innovation pipeline from clinical need identification to venture creation.
• Supporting the identification and prioritisation of unmet clinical needs in collaboration with clinicians and other experts.
• Providing business development and commercialisation support to selected HealthTech projects, including market assessment, business models, partnerships and funding.
• Mentoring multidisciplinary student teams and potential founders through teaching, coaching and venture development activities.
• Engaging relevant external stakeholders and contributing to the continued development of DTU's HealthTech innovation ecosystem.
You will have a high degree of independence in planning and executing activities while working closely with the TUH leadership and key stakeholders.

We are looking for a senior profile with strong experience in HealthTech innovation, entrepreneurship and commercialisation.

We expect that you have:

• An MSc degree in engineering, technology or a related scientific discipline.
• Proven experience in developing and commercialising healthcare technologies from early-stage innovation to venture creation or market implementation.
• Experience working across the healthcare, university and startup ecosystems.
• Strong business development and commercialisation skills, including market assessment, business model development and stakeholder engagement.
• Experience leading complex projects involving multiple stakeholders.
• Excellent communication, collaboration and facilitation skills.
• Professional proficiency in Danish and English.
It will be an advantage if you have:

• Founder or senior leadership experience from a MedTech or life-science company.
• A PhD or additional education in business, innovation or entrepreneurship.
• Experience with fundraising, partnerships or innovation funding programmes.
What we offer in return
You will become part of DTU Entrepreneurship and work closely with colleagues across DTU and the Technical University Hospital collaboration.

The position offers an opportunity to play a central role in developing a new university-hospital HealthTech innovation pipeline. This means to work with projects spanning clinical unmet needs, engineering, entrepreneurship, prototyping and venture creation.

You will interact with a broad ecosystem of clinicians, researchers, students, entrepreneurs, industry representatives, investors and innovation organisations. You will contribute to establishing a capability intended to remain beyond the present project period.

The role combines strategic development with hands-on engagement in individual innovation and venture projects.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Senior Officer or Senior Executive Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. 

The position is a fixed-term, part-time Special Consultant position until 31 December 2028. The expected employment is 29,6 hours per week. The starting date is 1 November 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Because the activities vary over the project period, the position requires flexibility in the organisation of working time. There will be periods of increased activity around project milestones, educational activities, stakeholder engagement and international collaboration.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than Tuesday, 27 October 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Professor Thomas Howard on thow@dtu.dk.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Entrepreneurship is amongst the leading international entities in technology entrepreneurship and helps develop an entrepreneurial culture across DTU. As part of a dynamic and evolving ecosystem, we combine practice-oriented education and research in entrepreneurship with real start-up opportunities from all DTU departments. With rigorous research at its core, the Center builds the entrepreneurial capabilities of students, industry leaders, academics and policymakers to address unsolved problems, and together create new knowledge, methodologies and initiatives. We enable ethically minded entrepreneurs to build solutions that benefit people, society and the world. The Center experiments with new entrepreneurial methodologies and activities to push boundaries within research and education.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Machine Learning for Non-Stationary and Non-Static Nano-Tomography - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time.

The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data.

The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project.

Responsibilities

• Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data.
• Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction.
• Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits.
• Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities.
• Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging.
• Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects.
• Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations.
Qualifications
You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English.

To succeed in this position, you are expected to have:

• A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline.
• A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models.
• Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks.
• A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods.
Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage:

• Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations.
• Computer vision, 3D vision, geometric modeling, or structure-from-motion.
• Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning.
• Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling.
• Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction.
• Knowledge of X-ray imaging and tomography is beneficial but not required. 
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc.

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

jobs.occupation: 2-Year Postdoctoral Position in Modeling of Microbial Soil Carbon Cycling
jobs.description:
Postdoc of genome-informed microbial biogeochemical modeling

  Department of Biology

  Faculty of SCIENCE

  University of Copenhagen

  Soils store 2300 Pg of organic carbon – three times as much as in the atmosphere. Yet, the fate of these huge carbon stocks under global warming remains highly uncertain. Although microorganisms are key players in soil carbon decomposition, large-scale models ignore microbial processes due to difficulty of quantifying microbial traits that can inform models. To overcome this limitation, the aim of this position is to quantify microbial traits from metagenomes to develop a microbial-explicit version of the dynamic vegetation model LPJ-GUESS.

  You will join a dynamic team at the Center of Excellence VOLT (Center for Volatile interactions, https://volt.ku.dk/) consisting of microbial ecologists, biogeochemists and ecosystem modelers. We offer a creative and stimulating working environment in a collaborative, international research group. We have state-of-the art laboratory facilities and bioninformatics pipelines for analyses of microbial communities and biogeochemical fluxes. Our team also comprises specialists in process-based ecosystem modeling with whom you will closely collaborate. We provide access to supercomputing facilities to carry out bioinformatics and modeling tasks.

  You will work with microbial genomes and metagenomes to predict microbial traits relevant for carbon cycling and modeling using computational structural biology tools to infer protein function. These tasks will use public databases as well as environmental metagenomic datasets produced by the group. You will moreover work with the process-based ecosystem model LPJ-GUESS to implement microbial decomposition of soil organic matter.

  We seek an ambitious and highly motivated candidate with a PhD in computational biology, environmental sciences or related fields. A successful candidate should have a strong background in environmental microbial ecology and bioinformatics as well as experience in advanced statistical analyses and programming with R, python or similar. Moreover, experience with process-based modeling is a plus. Fluency in written and spoken English is a requirement, as well as excellent writing skills demonstrated by the publication record. The candidate should be comfortable working in teams with a collaborative mindset.

  Further information on the Department of Biology is linked at https://www1.bio.ku.dk/ and on the recruiting unit at https://volt.ku.dk/. Inquiries about the position can be made to Jonathan Donhauser, jonathan.donhauser@bio.ku.dk

  The position is open from 1/2/2027 or as soon as possible thereafter and is for 2 years.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

   

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

   

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter describing the motivation for the position 	
• Curriculum vitae (maximum 2 pages) 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan – description of research plan (max. 3 pages) 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 3 particularly relevant papers 	
• Contact details (name, address, telephone & email) of 2 professional referees   
 The deadline for applications is 15 November 2026, 23:59 CET.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

   

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Senior Scientist in Centre for Structure & Interactions

Department: Centre for Structure & Interactions, Therapeutics Discovery, Research & Development

Location: Måløv, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As a Senior Scientist in our Centre for Structure & Interactions, you will turn molecular understanding into better drug candidates for people living with serious chronic diseases. Working hands-on in the laboratory, you will develop and apply biochemical and biophysical approaches to characterise protein interactions, including those involving challenging targets such as integral membrane proteins. Your insights will guide molecular design, enable high-throughput screening and help research teams across our modality portfolio select the most promising candidates to advance.

What you’ll bring

You are a hands-on protein scientist who combines scientific curiosity with rigorous experimental judgement and the initiative to tackle challenging questions. You will bring:

• A completed PhD in protein biochemistry, protein engineering, structural biology, biophysics or a closely related discipline, or at least five years of relevant industry experience demonstrating comparable scientific depth and independence.

• Demonstrated expertise in developing and interpreting biochemical and biophysical assays with purified proteins, using methods such as surface plasmon resonance (SPR), biolayer interferometry (BLI) or fluorescence-based in vitro assays. You can assess protein quality, recognise assay limitations and draw sound mechanistic conclusions.

• A strong foundation in protein biochemistry and experience in protein engineering, such as construct optimisation, mutagenesis or investigating sequence–function relationships, together with familiarity with natural and engineered protein binders.

• Evidence of scientific excellence and independent contributions, demonstrated through high-quality publications or significant achievements in industrial research.

• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to turn complex findings into clear recommendations and build productive relationships across disciplines and with internal and external partners.

Desirable, but not essential:

• Experience with directed evolution, display technologies or other protein selection systems.

• Experience working with challenging proteins, including integral membrane proteins, and an understanding of how preparation and handling affect their stability and activity.

• Experience in structural biology, or the ability to integrate interaction data with structural insights to guide molecular design.

• Experience with, or a strong interest in, automation, high-throughput workflows and computational tools for molecular modelling and visualisation.

What you’ll do

You will combine substantial hands-on laboratory work with scientific ownership of protein interaction studies, working closely with colleagues in the Centre and multidisciplinary project teams.

• Shape scientific questions and experimental strategies that support molecular design and drug candidate selection across our modality portfolio.

• Design, conduct and critically interpret biochemical and biophysical experiments to understand protein interactions, including those involving challenging targets such as integral membrane proteins.

• Apply your understanding of protein biochemistry, engineering and binder formats to guide experimental design and interpret molecular behaviour.

• Develop and deploy high-throughput screening assays, with careful attention to protein quality, assay performance and the biological relevance of the results.

• Develop and implement new approaches to protein interaction analysis, addressing scientific and technical challenges.

• Integrate your findings with complementary project data to provide clear recommendations and influence research decisions.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Centre for Structure & Interactions, a well-established area at the heart of Therapeutics Discovery in Research & Development. We play a central role in identifying, optimising and characterising drug candidates across all therapy areas, shaping project direction and informing key research decisions.

Your closest colleagues will be an interdisciplinary team of 18 highly skilled scientists and laboratory technicians, combining high scientific standards with a supportive, collaborative culture. Together, we connect molecular structure, function and interactions to generate insights that guide molecular design and candidate selection.

You will also work closely with multidisciplinary project teams and colleagues across our global research sites. This offers a strong scientific network and opportunities to influence research beyond your own experiments. Our colleagues bring diverse backgrounds and nationalities, and English is our working and social language.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to investigate challenging molecular questions, develop new experimental approaches and shape decisions that advance promising drug candidates. Working alongside skilled colleagues across disciplines, you will contribute your expertise and ideas in an environment with high scientific standards and a shared commitment to improving patients’ lives.

We value rigorous science, open discussion and a willingness to test new ideas. You will find support to learn from experiments, develop your expertise and take increasing scientific responsibility, within a team that approaches challenges together.

• 
Represent the department across a range of projects and help drive research project progression.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Centre for Functional Assays & Screening (CFAS), part of Therapeutics Discovery in Måløv, Denmark. CFAS designs and runs a range of biologically relevant medium- and high-throughput screening assays, with a strong focus on automation and digitalisation. The team delivers high-quality in vitro data to support the identification, optimisation and characterisation of drug candidates across multiple projects.

CFAS consists of three sub-departments with 20 scientists at different levels of seniority, 15 laboratory technicians and two PhD students. Day to day, you will work closely with department scientists, laboratory technicians and cross-functional project teams. Because CFAS operates in a matrix organisation, you will also partner with screening, automation and in vivo pharmacology colleagues, and connect with colleagues across our global research sites – combining different expertise to keep projects moving.

Your manager will be Assoc. Director Simon Erlendsson.

What you can expect here

You will be part of a high-performing, multidisciplinary team where knowledge-sharing and feedback are part of how the work gets done. Your expertise will be heard across projects, and you will be trusted to shape the cell-based models and screening strategies teams rely on.

The environment is dynamic and evolving, with close links to automation and digitalisation. Working with colleagues across global research sites gives you the opportunity to build a strong scientific network and grow your skills through practical, cross-project experience.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from DKK 570,200 to 838,100, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn cell line engineering and assay expertise into progress for our research projects, apply for the Research Scientist (in vitro biological assays) role by 1 November 2026.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

The Department of Science Education at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a 2-year postdoctoral position starting 1 March 2027. The postdoc position will be a part of the SPINE project (Strengthening Pathways and Infrastructures for Navigating Interdisciplinary Collaboration in Existing Academic Structures), funded by the Lundbeck Foundation

  We are looking for an engaged and independent researcher to help us develop and test practical ways of strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration in research and education.

  The SPINE project investigates how interdisciplinary collaboration can be better supported within existing academic structures. The project combines qualitative research, international fieldwork, and participatory action research to develop practical “plug-and-play” tools, such as methods, templates, games, and workshop formats, that can be readily used by researchers, educators, and research organisations.

   

  Your role

  As a postdoc in SPINE, you will lead the testing and refinement of tools and methods at SPINE’s test sites, including designing and facilitating intervention workshops with researchers and other stakeholders. You will evaluate and adapt approaches across different contexts and help turn research findings into practical, “plug-and-play” resources for interdisciplinary collaboration.

  The position combines research and reporting on the development and testing activities with qualitative research, but the main emphasis will be on the development, testing, and refinement of practical tools and interventions.

   

  You will also contribute to:

   	
• Conducting qualitative research and fieldwork 	
• Analysing and evaluating empirical material and interventions 	
• Working with project partners and stakeholders 	
• Disseminating findings through academic and practice-oriented outputs 	
• Teaching at the Department of Science Education   The position is based in Denmark, where most work will take place. Some international travel will be required for fieldwork, test-site visits, and collaboration with project partners.

   

  Who we are looking for

  We are looking for a researcher interested in how interdisciplinary collaboration works in practice, with the ability to move between research, facilitation, and development.

   

  You should have:

   	
• The ability to work independently while contributing actively to a collaborative team 	
• Strong written and oral communication skills 	
• Willingness and ability to travel internationally when required    

  We are particularly interested in candidates with experience in one or more of the following:

   	
• Interdisciplinary higher education research 	
• Participatory action research or co-design 	
• Workshop facilitation and stakeholder engagement 	
• Developing or evaluating practical approaches to research and collaboration 	
• Translating research into practical or policy-relevant outputs 	
• Spoken or written Danish, which is an advantage but not a requirement   We welcome candidates from different disciplinary and methodological backgrounds and do not expect applicants to meet every criterion.

   

  What we offer

  You will join an international and collaborative research environment in central Copenhagen and become part of a project with a strong focus on research that makes a practical difference.

  The SPINE project is led by Associate Professor Katrine Ellemose Lindvig at the Section for Higher Education Research and Development, Department of Science Education, University of Copenhagen. The SPINE team consists of the PI, one postdoc, and one PhD student, and works closely with colleagues in a wider research group on Interdisciplinary Higher Education, which includes an additional PhD student. As postdoc, you will work closely together with the researchers in SPINE and this wider group, while also collaborating with external partners and stakeholders.

   

  Application

  Start date: 1 March 2027
 Application deadline: 28 October 2026, 23:59 CET
  

  Please submit a single application of no more than 2 pages, combining:

   	
• Your motivation and qualifications for the position, including your relevant research, methodological, and facilitation experience. 	
• Your ideas for contributing to SPINE, including how you would approach testing and refining tools and methods, designing intervention workshops, and developing practical “plug-and-play” resources.    

  In addition, please include:

   	
• CV, including research, fieldwork, teaching, and project experience 	
• One publication that best demonstrates your research capabilities and fit with the position 	
• Publication list 	
• Diplomas and transcripts 	
• Contact details for two references   Applications must be submitted in English through the University of Copenhagen's online recruitment system.

  Before applying, prospective applicants are welcome to contact Associate Professor Katrine Ellemose Lindvig to discuss the position and how their experience might fit the project.
 
 Contact:
 Katrine Ellemose Lindvig
 Email: Katrine.lindvig@ind.ku.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Situational Awareness for Resilient Operation of Distribution Grids - DTU Wind
jobs.description:
How can the distribution grid be made more resilient? 

You have the opportunity to investigate how island operation of the distribution grid can mitigate severe incidents in the power system. Your project will be one of three PhDs in collaboration with DTU Space and DTU Electro. Your project will focus on how improved situational awareness can improve supply of prioritized loads by operating of parts of the distribution grid in island mode during interruptions.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will in the PhD project develop methods for enhancing the ability of microgrids and distribution systems to dynamically transition to and operate as islanded grids that are controlled robustly in a no-single-point-of-failure architecture. The research will investigate how conventional grid measurements can be combined with non-traditional information sources, including information from distributed energy resources or physical surveillance data to maintain a continuously updated understanding of system state, resource availability, and network topology. Operating strategies that can accommodate continuously changing resource situations and stability threats will be devised. To afford manageability of this ever-changing system situation and communication with grid operators and non-grid emergency procedures, a self-representing explainable data model for the coordination with grid operators and other entities.

The outcomes will contribute to the development of resilient distribution system operation concepts and intelligent energy management systems capable of supporting secure islanded operation, faster system recovery, and improved security of electricity supply.

You will be part of a dynamic working environment that will support the growth of your personal and academic skills. You will be part of an international group and will have the opportunity to collaborate with industry and international research groups. You will be involved in our teaching and assist in co-supervision of MSc and BSc students.

A successful candidate will have a solid background in:

• 
Power system engineering and optimization

• 
Data science

• 
Programming tools such as Python

• 
Power system simulation such as PandaPower, PowerFactory

• 
Excellent use of English language

• 
Strong ability to communicate scientific results orally and through scientific publications in international journals

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

Assessment
The assessment of the candidates will be based on the material they submit and one or two stages of interview, online and/or in person. During one of the two stages, the candidates will be asked to review a paper that will be sent to them, and describe its strengths, weaknesses, and potential for future extensions.

The assessment of applications will be ongoing and will start before the application deadline.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. The desired start date is 1 January 2027 depending on academic approval.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Senior Researcher Henrik Bindner, tel.:+452362786, email: hwbi@dtu.dk.

You can read more about the Department of Wind and Energy Systems at www.wind.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU.

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 4 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• 
A letter motivating the application (cover letter)

• 
Curriculum vitae

• 
Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Department of Wind and Energy Systems 
The Department of Wind and Energy Systems is one of the world’s largest centers of wind energy and energy systems research and knowledge, with a staff of more than 400 people from 37 countries working in research, innovation, research-based consulting and education. DTU Wind and Energy Systems has approximately 90 PhD students. The department’s cross-disciplinary research is organized through strategic research programmes that collaborate with Danish and international universities, research institutions and organizations, as well as the wind industry.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Monitoring and Evaluation Advisor for DIGNITY’s international programmes
jobs.description:
Would you like to work in an organisation that makes a tangible and positive difference for vulnerable people in Denmark and globally? If so, DIGNITY can offer you an exciting opportunity as MEAL Advisor.

The position is temporary, starting on 1 January and ending at the end of December 2027.

DIGNITY

Since 1982, DIGNITY has worked for a world free from torture and violence. We are a human rights and development organisation with our own rehabilitation clinic. We prevent torture and violence, rehabilitate traumatised survivors and document serious human rights violations so that those responsible can be brought to justice.

In DIGNITY's International Programmes Department, we work closely with our partners to develop and implement holistic and locally anchored interventions within torture and violence prevention and the rehabilitation of torture survivors.

The department consists of approximately 30 staff members based at our headquarters in Copenhagen. In addition, we have colleagues affiliated with country offices in Ukraine, Jordan and Tunisia, and representations in Uganda, Burkina Faso and Morocco.

About the position

As MEAL Advisor you will join our newly established International Research and Learning Unit together with an interdisciplinary team of senior researchers and monitoring and evaluation experts and analysts. Your primary role and area of responsibility will be to co-manage DIGNITY’s MEAL system related to all international projects, including clinical data related to programs and research, Outcome Harvesting, assessments of capacity building, trainings and learning outcomes etc. A key part of the job is also to guide and support project managers and partners on MEAL and data management as well as undertaking data analysis and dissemination (both qualitative and quantitative) and to deliver evidence-informed input to program and project development.

Your specific tasks will include:

• Coordination and management of Annual Evaluations and Annual plans to donors
• Continuous development and organizational implementation of MEAL-related chapters in DIGNITY’s project Manual
• Strengthening the use of Outcome Harvesting on a cross-cutting level
• Strengthening DIGNITY’s approach to high-quality implementation research through solid and systematic data collation and processing
• Guiding and supporting project managers and partners:
• Assist in yearly log frame and indicator development, including target setting on project level
• Visits to local partners in the Global South
• Training of partners and colleagues in all MEAL-related matters (incl. online, hybrid, and on-site training)
• Support the use and implementation of digital data collection systems, incl. KOBO Toolbox
• Development of surveys and questionnaires and guidance on the use of existing validated tools
• Assist in Partnership Health Checks, needs assessments and project evaluations when needed
• Advice on ethics and data security

We offer:

• A position in a dynamic organisation with a global outlook and a strong professional focus, where the work is driven by the desire to make a positive difference for some of the world's most vulnerable people.
• An opportunity to become part of an international team of committed and skilled colleagues with a focus on collaboration, shared learning and professional development.
• Flexible working hours and a focus on a good work-life balance.

Competencies

We are looking for a candidate with an academic background at Master’s level within a disciplinary field that has a strong focus on data management and methodology including public health, data science, evaluation science, sociology or other social sciences. We also expect you to have at least 2-3 years of experience with monitoring and evaluation as advisor, analyst, project manager, researcher etc.

In addition, we will emphasise that you have the following competencies:

• Solid experience with and understanding of MEAL concepts and methods
• Experience with both quantitative and qualitative data management and analysis
• Understanding of project management processes and tools
• Experience with key MEAL tools (e.g. KOBO Toolbox)
• Strong analytical skills
• Understanding of developing intervention logics and Theories of Change
• Documented experience in education and training of professionals
• Good writing skills, including the ability to write reports of high quality
• Ability to handle multiple priorities, tasks and deadlines simultaneously
• Good collaboration and communication skills
• Ability to work in a multi-cultural environment and with partners in the Global South
• Proficiency in Arabic, French, Ukrainian or Russian is an advantage, but not a requirement.

Terms of employment

The position is a maternity cover, and the employment is temporary from 1 January until the end of December 2027.

The working hours are 37 hours per week. Travel activity of a maximum of 30-40 days may occur.

The position is placed in DIGNITY's International Programmes Department and reports to the Head of International Research and Learning.

Your place of employment is Copenhagen at our HQ at Bryggervangen 55, 2100 Copenhagen Ø.

We expect you to have a registered address in Denmark.

The employment is based on the collective agreement for academics in the Danish State. The salary level is based on skills and relevant experience and within a range of DKK 34.-42.000 (gross, monthly) + pension (18.07%).

Further information

Further information about the position can be obtained by contacting the Head of International Research and Learning, Tomas Max Martin, by phone at +45 22 20 72 86 or by email at tm@dignity.dk.

Application with CV, diploma and any other relevant documents must be submitted via the link no later than 3 November 2026.

We expect to hold the first round of interviews on 11 November 2026 and the second round of interviews on 18 November 2026.

You can read about DIGNITY's processing of your personal data in our privacy policy, which you can find here: Privacy policy - DIGNITY - Danish Institute Against Torture.

We prevent torture and violence, treat traumatised victims and document serious human rights violations so that those responsible can be brought to justice. You can read more about our organisation and work at www.dignity.dk. DIGNITY considers diversity a strength and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply for the position regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion or age.

We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a 3 year position starting on February 1st 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  This post-doc project aims at developing analytical methods to identify and quantify gangliosides and glucosylsphingosine and to combine them with existing methods available at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the Danish Cancer Institute (DCI) to analyse post-mortem brain samples and stem cell derived brain cells from patients with Parkinson’s Disease in order to identify lipid changes associated with the disease pathology.

  Information on the department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk

   

  Our research

  The project will be anchored at the Galvagnion group and be in collaboration with Dr Mesut Bilgin and Dr Kenji Maeda at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the DCI.

  The Galvagnion group research aims at understanding the role of dysfunctions in lipid homeostasis in the emergence of neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s Diseases. Our approach consists in identifying, using biological models, lipid changes associated with these diseases and/or their risk factors and in using biophysical methods to provide at the molecular level the mechanism by which these lipid changes can influence functional protein-membrane interactions and protein aggregation. The different biological models that we consider vary in their complexity and include patient derived cells and brain materials. Our interdisciplinary research involves an international collaborative network including neuroscientists, stem cell biologists, biochemists, protein biophysicists and experts in lipidomics and proteomics.

  The main methods/techniques that we routinely use in the laboratory include molecular biology, recombinant protein production/purification; characterisation of protein, protein-membrane interactions and self/co-assembly using circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, calorimetry, electron microscopy; lipids extraction and characterisation using mass spectrometry; cell culture (established and iPS cell lines), Immunocytochemistry, Western Blot, qPCR; organelle and ex-vivo material isolation.

  We are an international group of 8 PhD students/post-doc/MSc and exchange students with expertise in protein and lipid biophysics, stem cell biology, biochemistry and proteomics.

  More information on our research can be found here:

   	
• Group website 	
• Google Scholar   The Lipidomics Core Facility, headed by Dr. Mesut Bilgin since its establishment in 2015, is a state-of-the-art mass spectrometry platform for the quantitative analysis of lipids in biological samples. Equipped with Orbitrap-based instrumentation for both shotgun and LC-MS lipidomics, the facility identifies and quantifies more than 400 lipid species across 44 lipid classes in materials ranging from cells and tissues to body fluids and organelles. The facility supports in-house research and national and international collaborations and also offers its services to external academic and industry partners. Its research focuses on the roles of lipid metabolism in cancer, including how obesity-related, adipocyte-secreted lipids reprogram the lipidome of cancer cells.

   

  Your job
 We are looking for an outstanding and passionate scientist who has a strong background in lipid analyses and method development. This post-doc project aims at developing new methods to identify and quantify gangliosides and glucosyl and galactosyl sphingosine and to use them in combination with existing methods available at the Lipidomics Core Facility at the DCI to determine lipid changes associated with Parkinson’s Disease in post-mortem brain homogenates, stem cell derived brain cells from patients with PD as well as aggregates isolated from these biological samples.

  The project is funded by a Novo Nordisk Ascending Investigator grant.

   

  Profile 
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• You hold a PhD in analytical chemistry, chemistry, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, molecular life sciences, or a related field. 	
• You have practical experience with LC-MS-based analysis of small molecules, such as lipids, metabolites, or related biomolecules. 	
• You have experience in developing and/or optimizing LC-MS methods and are able to plan, perform, and troubleshoot analytical experiments independently. 	
• You have experience working with biological samples and standard biochemical sample preparation methods. 	
• You have an interest in lipid metabolism and its role in neuroscience and neurodegenerative diseases. 	
• You have strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively in an interdisciplinary team. 	
• You have excellent written and spoken English.   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Experience with lipidomics and/or MS-based lipid analysis. 	
• Experience working with cells, tissues, subcellular fractions, or other complex biological samples. 	
• Knowledge of Parkinson’s disease, neurodegeneration, or protein amyloid/aggregation.    

  Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and state of the art lipidomic facilities.

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The starting date is February 1st 2027, or as soon as possible afterwards.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,900 DKK/approx. 5,300 EUR (August 2026-level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

   

  Questions
 For further information please contact Céline Galvagnion; celine.galvagnion@sund.ku.dk; www.sund.ku.dk 

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

   

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do. 	
• List of publications.    

  Deadline for applications: 15/11/2026, 23.59pm CET

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  Online interviews are expected to be held in week 49 and in-person interviews in week 51.

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.description:
Do you want to kick-start your international career in trading and work in a fast-growing, entrepreneurial company in the heart of Copenhagen?

We are looking for a Trader Trainee with strong German language skills (professional or native level) to join our international trading team. This is your opportunity to gain hands-on experience across the full trading cycle and build a commercial career with a global outlook.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Trader Trainee, you’ll be involved in the entire trading process, from sourcing and purchasing to sales and customer dialogue in international markets, with an initial focus on the German market.

You’ll work closely with suppliers, logistics partners, and customers, gaining insights into both the commercial and operational side of trading.

Your tasks will typically include:

• Administrative and operational support tasks, including order creation

• Building your own customer portfolio over time

• Sales and client dialogue

• Purchasing and supplier dialogue

• Close collaboration with Logistics, Business Operations, and Finance

• Market research and outreach to new customers

• Handling claims and commercial follow-ups

You will follow a structured trainee programme with onboarding, mentoring, and continuous development, giving you the tools to grow into a commercial role within trading. As part of our trainee team in Copenhagen, you will also contribute to shared trainee responsibilities and support day-to-day activities in the office.

YOUR PROFIL

We are looking for someone who is motivated by learning, responsibility, and international collaboration:

• You are curious, proactive, and eager to learn

• You thrive in a fast-paced environment and keep a cool head under pressure

• You are commercially minded and enjoy working with people

• You take ownership and follow through on your tasks

• You are outgoing and confident in building relationships

LANGUAGE SKILLS

• You speak German at a professional or native level (essential)

• You communicate fluently in English

• Danish is an advantage, but not a requirement

We imagine that you have completed HHX, EUD, EUX Business, a foundational course (HG, HGV, HGS) from a business college, or a general upper-secondary education (HF, STX, HTX). Experience from a similar industry or relevant background is an advantage, but not a requirement.

WHY JOIN US

We offer a 2-year in-house trainee programme with the possibility of permanent employment upon completion.

You’ll gain hands-on experience, take on real responsibility, and develop both professionally and personally in a supportive and ambitious team. We are a young, social company with a flat structure, where your ideas matter and you have the opportunity to make an impact.

Our office is centrally located in Copenhagen, close to the metro, in an international and dynamic environment.

WE ALSO OFFER

• Pension scheme and health insurance

• 5 weeks of vacation + 5 additional paid days

• Mobile phone plan and equipment allowance

• Lunch, breakfast, and snacks

• Social events incl. Friday bar, team dinners, and annual company trip

• Staff discounts

• Transport scheme

• Opportunities for international travel and placements

ABOUT NORIDANE

At NoriDane, you’ll be part of a fast-growing international trading company with more than 100 colleagues across 20+ nationalities and operations in Europe, Latin America, and Asia.

We specialize in global food trading, supplying high-quality meat, seafood, and dry goods that meet the highest standards. Our ambition is to be the preferred link between suppliers and customers worldwide by combining market insight, product expertise, and efficient logistics.

OUR CULTURE

You will be part of a growing company with highly committed and dynamic colleagues, all united by a strong value-based approach. At NoriDane, we embrace the Arbinger principles, integrating them into our daily ways of working, thinking, and interacting. We believe in empowering individuals to take ownership of their tasks while fostering a culture where mistakes are seen as valuable learning opportunities. Our envi-ronment promotes openness, transparency, and continuous growth, creating a workplace that is not only ambitious and passionate but also collaborative, fun, and supportive. We believe in promoting a healthy work-life balance and offer flexible work arrangements to support the well-being of our team.

WANT TO JOIN OUR TEAM?

Please send your CV, application, and other relevant information to jobs@noridane.com. We will review applications on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

By submitting your application, you consent to the processing of your personal data in accordance with our privacy policy.

We encourage a diverse culture and invite all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, reli-gion, sexual orientation, handicap, country of origin, or ethnicity.

jobs.occupation: PhD Fellowship in Nutrition and Inflammatory Bowel Disease
jobs.description:
The National Center of Excellence for the Molecular Prediction of Inflammatory Bowel Disease (PREDICT), based at Department of Clinical Medicine, Aalborg University (AAU) in Copenhagen, is looking to recruit a highly skilled and motivated PhD student in nutrition and inflammatory bowel disease to join our international and interdisciplinary group of dedicated researchers.The 3-year stipend (full-time, 37 hours per week) is available within the doctoral program Clinical Science, Laboratory and Translational Medicine, and is open for appointment from 1st of March 2027 or soon thereafter.

**Your work tasks
**We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student to join our Nutrition Research Group and contribute to research exploring the role of diet in the development and progression of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The project aims to improve our understanding of diet-disease relationships and generate evidence that can support future dietary recommendations for individuals living with IBD.

The PhD student will work with large population-based cohorts to investigate associations between dietary patterns, nutritional exposures, and disease outcomes. As part of an interdisciplinary research environment, you will collaborate closely with epidemiologists, nutrition scientists, clinicians, and biostatisticians engaged in internationally recognized research.

Your main responsibilities will include:

• 
Conducting systematic literature reviews and evidence syntheses

• 
Developing research protocols and statistical analysis plans

• 
Managing and analyzing large-scale epidemiological data

• 
Conducting statistical analyses using R and other relevant software

• 
Writing and publishing scientific articles in peer-reviewed journals

• 
Presenting research findings at national and international conferences

• 
Contributing to collaborative research activities within the Center and with external partners

You will receive supervision and training from experienced researchers and become an integral part of a dynamic and supportive research environment.

Your competencies We are looking for an ambitious and self-driven candidate with a strong interest in nutrition, epidemiology, and inflammatory bowel disease research. Previous experience in nutrition-related research, preferably in the field of inflammatory bowel disease, is an advantage.

The ideal candidate has:

• 
A Master's degree in Nutrition and Dietetics, Human Nutrition, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Sciences, or another relevant discipline

• 
Knowledge of nutritional epidemiology and inflammatory bowel disease

• 
Experience writing scientific reports, theses, or manuscripts

• 
Familiarity with statistical programming, preferably in R

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

• 
Excellent collaboration and communication skills

• 
Excellent written and spoken English proficiency

• 
The ability to work independently while contributing to a multidisciplinary research team

**Qualification requirements
**PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School in Medicine, Biomedical Science and Technology in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions.

According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Please visit the website of the doctoral school for further information on admission requirements.

Who we are
PREDICT is at the forefront of international research to unravel the cause and prognosis of inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), which are chronic and disabling conditions affecting millions of people worldwide. The Center is composed of biologists, clinicians, epidemiologists, and data scientists working with collaborators nationally and internationally to push the boundaries of precision medicine research and create real-world impact in IBD. We have state-of-the-art facilities within the center and this means through PREDICT you will be part of a well-funded research environment equipped with the latest technologies, unique data, and a world-leading network of collaborators.

We offer an exciting PhD program in a dynamic, high-performing, international environment with dedicated, friendly colleagues. We also offer superb opportunities for personal and professional development and unique access to state-of-the-art data resources, including linkable Danish nationwide health registries, Danish National Biobank data and individual level clinical data from the largest Danish IBD inception cohort; the NorDIBD Cohort.

You can read more about PREDICT here.

**About the Department of Clinical Medicine
**The Department of Clinical Medicine provides research-based teaching across all disciplines of the medical degree programme and conducts research within the clinical specialties.

Read more about the Department of Clinical Medicine here.

**How to apply
**Your application must include the following:

• 
Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position

• 
Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• 
Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades)

• 
Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions?     If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School in Medicine, Biomedical Science and Technology

**Salary and terms of employment
**The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

Contacts

**About The Role

As Global Operational Excellence Deployment Lead, you will play a key role in bringing AAK's Operational Excellence vision to life across our global manufacturing network and value chain functions. • Fluent in English; additional languages are an advantage.

Contact and information
