jobs.occupation: Field Services Engineer, EMEA (Denmark or Germany)
jobs.description:
Introduction

We are looking for a talented Field Service Engineer based in Ballerup, Denmark or in Southern Germany. The ideal candidate has a minimum of 7 years of experience in servicing and maintaining scientific, analytical, biomedical, or laboratory equipment**.

About the Role

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Field Service Engineer to join Sophion Bioscience’s small, dedicated service team.

You will work alongside curious, hands-on colleagues who solve problems, share knowledge, and support one another - even when working independently in the field.

The team values high-quality work, clear communication, and a straightforward, respectful customer experience. In this key role, you will ensure the reliable performance of our automated patch clamp and organ-on-a-chip instruments at customer sites. Your responsibilities will include troubleshooting, maintenance and repairs, system evaluations, customer training, and coordinating upgrades with cross-functional teams.

As an ambassador for Sophion, you will build strong customer relationships by communicating effectively and resolving technical issues promptly, helping drive the continued growth of Sophion Bioscience.

About Us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ On a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are driven by curiosity, teamwork, and a genuine passion for helping scientists succeed. We work in an open and collaborative environment where people share knowledge freely, support each other across roles and borders, and take pride in doing things properly. Our culture is informal, trusting, and grounded in respect — for colleagues, customers, and the science we enable. Even as we grow globally, we remain a company where people feel welcome, included, and able to make a meaningful impact.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

• Installation and Commissioning: Conducting on-site installation and commissioning of Sophion Automated Patch Clamp and Ethica M instrumentation, ensuring it meets the client's specifications and quality standards.

• Maintenance and Repairs: Performing routine maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs of QPatch, Qube and Ethica M systems to ensure uninterrupted functionality. Responding promptly to service requests and providing timely resolutions.

• Documentation: Creating detailed service reports, documentation, and maintaining accurate records of all service activities. Providing feedback to the engineering and R&D teams for continuous product improvement.

• Training: Providing training to clients on the proper usage, maintenance, and troubleshooting of Sophion automated patch clamp & Ethica M instrumentation, ensuring they have a clear understanding of its features and capabilities.

• Customer Support: Serving as a point of contact for technical support, addressing client inquiries, and maintaining strong relationships with customers to enhance satisfaction.

• Collaboration: Collaborating with the Sales, Application Science and Engineering teams to communicate client feedback, potential product enhancements, and identify opportunities for upselling additional services or products.

Who You Are

You are an experienced service professional with a passion for customer success, technical excellence, and being a team player. You thrive in a hands-on environment where no two days are the same and enjoy executing your day-to-day responsibilities in close collaboration with the rest of the Sophion team.

We imagine that you:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Biomedical Engineering, a related field or equivalent certifications

• In-depth knowledge of liquid handling devices from various industry systems is a benefit.

• Experience with electrical and pneumatics preferred

• Must possess a good grasp of core engineering concepts which include the ability to read and interpret electrical/circuit Schematic drawings.

• Able to use test/measuring equipment like Digital Multimeter (DVM).

• Team player, critical thinker, and flexible for effective performance in the field.

• Experience with service management systems and processes

• Familiarity with the operation and maintenance of Festo pressure systems is a plus

• Manage MySQL and Oracle databases to ensure seamless system integration and performance.

• Network Configuration and Maintenance: configure and troubleshoot network setups, routers, and DHCP configurations to guarantee optimal system connectivity.

• Possess a basic understanding of Linux systems to address software and operating system-related challenges.

• Demonstrate excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities to address technical issues promptly.

• Communicate effectively with customers and colleagues, ensuring a positive and collaborative working place.

• Ability to travel 50-60% once initial training is complete.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact the HR Director, Helene Fife, (+45 51 20 34 43).

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

As senior commercial lead, you will own oasicare’s commercial strategy, market development, revenue delivery and commercial organisation.

Your initial mandate is to determine how the existing distributor, direct-to-hospital and consumer-driven opportunities should be combined and sequenced by market. You will then lead execution of the optimal strategy.

You will personally own critical customers, hospitals and distributor relationships, early commercial experiments and major negotiations while building the team and systems required for scale.

• Build relationships with maternity wards, clinicians, hospital management, procurement teams and relevant professional organisations.

• Personally lead strategically important early accounts and partnerships.

Advance and activate a suitable distributor strategy

• Validate partner fit, commitment, commercial terms, evidence expectations, country access and launch capabilities.

• Negotiate, appoint, onboard and manage distributors in markets where this is the preferred route.

• Establish country plans, training, marketing support, order commitments and performance expectations.

Advance and activate consumer-funded, hospital-enabled model

You should understand that selling a regulated healthcare product is very different from selling conventional products and services.

• Experience with distributors and international market expansion.

• Strong negotiation and deal-closing skills.

• Experience in an entrepreneurial, scale-up or early commercial-stage environment.

How you work

jobs.occupation: Two-year Postdoc position on Spintronic Quantum-inspired Computing
jobs.description:
Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a 2-year Postdoctoral Researcher position within the newly funded QUANTRONIC – Spintronic Pseudo-Qubits for Room-Temperature Quantum Computing project, supported by the Villum Experiment programme of Villum Fonden.

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate a new class of spintronic pseudo-qubits (p-qubits) based on spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs). The project explores whether engineered stochastic spintronic devices can reproduce key computational mechanisms associated with quantum systems - including superposition-like states, probability-amplitude-based interference, and entanglement-like correlations—without relying on fragile quantum coherence or cryogenic operation.

QUANTRONIC is a high-risk, high-gain research project positioned at the intersection of spintronics, probabilistic computing, quantum-inspired computing, nanoelectronics, and integrated circuit design. The central concept is a novel SOT-MTJ architecture designed to represent and manipulate probability amplitudes and to enable synchronization between multiple pseudo-qubits. The project will combine physics-based modelling, device design and fabrication, experimental characterization, and system-level demonstrations.

The successful candidate will work within SDU Microelectronics and collaborate closely with international partners, particularly INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory, on the design and fabrication of spintronic devices.

The position is expected to start in February 2027, with the specific starting date to be agreed with the successful candidate.

 

As a Postdoctoral Researcher in QUANTRONIC, your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Develop and refine physics-based compact models of SOT-MTJ-based pseudo-qubits, including stochastic switching and inter-device coupling.

• 
Develop Verilog-A models and integrate them into circuit-level simulation environments such as Cadence.

• 
Investigate the physical requirements for controlling probabilistic states and representing probability amplitudes in spintronic devices.

• 
Collaborate with project partners on the design and fabrication of SOT-MTJ devices and arrays.

• 
Experimentally characterize standalone devices and coupled arrays, including stochastic switching, synchronization, and entanglement-like correlations.

• 
Investigate quantum-inspired gate operations and system-level demonstrations using networks of pseudo-qubits.

• 
Contribute to proof-of-concept demonstrations, including integer factorization and other quantum-inspired computational problems.

• 
Publish research results in high-quality international journals and conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results.

• 
Collaborate with researchers in spintronics, probabilistic computing, microelectronics, materials science, and quantum information.

 

What we offer

• 
A unique opportunity to work on a high-risk, high-gain research concept exploring a new computational regime between classical probabilistic and quantum computing.

• 
A stimulating research environment within SDU Microelectronics, a growing research section with expertise in spintronics, probabilistic computing, neuromorphic computing, analog/digital IC design, and emerging computing architectures.

• 
Access to advanced facilities for electronic design, device characterization, measurement, and system prototyping.

• 
Close collaboration with INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory on spintronic device technology and fabrication.

• 
Opportunities to collaborate with national and international researchers in spintronics, quantum-inspired computing, quantum technologies, and nanoelectronics.

• 
An open, international, and collaborative research environment within SDU's Faculty of Engineering, supporting interdisciplinary research across electronics, physics, materials science, and computing.

• 
Strong opportunities for developing an independent research profile in an emerging area of probabilistic and quantum-inspired hardware.

 

What we expect

Applicants should hold a PhD in electronic engineering, electrical engineering, applied physics, nanotechnology, spintronics, or a closely related field.

The ideal candidate should have experience in one or more of the following areas:

• 
Spintronics and magnetic devices, particularly MTJs, STT-MTJs, SOT-MTJs, or related technologies.

• 
Physics-based modelling of nanoscale or magnetic devices.

• 
Verilog-A, SPICE, and Cadence or comparable circuit/device simulation environments.

• 
Experimental characterization of electronic, magnetic, or spintronic devices.

• 
Stochastic or probabilistic computing systems.

Experience in micromagnetic simulation, magnetotransport measurements, nanofabrication, probabilistic computing, or quantum/quantum-inspired computing will be considered a strong advantage.

We are particularly interested in candidates who are enthusiastic about working across traditional disciplinary boundaries and are comfortable combining device physics, modelling, experimentation, and computing concepts.

The successful candidate should be able to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary and international research team. Excellent written and spoken English and strong communication skills are required.

 

Workplace description 

The successful candidate will join SDU Microelectronics, a dynamic and expanding section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME). The section conducts internationally recognized research in integrated circuits, spintronics, photonics, and neuromorphic computing, and plays a central role in SDU’s ambition to be a national and European hub for semiconductor and chip innovation. 

 

Further information 

For further information about the position, please contact Professor Farshad Moradi (moradi@sdu.dk / email), Head of the SDU Microelectronics section and Associate Professor Hooman Farkhani (farkhani@sdu.dk / email), Deputy Head of SDU Microelectronics. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is February 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

jobs.description:
The Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a 2-year position as a postdoctoral researcher within spintronic computing. The position offers an exciting opportunity to advance spintronics through device physics, simulation, fabrication, experimental characterization, and integration of spintronic devices for advanced computing applications.

We are seeking a highly motivated candidate to investigate, design, fabricate, and characterize spintronic devices, with particular emphasis on Anisotropic Magnetoresistance (AMR), Giant Magnetoresistance (GMR), and Tunneling Magneto Resistance (TMR) devices. The work will combine magnetic and spintronic device physics, materials and multilayer structures, device fabrication, electrical measurement, modelling, and data analysis, with the aim of developing reliable spintronic technologies for advanced computing and emerging semiconductor applications.

The research will focus on understanding, controlling, and exploiting thermal fluctuations and stochastic switching in MTJs for physical entropy generation and energy-efficient computing, with particular emphasis on True Random Number Generators (TRNGs) and Stochastic Neural Accelerators (SNAs).

The successful candidate will work on the physics-based design, modelling, simulation, fabrication, and experimental characterization of spintronic devices and their integration into advanced computing systems. The position also includes a role in the Danish Chips Competence Center, where the candidate will contribute to connecting the Danish semiconductor and spintronics ecosystem with relevant EU pilot lines, facilitating collaboration, technology development, prototyping, and access to European semiconductor fabrication capabilities. The candidate will also contribute to preparing and writing research proposals and funding applications related to spintronics, semiconductor technologies, and advanced computing.

Would you like to be part of an ambitious Compliance team where you play a key role in ensuring that Saxo meets its regulatory obligations across all parts of the Information Communication Technology (ICT) organisation?

If so, this may be the right opportunity for you.

You will join the Prudential Oversight team within Group Compliance, Saxo's second line of defence function, based at our headquarters in Hellerup. The team oversees compliance risks across ICT, operational risk and data governance, supporting the business in meeting regulatory requirements, market standards and internal policies. Working closely with Compliance colleagues in Denmark and internationally, you will play a key role in strengthening compliance oversight across Saxo's technology organisation.

Your primary responsibility will be to conduct compliance oversight and monitoring across ICT areas regulated by DORA, including ICT risk management, incident management, business continuity and resilience testing, access management, critical functions and systems and third-party ICT service providers.

Depending on your profile, knowledge and experience, the role may also include compliance activities within operational risk, data quality and data governance.

As a team, we balance professionalism with a sense of humour and maintain an informal atmosphere where people enjoy coming to work.

You will join an organisation where the foundation of the business is built on ICT and where platform availability is key to help clients get invested in the world. In the Prudential Oversight Compliance Team, ICT regulation is a core focus, and you will help us support Saxo in continuously driving this important area in a compliant direction.

Perform compliance risk assessments within the areas of ICT risks, operational risks and data risks, with a particular focus on DORA-related requirements

• 
Provide advice, challenge and compliance opinions to the business on regulatory requirements and compliance risks

• 
Conduct compliance monitoring activities, including follow-up and closure of recommendations

• 
Contribute to regular compliance reporting to the senior management of the bank

• 
Participate in developing Saxo’s compliance framework

• 
Collaborate closely with our Compliance Team in India

• 
Interact with the business across organisational levels and seniority

Your profile

We are looking for a colleague with solid experience working in ICT compliance, operational risk, data governance or technology risk management.

Most importantly, you have experience working with ICT requirements and legislation, ICT governance, risk assessments, and advisory work related to ICT requirements, and you are familiar with DORA or NIS2.

You may have gained this experience within a second line of defence compliance or risk function, a first line of defence risk or control role within financial services, internal or external audit, IT audit, consultancy or another highly regulated industry. jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer – IoT Platform, Load and Energy Management
jobs.description:
🚀 About the role

We're looking for a senior software engineer who writes solid, reliable code and wants that code to control real hardware. At FLEXECHARGE, our HARMON-E platform manages load and energy for EV charging operators across Europe. Part of it runs at the edge, on an industrial PC next to chargers, batteries and solar inverters, and connected to the interfaces DSOs use to curtail load.

You'll build and maintain the TypeScript microservices that talk to those devices and turn their data into decisions. This is not a web-app role. It's software engineering for systems where the other side is physical, stateful and often unreliable.

⚡ What is special about this role

It sits where two worlds meet:

• 
Web and cloud toolchain: TypeScript, Docker, MQTT, Azure, Kubernetes.

• 
Operational technology and system integration: talking to real chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus and OCPP, running at the edge on an industrial PC.

Your code won't only talk to clean APIs in a data centre. It runs on site, next to real peripheral devices, and has to keep doing its job when those devices and the networks between them don't behave as expected.

We recognize that TypeScript is not typically used for edge computing or hardware interfacing. This is why we're looking for a strong software engineer who is interested in learning new techniques and applications, as well as applying their technical skills in novel ways.

🛠️ What you'll do

• 
Write and maintain a combination of TypeScript microservices and the business logic behind them: control algorithms, scheduling and decision-making, not just plumbing.

• 
Build and extend device drivers for chargers, batteries and inverters over Modbus TCP, using our existing driver services as a starting point.

• 
Work with OCPP, which our platform already supports, as you ramp up.

• 
Run services in containers at the edge and connect them through MQTT and pub/sub messaging to our cloud backend.

• 
Profile and optimise software on edge hardware, where hardware resources are constrained.

• 
Help shape the long-term move of performance-critical services to compiled languages.

• 
Mentor and pair with colleagues on integrations and software craft.

🤔 Why compiled languages, if we write TypeScript?

It may sound odd, so here's the reasoning. Today the majority of our edge stack is TypeScript, and you'll develop in it from day one. Over time we want to move selected services, such as device interfaces and performance-critical paths, to a compiled language while keeping them part of the same stack.

To do that well, you need to understand both sides: the TypeScript services as they are now, and the concepts of memory, types and performance that compiled languages force you to think about. In our experience, it's much easier to go from a compiled language to a scripting environment than the other way around. So if you're a Go, C, C++, Rust or similar developer who is happy to work in TypeScript (or happy to learn), you're exactly who we're looking for.

✅ Must-have

• 
3–5+ years of professional software development, with strong software and engineering fundamentals.

• 
Professional experience in a compiled language (for example Go, C, C++, Rust, C# or Java).

• 
Proficiency in a scripting language, ideally TypeScript, otherwise JavaScript or Python, or a clear willingness to become productive in TypeScript quickly.

• 
Experience writing business logic with stateful calculations and operations, which can self-heal and recover gracefully.

• 
Comfort with asynchronous and event-driven systems that talk to unreliable external components or peripheral devices.

💡 Strongly preferred (but we'll teach it)

• 
Hands-on device or protocol integration: Modbus, serial interfaces, Ethernet/TCP-IP or comparable.

• 
Containerised applications. Docker, Docker Compose or Kubernetes are ideal, but any container technology counts.

• 
Pub/sub and distributed systems, ideally MQTT or another IoT messaging protocol, and an understanding of their reliability concerns.

• 
Working within constrained systems, including profiling software to find where CPU or memory limits bite.

🎁 Bonus, not a requirement

• 
OCPP experience.

• 
Energy, EV charging or power-systems domain knowledge.

• 
Edge deployment experience.

If you don't have these, apply anyway. Strong fundamentals and the right mindset matter more. 💪

🚫 This role is probably not for you if

• 
Your experience is mainly frontend or request/response web apps, with no compiled-language background.

• 
You prefer to stay in one language and aren't interested in working in TypeScript.

• 
You want a pure firmware or PLC role without writing higher-level services.

• 
You don't enjoy debugging the messy cases where hardware doesn't behave as documented.

🌆 What is it like to work at FLEXECHARGE?

• 
Our office is in Frederiksberg: bright, comfortable, and a genuinely nice place to spend your workday.

• 
You're covered with pension contributions.

• 
Lunch is served on-site, and it's delicious, healthy and nutritious.

• 
We enjoy each other's company outside work too, with Friday bars, company events and team-building activities within each team.

• 
You'll have opportunities for individual development.

🤝 Our interview process

Here's roughly what happens once we've had a look at your application:

• 
A first conversation (about 30 minutes) with our recruiter. You'll get a feel for the role, ask whatever's on your mind, and we'll both get a sense of whether this is worth pursuing further.

• 
Time with the team: a conversation with Kasper, our Head of Architecture & Systems, and Robert, our CTO.

• 
A technical stage: one or more interviews with the team, which may include a case exercise and follow-up discussions. These can take place remotely or at our office.

• 
A conversation with Max, our CEO, alongside someone else from the team.

Hiring carefully matters to us. We want to get to know you properly, and we want you to get a real feel for us too. If there's anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us.

We'd love to hear from you.

📍 Location & practical details

This is an on-site role based in Copenhagen. Only candidates currently located in Copenhagen, or those who clearly state in their application that they plan to relocate, will be considered.

Please note:

• 
We do not offer visa sponsorship for this role.

• 
We do not offer relocation services.

🔐 Data privacy (GDPR)

Applications for this role are processed exclusively through The Hub (thehub.io), our recruitment platform, in accordance with their privacy policy and applicable GDPR requirements. As part of our interview process, conversations may be recorded and transcribed via Microsoft Teams, and AI tools may be used to summarise interview notes to support our hiring team's evaluation. Your data will be handled confidentially, retained only during the interview process, and used only for this recruitment process.

For more information or questions please contact us at iva@flexecharge.com

Working at

FLEXECHARGE

FLEXECHARGE is a cleantech scale-up which offers a powerful load & energy management platform, as a SaaS, to help Charge Point Operators (ex: Clever, eOn, etc.) to optimise their charging operations & business. Our mission is accelerate green mobility through our Smart Charging solutions that make charging faster, greener and cheaper. Our vision is to integrate charging infrastructures better with the grid supply and the ever more volatile & growing production of renewable energy. We want to connect electric vehicles with the grid in a whole new way. By seeing electric vehicles not as a risk for our supply grid, but as a crucial asset for the transition towards 100% renewable energy. We do this through constant innovation of new smart charging features which will make us the preferred partner for EV infrastructure owners, developers, and operators.

jobs.occupation: Project manager for international research projects
jobs.description:
Are you enthusiastic about making a difference to large societal challenges such as green transition of energy, materials and food systems?

Do you have experience with research project management, funding administration and project development? 

Do you know your way around a Horizon Europe project and do you enjoy being the person who keeps a large international consortium on track?

Do you thrive in a dynamic working environment, with multiple external and internal stakeholders?

Then we might be looking for you!

At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering at Aarhus University, we are busy conducting research on a broad range of topics related to green transition, sustainability and health. Our portfolio of EU-funded projects is growing, and we are therefore looking for an experienced EU project manager with international experience who can drive development and execution of international projects in close collaboration with researchers, external partners and the department’s Partnerships and External Relations team.

Expected starting date and duration
The position is a two-year fixed-term position starting on 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job descripton
At Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering, we are experiencing an increase in externally funded, international research and innovation projects. As project manager you will play a key role in managing and coordinating the department’s participation in such projects, in particular large Horizon Europe projects with multiple partners, where our department has a leading role 

Working closely with the scientific coordinator, you will:

• Act as the day-to-day operational point of contact for the consortium. 
• Drive the coordination machinery: Track deliverables, milestones and risks, chase and quality-assure partner contributions.
• Prepare periodic/final reporting, and coordinate financial reporting with partners and with the administrative and financial experts in AU’s central research support office.
• Plan and run consortium, General Assembly and review meetings: Agendas, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
• Maintain the Consortium Agreement and support obligations on data management, ethics, dissemination, exploitation and communication.
In addition to this, you will:

• Support the department’s wider portfolio of international projects, being work package or task manager where relevant.
• Provide guidance and support to the development of new European grant proposals and the building of new consortia.
• Participate in and help organise externally oriented activities and events.
• Help shape the department’s way of working around externally funded projects, so that good practice is developed and shared.
The role is vested in the department’s Partnerships and External Relations team. The team supports our researchers within multiple aspects of externally funded research collaborations - from strategy development, visibility, partnership and project development to execution of complex projects. We are continuously developing our way of working to support increased activity level and creation of impact.

Qualifications
We are looking for someone who combines hands-on experience of EU project execution with the ability to work comfortably alongside researchers in a technical field.

Technical qualifications:

• Academic degree in a relevant field (e.g., technical sciences, international relations etc.).
• Experience with the day-to-day management of Horizon Europe or Horizon 2020 projects; including reporting, deliverable and milestone tracking.
• Experience of working with international research consortia and of coordinating contributions from partners in several countries.
• The ability to engage with technical content well enough to quality-assure deliverables and to discuss the work with researchers on their own terms.
Qualifications we regard as an advantage:

• Experience from the coordinator side of an EU project, rather than as a beneficiary partner only.
• Experience with proposal development, grant writing and consortium building.
• Familiarity with research areas related to the green transition; for example bioresources, biotechnology, chemical or environmental engineering.
• Familiarity with EU financial rules, cost eligibility and audit requirements.
Personal qualifications:

• Excellent communication skills, with fluency in English. Knowledge of Danish is an advantage.
• Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple stakeholders and priorities effectively
• Service-minded attitude, flexibility, and a collaborative approach to working in a team
• Ability to travel internationally as needed (few times per year). 
Who we are
At the Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering we focus on living systems, the biology of organisms, efficient production, and transformation of chemicals, materials and energy. We translate knowledge within biotechnology, food technology, environmental technology, chemical engineering, industrial biotechnology, medical biotechnology and electrochemical engineering etc. more into new technologies and value-creating solutions that can also be used in the business community.

Many of our research and development activities are based on companies' specific innovation needs or specialist application areas. Close collaboration with the public sector and private businesses ensures that the knowledge and technology generated in the department's research environments has a clear anchoring in reality and benefits the surrounding society. We also provide research-based public sector consultancy and advice on technology in agriculture and food.

At the department, we educate BEng, BSc and MSc graduates in engineering for Danish society.

Read more about the department and sections here:
https://bce.au.dk/en/research/key-areas-in-research-and-development

Department of Biological and Chemical Engineering offers:

• The possibility of being part of a dynamic research environment in rapid development

You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8. For the right candidate, there will be an opportunity to be appointed as a Special Consultant, with remuneration in accordance with Appendix 4 of the collective agreement.

jobs.employer_name: Natural Sciences - Institut for Fysik og Astronomi
jobs.description:
The Aarhus Laboratory Astrochemistry Group is seeking applications for a postdoctoral position in laboratory astrochemistry under supervision of Prof. Liv Hornekær at the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Aarhus University.

Job description
The successful applicants will participate in the experimental research activities under ERC Synergy Grant IRAstro and DNRF Center of Excellence for Interstellar Catalysis – InterCat. This combined project aims at elucidating how molecules on interstellar dust grain analogue surfaces organize, react and dissipate energy under low temperature and low pressure conditions mimicking dense interstellar dust and molecular clouds. The applicant will use low temperature scanning tunneling microscopy (STM), temperature programmed desorption, and (single molecule) IR spectroscopy to follow in situ reactions leading to complex molecule formation on realistic dust grain analogue surfaces. Close collaboration with theoreticians, observers and the experimental astrochemistry groups at Aarhus University and at the nodes of collaborative partners is expected.

The job includes:

• Mapping of catalytic pathways and reaction rates on interstellar dust grain analogue surfaces using STM, TPD, and RAIRS. 
• development, maintenance and troubleshooting on various experimental UHV setups
• participating in maintenance of the group laboratories.
• data analysis and writing scientific publications.
• supervision of PhD, Master and bachelor students.
• project administration, such as writing reports etc.
 
Qualifications
Candidates should have a PhD degree in physics or similar field, with strong experience in experimental surface science, UHV techniques, catalysis/reactions on surfaces and atomic scale characterization. A background in laboratory astrochemistry is preferred.

The ideal candidate has good collaboration skills and is also able to work independently.

About IRAstro - Molecular Quantum Dynamics in Low-Temperature Astrochemistry 
The ERC Synergy project IRAstro brings together leading researchers in physics, chemistry, and astrochemistry to uncover how molecules behave and react under the extreme conditions of interstellar space.

Recent observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) reveal the complexity of low temperature molecular ices frozen out on interstellar dust grains in regions where new stars and planetary systems are formed. Interpreting these observations requires a deeper understanding of the fundamental physical and chemical processes that govern molecular behaviour at temperatures close to absolute zero.

IRAstro addresses this challenge by combining cutting-edge laboratory experiments, advanced instrumentation, and first-principles theory. The project focuses on the quantum dynamics of molecules in low-temperature condensed phases - a frontier area essential for understanding how chemical complexity arises in space.

https://phys.au.dk/irastro

About InterCat – Center for Interstellar Catalysis 
InterCat is a center of excellence supported by the Danish National Research Foundation. The center is situated at the Department of Physics and Astronomy and at the Interdisciplinary Nanoscience Center at Aarhus University in Denmark, at Leiden Observatory at Leiden University in the Netherlands and Niels Bohr Institute at University of Copenhagen in Denmark. See https://phys.au.dk/intercat/ for further details.

The scientific aim of the Center for Interstellar Catalysis is to determine whether the production of the molecular building blocks of life, e.g., sugars, amino acids, fats and DNA bases, predates the formation of stars and planets, and occurs at the extremely low temperatures and pressures found in interstellar space. InterCat thus aims to determine the molecular starting conditions for the origin of life across the universe.

InterCat brings together research teams within surface science, nanoscience, heterogeneous catalysis and experimental and observational astrochemistry.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2-year postdoc position expected to start 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible. 

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Prof. Liv Hornekær, liv@phys.au.dk. 

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 28 October 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

The Research Group for Global Capacity Building (GCB) is looking for a part-time student assistant to support administrative tasks related to project management, communications, and training for the Global Pathogen Analysis Platform (GPAP) project.

The Research Group for Global Capacity Building with DTU National Food Institute works to strengthen the global surveillance of infectious disease agents and antimicrobial resistance and to develop and implement procedures for building laboratory capacity with a focus on whole genome sequencing. All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU National Food Institute
DTU National Food Institute conducts research into and disseminates - through advice, innovation and teaching - sustainable and value-creating solutions in the area of food and health for the benefit of society. The vision is to make a difference by generating future prosperity through research into food and health. The institute works to prevent disease and promote health, develop new and better food products for a growing population and create sustainable technological solutions, including biosolutions. The institute’s tasks are carried out in interdisciplinary collaboration within e.g. nutrition, chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, epidemiology, modelling, and technology. This is achieved through a strong academic environment of international top class with correspondingly skilled researchers and employees. The Institute employs approximately 390 staff members.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Protein Dynamics at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology
jobs.description:
We are offering a three-year PhD fellowship in protein analysis commencing Feb 1, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  Research group
 This PhD project is a collaborative project between the lab of Professor Petrine Wellendorph (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, specializing in molecular pharmacology, principal supervisor), the Protein Analysis Group of Professor Kasper D. Rand (Department of Pharmacy, specializing in HDX-MS, principal co-supervisor), and Associate Professor Annette E. Langkilde (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, specialist in SAXS, co-supervisor). This interdisciplinary setup uniquely bridges brain mechanisms with protein dynamics and structure, enabling new biological insights and cross-fertilization between fields. The PhD fellowship is funded by a larger project grant from the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

  Project description
 Neuronal signalling underlies every function of the brain, from basic communication to learning and memory. This project focuses on a calcium-sensing protein that plays a central role in these processes. The project will apply in-solution biophysical and analytical methods to explore molecular details of ligand binding on protein dynamics to promote structure-function of the protein and, ultimately, advance drug discovery. As the primary methodology, mass spectrometry to measure the hydrogen/deuterium exchange (HDX-MS) of the protein in solution will be used. The HDX-MS method has emerged as a sensitive and powerful alternative technology to study the conformation of proteins using only small quantities of dilute samples. The project will utilize HDX-MS to analyze the protein in various conformational and activational states and elucidate its interaction with ligands and other proteins. Furthermore, the project will also use classical radioligand binding techniques and state-of-the-art biophysical methods e.g. DSF and SAXS to measure affinity and oligomerization. This combined experimental approach will allow for a detailed analysis of the biophysical, structural, and pharmacological properties of the protein.

  Principal supervisor
 Professor Petrine Wellendorph, Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, e-mail: pw@sund.ku.dk, tel. +45 3533 6397.

  Start
 1. Feb 2027

  Duration
 3 years as a PhD student

  Place of employment
 The Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology will be the primary host, but the project will also be highly integrated with activities at Department of Pharmacy. Both departments offer research-based education and interdisciplinary research that supports the development and understanding of drugs at the highest level for the benefit of society. We work as part of a dynamic academic community of research, education and innovation within the Pharmaceutical Sciences bridging Health Sciences and Life Sciences.

  Information about the primary host Department can be found at www.drug.ku.dk

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences are:

   	
• Carrying through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points 	
• Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team, preferably abroad 	
• Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project 	
• Teaching of undergraduate students in pharmaceutical sciences 	
• Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   PhD Programme description
 The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., pharmaceutical sciences, analytical chemistry, biophysics, biochemistry, or related areas).

  Qualifications
 If you have completed your academic education in Denmark, the admission to the PhD programme requires a relevant Master’s degree (equivalent to 180 ECTS BSc + 120 ECTS MSc).

  If you have an academic education from abroad, you must have either a degree equivalent to a Danish master's degree (180 ETCS + 120 ECTS MSc), or at a minimum, a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) and be academically qualified at master's level.

  As part of the assessment of whether you meet the educational requirements, you must also achieve a positive academic evaluation and be assessed as the best qualified for the position.

  General criteria:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project (see specific qualifications below) 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Previous publications 	
• The grade point average achieved 	
• Other professional activities 	
• A curious mind-set with an overall interest in protein structure-function 	
• Good language skills in English and, preferably, Danish 	
• A collaborative mindset and strong communication skills   Specific criteria:

  The successful candidate will be an experimentally oriented scientist with a primary interest in protein chemistry, structural biology, mass spectrometry and bioanalytical science. A good understanding of biochemistry and pharmacology is also a clear advantage. Preference will be given to applicants with experience in protein chemistry, mass spectrometry and data analysis. Experience with HDX-MS will give the applicant a particularly strong standing. As the project is highly collaborative, we are looking for applicants who are motivated to work across academic research groups and who bring strong interpersonal and communication skills to this kind of setting.

  Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. Associated is also the Department of Pharmacy. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories within molecular pharmacology, protein chemistry and mass spectrometry.

  Terms of employment
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years.

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project to the Graduate School of Health and Medical Sciences.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2025) and www.healthsciences.ku.dk on achieving the degree.

  The PhD student is expected to be affiliated to the graduate programme in pharmaceutical sciences, www.dra.ku.dk

  Salary, pension, and terms of employment are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,800 DKK/Roughly 4,250 EUR (August 2026) plus pension.

  Application procedure
 Your application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking “Apply now” below and must include the following documents in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Certified copy of original Master diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science. Applicants with a Master´s degree from abroad should also enclose a short description of the grading scale used 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Other information to consider: References and recommendations (if possible)   The deadline for applications is 1 November 2026, 23.59 (CET)
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor.

  The assessor makes a non-prioritized assessment of the academic qualifications and experience with respect to the above-mentioned area of research, techniques, skills and other requirements listed in the advertisement.

  Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Questions
 For further information, applicants may contact the principal supervisor Petrine Wellendorph, e-mail:  pw@sund.ku.dk, phone: +45 3533 6397 or PhD coordinator Marianne W. Jørgensen, e-mail: marianne.joergensen@sund.ku.dk, phone: +45 3533 6449.

  General information about PhD studies at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences is available at the Graduate School’s website: https://healthsciences.ku.dk/phd/guidelines/

  For more information on working and living in Denmark visit http://ism.ku.dk (International staff mobility) and https://www.workindenmark.dk

   

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Laboratory technician at DTU Metabolomics Core - DTU Bioengineering
jobs.description:
The DTU Metabolomics Core at DTU Bioengineering, Kgs. Lyngby, is looking for a skilled and motivated Laboratory Technician to join our team of excellent scientists and technicians collaborating on microbial molecules, trying to unravel their importance in nature, and discover how they can benefit humanity in various ways, such as in agriculture, and novel pharmaceuticals.

About the DTU Metabolomics Core
The DTU Metabolomics Core in the Department of Bioengineering is one of a several Core facilities within the Department that supports a wide range of research and teaching. The area in which the Metabolomics Core specializes is in the chemical analysis of small secondary metabolites from microorganisms, such as bacteria, fungi, and microalgae. This analysis is undertaken in our extensive instrument suite (HPLC, LCMS, GCMS, MALDI etc.), a collection of instrumentation that you will work closely with as our new technician.

The primary job areas of responsibility
As Laboratory Technician in the Metabolomics Core, you will play a key role in the day-to-day operation of the facility in close collaboration with the Facility Manager. Your responsibilities will include:

• Operating and maintaining our analytical instrumentation, including high-resolution LC-MS systems (sample preparation, calibration, QC runs, routine troubleshooting and preventive maintenance in cooperation with service engineers)
• Running samples for internal researchers and external contract projects, from sample preparation to data acquisition
• Ordering and managing laboratory supplies, consumables, and chemicals, and keeping the lab stocked and organized
• Maintaining lab standards: cleanliness, safety, waste handling, documentation, and quality control routines
• Supporting users of the facility with practical guidance on sample submission and preparation
• Contributing to the ongoing development of workflows and procedures in the facility
• Supporting students
In addition to this is it expected that you will take part in some Department duties, particularly involving laboratory and chemical safety. This will be done in close collaboration with a team of 4 other technicians working within the same section that hosts the Metabolomics Core.

Qualifications
We expect that you:

• Hold a degree as a laboratory technician (laborant) and/or a BSc/MSc in analytical chemistry, biochemistry, chemical engineering, or a related field
• Have hands-on experience with HPLC instrumentation. Experience with high-resolution MS (e.g., QTOF) is a strong advantage
• Are experienced in routine laboratory work, including sample preparation, solvent handling, and general upkeep of analytical labs
• Have knowledge of Good Laboratory Practice, safety regulations, and documentation standards
• Are structured, detail-oriented, and able to plan your own work independently
• Enjoy collaborating with researchers of different backgrounds and communicating in English (our working language)
• Ideally, have experience with natural products chemistry, and sample preparation
What we offer in return
With this job we offer you an exciting and versatile position in a multicultural, respectful and dynamic research and learning environment with many international employees and students. You will gain hands on experience with a wide variety of different analytical instrumentation and have the freedom to create your own daily agenda by prioritizing your tasks.

You will have:

• A central role in a well-equipped core facility with diverse and exciting projects spanning microbiology, natural products, and industrial collaborations
• Close collaboration with leading research groups at DTU Bioengineering
• A flexible, informal working environment at DTU's Lyngby campus
• Professional development opportunities, including training on new instrumentation and methods
Salary and appointment terms
Salary and appointment terms are in accordance with the OAO-S Joint Agreement and the organization agreement for Office Clerks, Laboratory Technicians and IT staff (HK/stat). In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for clerical employees OR laboratory technicians: https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The appointment is permanent full time. The position starts 1st December 2026 or as soon as possible after.

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 4 November 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Facility Manager, Aaron Andersen by e-mail (ajca@dtu.dk) or by telephone (+45 45 25 61 38). DTU Bioengineering website: https://www.bioengineering.dtu.dk/english.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Department of Biotechnology and Biomedicine (DTU Bioengineering) is an international leader in the areas of biotechnology and biomedicine. Our engineering approach to all aspects of biotechnology and biomedicine positions us as a valuable player with unique competences in a growing bio-based economy and with health systems transforming towards personalized medicine. We have a clear focus on the needs in life science- and biotech industries and point towards innovation, new businesses, and scientific services for the benefit of society. Nice to Have

What We Offer

• Exposure to senior stakeholders and international teams.

About us

Join Dynatest as a Software & Embedded Engineer and help us make every road a safer journey.

About Dynatest Since 1976, Dynatest has been shaping the future of smarter, safer, and more sustainable roads. We develop and manufacture world-leading pavement testing equipment, used by customers across the globe. Our equipment is in high demand, and we are therefore expanding our team with an experienced and multi-skilled Software & Embedded Engineer who can help us bring precision and reliability to every road project.

**Your work at Dynatest

**Based at our headquarter in Ballerup, you will join our growing software team, reporting to the Software Manager. You will work across the full stack—from embedded processors and PLCs, signal processing, communication protocols, and computer vision to higher-level software applications that interact with our machines. You will help define technical solutions and estimates for new hardware and software implementations, develop test procedures and specifications, and provide technical guidance to ensure robust, reliable, and maintainable solutions. The role also includes participation in customer-specific tasks to assess feasibility, identify optimal solutions, estimate costs and implementation effort, and report recommendations to the Software Manager.

As our Software & Embedded Engineer your assignments would be:

• Develop and maintain embedded firmware, PLC software, and supporting applications for pavement testing equipment and related systems

• Design and optimize software architectures, communication interfaces, and existing codebases to ensure performance, reliability, maintainability, and scalability

• Plan, execute, and document testing, validation activities, and software releases to ensure solutions meet technical and quality requirements

• Maintain clear and structured technical documentation covering software design, system changes, engineering decisions, and test results

• Support customer projects through technical clarification, feasibility assessments, solution development, and technical recommendations

• Collaborate across functions while contributing to engineering standards, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement initiatives

Professional qualifications

• Engineering degree in Automation, Electrical, Software, Mechatronics, or similar

• 3+ years of professional experience in software and embedded development

• Experience with several of the following: C, C++, C#, Structured Text (IEC 61131-3), VBA, communication protocols (e.g., TCP/IP, CAN, Modbus), signal processing, computer vision, Git and Jira (or similar)

• Solid problem-solving skills and an analytical, structured approach

• Experience with embedded processors and PLCs; familiarity with industrial sensors/actuators is an advantage

• Proficient in English

**Personal qualifications

**You are independent, self-driven, and take professional pride in your work. You work in a structured and systematic manner, continuously seek improvements, and are able to analyze and assess technical challenges. You understand consequences and dependencies across systems and thrive in collaboration with colleagues and stakeholders.

**Why you should join Dynatest

**We offer an exciting opportunity to work independently in a dynamic and informal environment. At Dynatest, you will be challenged both professionally and personally, with the chance to shape the company’s future and have a real impact on our products and solutions.

You will join a highly skilled team of professionals with deep technical expertise, contributing to maintaining and strengthening Dynatest’s position as the world’s leading provider of pavement testing equipment.

An exciting and independent position in an innovative engineering company with a high technical and professional level.

Dynatest is a growing company, offering excellent opportunities for both professional and personal development. Currently, we employ around 50 people in Ballerup, Denmark, and Florida, USA.

We offer attractive employee benefits, salary according to qualifications, wide-ranging responsibilities, and freedom with accountability.

_

Dynatest value diversity and inclusion. We encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of country of origin, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age._

Dynatest is the pavement industry’s global partner on pavement evaluation solutions. We develop, manufacture, and service equipment and software that defines the industry standard. With more than 40 years of experience, we deliver seamless 360° solutions based on innovative, market-leading expertise. Knowledge is the very backbone of Dynatest, and our know-how is one of our biggest assets. We are passionate about technology and pavement engineering and our employees are some of the most respected and trusted engineers and technicians in the business. In collaboration with our highly skilled distributors, we operate in every corner of the world from our offices and production facilities in Ballerup, Denmark, and Gainesville, Florida, USA.
