FirePoint Rocket Technology is building one of the most unique and strategically important industrial projects in Denmark - a new production facility for solid rocket propellant and advanced defense-tech components. Our ambition is significant: we are scaling from the early operational phase to 200+ employees within the next 18 months.

It is a Danish-based defense technology company, part of the international Fire Point Group — a fast-growing ecosystem born out of Ukraine’s innovation and resilience. The group was founded by engineers and entrepreneurs who, during the first months of the full-scale war, decided to use their expertise to create advanced defense technologies — including long-range drones and precision systems.

Joining FPRT now means becoming part of the core team shaping a new high-tech, safety-critical production environment from the ground up.

They are looking for a Maintenance & Engineering Manager who will establish and execute an absolute, zero-compromise reliability strategy from day one.

The Role

As the Maintenance & Engineering Manager, you are responsible for the operational integrity, availability, and safety of all production assets and process equipment. Manufacturing rocket propellant leaves no room for trial and error—our process equipment must be predictable, fully mastered down to the individual component, and maintained at peak condition.

Reporting directly to the Chief Production Officer (CPO), you will lead the technical team in deep equipment mastery, anticipating service intervals with precision, and proactively replacing high-risk components before failures occur. You will work in close functional alignment with Process Engineering, Manufacturing Automation, EHS, Quality, and Production Planning to ensure seamless, compliant operations.

What You Will Do

1. Production Maintenance Strategy & Asset Management

• Develop and implement a preventive and predictive maintenance strategy for all production equipment, focusing on long-cycle and batch-based processes (mixers, thermal curing ovens, polymerization, climate-controlled chambers) to ensure thermal stability and high uptime.

• Minimize downtime by transitioning from reactive repairs to condition-based monitoring and planned interventions.

• Lead the selection, implementation, and management of a CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) to track work orders, asset history, and maintenance costs.

• Integrate maintenance requirements into the equipment acquisition process alongside QA, establishing preventive risk assessments and managing obsolescence planning.

2. Process Utilities & Production Support Engineering

• Oversee point-of-use process utilities directly feeding production lines, such as process vacuum, specialized process gas loops, and line-dedicated thermal fluids.

• Coordinate with internal and external facility teams on utility drop interfaces to ensure production machinery interface readiness.

3. EHS & Process Safety Compliance

• Enforce strict adherence to EHS standards across all equipment maintenance activities.

• Rigorously execute Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures and "Permit to Work" systems on energetic material processing machinery and hazardous equipment zones.

4. Production Spare Parts & Technical Inventory

• Define critical spare parts strategies for production machinery to balance inventory costs with operational risk mitigation.

• Partner with the Warehouse team to track, store, and preserve technical production spares correctly.

• Monitor market lifecycle status for key equipment components and execute end-of-life obsolescence planning.

5. Team Leadership & Technical Development

• Lead, mentor, and schedule a team of production maintenance technicians and equipment specialists.

• Ensure the team is fully trained in safety protocols (ATEX, energetic materials) and advanced technical troubleshooting.

• Plan technician resources and build mechanical redundancy strategies to protect production during interventions or unplanned events.

6. Production Line CapEx & Commissioning Support

• Support the installation, mechanical integration, and commissioning of new production lines with Process Engineering and Automation.

• Provide early input on machine "serviceability and accessibility" during the design phase to eliminate future shop-floor bottlenecks.

First 90 Days – Expected Outcomes

• Critical spare parts inventory analysis completed and gaps identified.

• Preventative Maintenance (PM) schedule established for all key production assets.

• Maintenance team skills matrix assessed and training plan initiated.

• Design of the “obtain equipment” process and equipment lifecycle framework completed in collaboration with QA.

What We Offer

• A rare career opportunity to lead the engineering and maintenance function for one of Denmark's most unique industrial and defense-tech projects.

• A role where your technical expertise directly determines the reliability and safety of high-stakes, safety-critical production.

• A professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose.

• Brand-new factory & equipment.

• Real authority, Greenfield impact, Zero toxic culture, Mastery over busywork.

• Top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

We Are Looking For

You are a highly structured, disciplined, and hands-on leader who thrives on the shop floor and maintains an absolute zero-compromise approach to equipment safety and operational reliability.

Requirements:

• Education: Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Marine Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Experience: 5+ years of maintenance management experience within heavy industry, chemical processing, pharma, defense, or similar high-safety manufacturing environments.

• Leadership: Proven track record of managing technical teams, scheduling resources, and coordinating external contractors and facility service providers.

• Technical Mastery: Strong working knowledge of mechanical systems (hydraulics, pneumatics, rotating equipment), electrical systems, and industrial automation (PLC, SCADA).

Head of Data Platform – build Gubra’s data foundation from the ground up

Do you want to build the data foundation behind scientific innovation in a growing biotech company? Gubra is looking for a Head of Data Platform to take end-to-end ownership of a new enterprise data platform connecting scientific, operational, and business data across the organisation.

This is a director-level role combining technical ownership, people leadership, and greenfield development. You will shape the architecture and roadmap, build the team around the platform, and remain close enough to the technology to take part in key technical decisions.

The ambition is to create a scalable data foundation that supports research, laboratory operations, machine learning, and selected business functions across Gubra.

Build the platform – and the team around it

Gubra is investing in its digital and data foundation, and you will join at an early stage.

As Head of Data Platform, you will lead the design, implementation, and operation of the platform, built around AWS and Databricks. You will work across architecture, data pipelines, reusable data products, governance, and security while translating scientific and business needs into technical priorities.

At the same time, you will build and lead the data engineering team. Two Data Engineers are planned to join, an external Data Architect is already supporting the initial design, and the team is expected to grow further. You will report directly to the CTO and become part of the CTO’s leadership team.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Leading the design and development of a scalable and secure enterprise data platform

• Building reliable data pipelines and reusable data products for scientists, ML teams, engineers, and business users

• Defining the platform roadmap and driving key architectural and technical decisions

• Establishing data governance, security, access control, and documentation standards

• Building, mentoring, and developing the data engineering team

• Working closely with stakeholders across research, laboratory operations, software engineering, and the wider business.

Who are you?

You have a strong background in data engineering, analytics, or data platforms and experience leading both people and technical delivery. You combine leadership with enough technical depth to challenge architectural decisions and engage credibly with engineers.

You bring extensive experience with AWS and Databricks and have designed scalable, secure, and governed data solutions before. Experience with lakehouse architecture, data mesh, medallion architecture, Airflow, Delta Lake, or Unity Catalog is an advantage.

Experience from biotech, pharma, life sciences, or another research-intensive environment is beneficial but not required. The same applies to experience with regulated environments and GxP.

Personally, you are a pragmatic and collaborative leader who can create a clear direction, bring stakeholders and employees with you, and balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

About Gubra

Gubra is a purpose-driven biotech company where technology, data, and science come together to create life-changing therapies. The organisation combines Biotech, CRO, and Venture activities and brings scientists, engineers, and business teams together across the organisation.

Digital, Data & IT is strengthening the foundation beneath this work by connecting scientific, operational, and business data and enabling advanced analytics and machine learning.

The position is based at Gubra in Hørsholm, Denmark.

If you have any questions about the position, you are always welcome to contact Kathrine Schlegel Rasmussen at ksr@capaxrecruitment.com.

Capax Recruitment manages the recruitment process on behalf of Gubra.

Principal Enterprise Architect – shape the technology choices behind Gubra’s growth

Build, buy, integrate or simplify? As Gubra grows, so does the number and complexity of technology decisions across the organisation. Gubra is therefore looking for a Principal Enterprise Architect who can bring direction and coherence to its technology landscape.

In this newly established role, you will become a close architectural partner to the CTO and work across business, science, and technology. Your job is not to own one particular platform or technology. Instead, you will help Gubra make the right technology choices across scientific systems, enterprise applications, ERP, data, AI, cloud, and integrations.

Turn complex needs into pragmatic technology choices

As Principal Enterprise Architect, you will work closely with business leaders, scientists, Product Managers, and technology teams to understand what they are trying to achieve before translating those needs into architecture options and recommendations.

That could mean assessing whether to build a capability internally or invest in a SaaS platform. Another could involve defining how a new solution should integrate with Gubra’s existing landscape, exploring an AI opportunity, or helping a new venture establish a technology foundation that works today without limiting it tomorrow.

You will also help establish the architecture principles, standards, and guardrails that create consistency across Gubra. The ambition is not architecture for architecture’s sake, but enough direction to enable teams to make better decisions independently.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Advising on technology choices across enterprise applications, ERP, data, AI, cloud, security, and integrations

• Evaluating COTS and SaaS solutions and supporting build-vs-buy decisions

• Defining and evolving architecture principles, standards, and reusable patterns

• Translating business and scientific needs into pragmatic architecture recommendations

• Working with Software, Data, ML, Infrastructure, and Security teams to ensure decisions are technically viable

• Identifying opportunities for AI and modernisation across the organisation

• Following developments within AI, cloud, data sovereignty, and emerging technologies.

An architect who asks the right questions

You bring 5+ years of relevant experience as an Enterprise Architect, Principal Architect, or in a similar role, with broad experience across enterprise applications, data, cloud, integrations, security, and modern software platforms.

You understand ERP and enterprise business systems and how they connect to a broader technology landscape. You are comfortable discussing APIs, integration patterns, identity, security, cloud architecture, and data interoperability, and you have experience assessing COTS or SaaS platforms and making technology recommendations.

You also understand modern AI architecture and how AI capabilities can become part of real business workflows. Experience from pharma, biotech, life sciences, drug discovery, or another R&D-intensive environment is relevant, while experience with GxP is an advantage.

Just as importantly, you are curious enough to challenge the problem before proposing the solution. You can discuss opportunities with business leaders and scientists and then go into sufficient technical depth with engineers to make decisions credible and implementable.

You are comfortable influencing across teams without formal authority and know when architecture adds value – and when it simply adds another layer of complexity.

Where science, business and technology meet

Gubra is a purpose-driven biotech company where technology, data, and science come together to create life-changing therapies. Its activities span Biotech, CRO, and Venture, creating a technology landscape that needs to support different business models, scientific disciplines, and ways of working.

Digital, Data & IT works across these areas to create the digital foundation supporting both scientific innovation and business operations. As Principal Enterprise Architect, you will have a broad view across that landscape and help ensure technology decisions support where Gubra is going next.

The position is based at Gubra in Hørsholm, Denmark and reports directly to the CTO.

jobs.occupation: Computational and Data Staff Scientist Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design
jobs.description:
We seek an experienced, highly motivated, and independent computational and data scientist to support the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design (CPD), University of Copenhagen (UCPH). The post suits someone with experience in computational chemistry, biology, and/or structural biology, as well as managing big data. This is a full-time position, starting 1 February 2027 and employment through 31 July 2032.

  Our research
 The CPD is a new initiative at UCPH. It is a multidisciplinary centre that works across the university—notably with the Departments of Biology, Drug Design and Pharmacology, Chemistry, and Computer Science—and with national and international academic and industrial partners. CPD is funded by an initial grant of 700M DKK for seven years from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. At capacity, the CPD is expected to have ≈8 research groups, ≈80 researchers, and support staff. Research will encompass the growing protein design landscape with computational, experimental, applied and hybrid projects.

  The CPD's vision and mission are to accelerate protein design by deepening understanding of sequence-to-structure/function relationships in proteins, and to train the next generation of protein scientists to apply protein-design approaches and methods to a diverse array of fundamental and real-world challenges.  

  CPD research is broadly organised into three themes: Programmable De Novo Protein Design, aimed at improving methods for protein design by combining rational, physics-based and AI-based approaches; Contextualised Protein Design, that is, designing proteins that are fit for purpose such as working directly and optimally in cells, chemical reactors, etc; and Biodesign for Sustainability and Healthcare, for instance working with biotech and industry to deliver synthetic proteins to address grand challenges in these areas.

  Data science at CPD: Increasingly, modern protein science is about data: collecting it, organising it, analysing it, and learning from it to build a deeper understanding of how proteins fold and function. Protein design is no different. Indeed, through the application of generative AI, it is at the leading edge of the confluence of data science and protein science. To coordinate this in the CPD, we are looking for someone experienced in and excited about working at this interface.

  Further information on the CPD see: cpd.ku.dk.

  Learn more about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, https://drug.ku.dk/

  Your job
 Specifically, we seek a talented computational and data scientist and team player to help develop research infrastructure, including hardware and computational tools, to advance the CPD’s research and mission. The successful candidate will join a growing multidisciplinary team to help collect, organise, analyse, and exploit data from computationally designed protein sequences and structural models, through protein expression levels, and onto a wide range of experimental structure-function studies. A key part of the role will be integrating into the wider team and working collaboratively with CPD researchers, rather than simply providing a data-management service. For example, we anticipate that the successful candidate would assist with and lead on various projects with CPD researchers to develop robust, reliable, and scalable data and computational tools to enable the very best protein design.

  Key responsibilities will include

   	
• Helping establish CPD's computational infrastructure to provide computing and data management for its researchers 	
• Developing automated pipelines that convert raw instrument output files directly into data plots suitable for analysis, saving time and resources across the research pipeline 	
• Collecting data and generating databases of designed proteins, e.g., constructs, sequences, models, and biophysical data (LIMS) 	
• Assisting in the development of new predictive models based on the gathered experimental and computational data using machine learning methods 	
• Being responsible for data management plans at the CPD and coordinating these plans with the host departments 	
• Related to the above, managing (i.e., best practice in collecting, organising, accessing) data generated by computational protein design workflows and by the CPD’s Protein Biophysics Facility 	
• Advising and training CPD scientists in creating and analysing large computational datasets, linking their experimental data and computational data to extract key information, and managing their computational protein design pipelines 	
• Contributing to, and where appropriate leading, grant applications for and publications from CPD research projects 	
• Teaching appropriate aspects of the above on CPD Master’s and PhD courses 	
• Serving as the primary technical bridge between the CPD and central KU IT to set up CPD’s computing systems in close collaboration with KU IT and establish internal data processing environments   Qualifications and expectations
 To succeed in this role, we anticipate that your areas of expertise could include one or more of the following:

   	
• Computational protein modelling and, ideally, design 	
• Protein or biomolecular sequence data and analysis 	
• Collection, manipulation and use of data from protein biophysics and structural biology 	
• Use and understanding of modern biomolecular statistical data analysis, including ML and AI methods, and generative AI for protein modelling and design 	
• Experience of establishing computational infrastructures for the above   Essential experience and skills

   	
• A PhD in bioinformatics, data science or a related domain, e.g. computational/structural biology 	
• Excellent knowledge of scientific computing and coding languages, e.g., Python 	
• Documented experience (e.g., scientific publications) in machine learning, scientific computing, and similar 	
• An active interest in protein design, engineering, and structure  	
• A proven ability to work with others on challenging multidisciplinary problems 	
• A team player keen on collaborating with researchers from different backgrounds and who is service-minded with clear organisational, communication, and networking skills. 	
• Excellent skills in written and spoken English   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Knowledge of experimental protein science, for example, biophysical methods and/or structural biology 	
• Experience in computational molecular/structural biology   Place of employment
 The place of employment is at the NNF Center for Protein Design, located at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative, stimulating working conditions in a dynamic, international research environment.

  Salary and terms of employment
 The employment is a full-time (37 hours/week) position with a fixed-term until 31 July 2032. The starting date will be 1 February 2027.

  Depending on qualifications the position will take place as Special Consultant or Senior Consultant in accordance with the Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning Academics in the state sector concluded between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. The monthly salary will be based on the number of years of work experience (seniority), with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experience and qualifications. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact Center Manager Gretchen Repasky, Gretchen.repasky@bio.ku.dk.

  Application
 Your application should be in English and include:

   	
• A cover letter outlining your fit to the role and motivation for applying (max. one page). 	
• Curriculum Vitae (incl. the names of two referees) (max. two pages)  	
• List of publications including preprints (no limit, but do not include copies of the papers) 	
• A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below.

  Application deadline: 8 November 2026

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not meet the above requirements.

  The University wishes to reflect the diversity of the surrounding society and encourages all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.
 The University of Copenhagen has established a new shared administrative organizational structure, which is currently being implemented. This entails ongoing changes and the development of, among other things, workflows and interfaces for collaboration. 

  As part of the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU) and among Europe’s top-ranking universities, the University of Copenhagen promotes research and teaching to the highest international standard. Rich in tradition and modern in outlook, the University gives students and staff the opportunity to cultivate their talent in an ambitious and informal environment. An effective organisation – with good working conditions and a collaborative work culture – creates the ideal framework for a successful academic career.

jobs.occupation: 3 Postdoc positions within forest microbiome assisted afforestation
jobs.employer_name: KU - SCIENCE - IGN frb campus omr. 3
jobs.description:
Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management and Department of Biology, invites applicants for three two-year Postdoc positions within forest microbiome manipulation. The positions are part of the project “MycoForest - Stimulating Forest carbon uptake and storage by mycorrhizal inoculation”, which is financed under the Innomission partnership INNO-CCUS by Innovation Fund Denmark.
 
 Start date is 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The project
 The soil microbiome plays a crucial role in soil- and ecosystem functioning including ecosystem carbon sequestration and support of plant nutrient acquisition.
 
 Denmark is devoted to become carbon neutral by 2045/2050, a goal involving a significant role for biological carbon sequestration and storage. A part of the Danish strategy to reach carbon neutrality is to afforest former agricultural land thereby increasing biological ecosystem carbon capture and storage. However, agricultural soils do not harbor an optimal microbiome for initial tree growth and forest ecosystem development. This may lead to increased mortality, reduced tree growth and slower development of forest soil functions and ultimately non-optimal carbon capture, especially in the early stages of afforestation.
 
 Therefore, the MycoForest project aims to manipulate and assist the microbiome of agricultural soils through mycorrhizal inoculation as an integrated part of tree planting to stimulate tree growth and carbon sequestration. Therefore, MycoForest at University of Copenhagen is hiring three postdocs to become part of this novel journey towards increased biological carbon sequestration and to play key roles in the scientific investigations.
 
 Each of the three postdocs will cover one of three distinct areas of fundamental importance to understand and document the role of the microbiome in afforestation.
 
 The three key areas are:

   	
• Microbial and mycorrhizal fungal development 	
• Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics 	
• Tree survival and growth, and carbon uptake   
 The studies will involve controlled greenhouse as well as field scale experiments, and the three postdocs will each be responsible for one of the three specific parts of the project. At the same time, they will be closely linked to each other through tight collaboration on establishment and sampling of the afforestation experiment. The postdoc positions will start as soon as possible and will run for 2 years. For the requirements of the specific postdocs, please see the descriptions below.
 
 Contact: Specific questions for each of the postdocs, please see below. For general MycoForest questions, please contact Claus Beier, cbe@ign.ku.dk.
 
 Postdoc 1 – Soil microbial development after mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will oversee the formulation and addition of fungal or other types of inoculums and will follow and quantify the mycorrhizal fungal colonization of seedlings, root and soil. Experimentation will be both in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions and in the field. Colonization will be followed in different soils and host trees with a combination of classical microscopic techniques and novel molecular methods. The studies aim to document successful establishment of mycorrhizal fungi within the indigenous communities.
 
 Therefore, we are looking for candidates with specific knowledge and hands-on with:

   	
• Fungi in general including mycorrhizal fungi, preferentially ectomycorrhiza 	
• Field experience in general, handling and sorting soils and roots in specific 	
• Microscopy, especially stereo microscopy of roots 	
• DNA extraction og plants and soil and PCR optimizations including qPCR 	
• Bioinformatics and statistical analysis of meta-barcoding datasets   
 The post doc will work closely together with PD 2 and 3 for plant and soil responses to inoculations.
 
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Rasmus Kjøller, Department of Biology, rasmusk@bio.ku.dk, Phone: +45 35322311
 
 Postdoc 2 – Soil functioning and soil carbon dynamics in response to mycorrhizal inoculation
 The post doc will study effects of inoculation in different soil types and tree species on soil carbon processes including formation of persistent SOC fractions.  The postdoc will study soil carbon dynamics in mesocosm/greenhouse conditions in close cooperation with postdoc 1 and in field experimental conditions in cooperation with postdoc 3. The project will address how inoculation and changes in the mycorrhizal community composition will affect soil carbon sequestration processes in post-agricultural soils. The studies will shed light on the extent to which inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil will change the soil C input quantity and quality from roots and microbial necromass, eventually enhancing accumulation of persistent forms of SOC. 
 
 We are looking for a candidate with a PhD in the fields of soil science and organic matter studies, soil ecology and biogeochemistry. Previous experience with plant-soil interactions in field, mesocosm and laboratory experiments using chemical soil analyses including soil organic carbon (organic matter fractionation and biomarkers targeting microbial and plant origin of organic matter), carbon isotopes, roots, and microbial taxonomic and functional community composition will be considered a plus.
 
 Principal supervisor is Professor Lars Vesterdal, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, lv@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 61670865
 
 Postdoc 3 – Tree responses to mycorrhiza inoculation
 The postdoc will establish and follow field experiments in practical afforestation sites and monitor plant responses such as growth and survival, mycorrhizal colonization, and plant community development.
 
 The studies will address the potential of inoculation with forest-associated mycorrhiza and forest soil to stimulate survival, growth and carbon draw down of forest trees and communities including the role of tree species and soil type interactions. 
 
 We are looking for highly motivated candidates with a PhD in plant or forestry science and interest and experience in:

   	
• Afforestation, forestry and forest ecology 	
• Design and analysis of experiments 	
• Field work and practical application of technology in land management    
 Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Niclas Scott Bentsen, Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, nb@ign.ku.dk, Phone: +45 20206318.
 
 General qualifications
 Apart from the specific qualifications and interests listed above, we look for candidates with general competences in:

   	
• Driver license (mandatory) 	
• Handling of plants and soil 	
• Organizing and conducting field sampling 	
• Data management 	
• Statistics 	
• Scientific writing and publishing   
 Our groups and research – and what do we offer?
 The positions are located in three different groups at the university.
 
 Postdoc 1 is with Department of Biology, Fungal Ecology lab within Section of Terrestrial Ecology. The group works with/focuses on mycorrhizal fungal communities and their impact on ecosystem processes and plant health. We apply molecular markers to disentangle these otherwise invisible fungal populations and communities associated with plants and soil. Besides molecular markers, we also apply biochemical markers as well as classic microscopy and microbiological culturing of fungi. Another methodological strongpoint is various mesh-enclosure techniques to study and compartmentalize both the function and community composition of mycorrhizal fungal mycelia in soil.
 
 Postdoc 2 and 3 are with Department of Geosciences and Natural Resource Management, one in the Biogeochemistry group and one in the Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group. In the Biogeochemistry Group we are dedicated to improving the understanding of ecosystem functioning with particular focus on how ecosystems will respond to environmental changes and to management actions. We quantify the pools and fluxes of matter in semi-natural and managed ecosystems and measure the processes related to input and output fluxes in control of soil C stocks to answer questions such as “Can we sequester C in soils by afforestation of cropland soils, and how does this interact with the soil fauna and microbes when using certain tree species or tree species mixtures?” The Silviculture, Trees and Bioresources group encompas expertise in forestry, ecological restoration, growth modelling and systems analysis. The group is dedicated to advance the understanding, development, and management of forest ecosystems to support a wide range of ecosystem services, including carbon storage, material and energy provision, groundwater regulation, and biodiversity conservation.
 
 Department of Biology is located at Norre Campus and Department of Geosciences on Frederiksberg Campus, close to central Copenhagen. The departments offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environments. The departments are planning to increase their focus on the climate change mitigation potential of forests in upcoming projects. We therefore welcome applications from candidates with a broader interest in the intersection of forests, forest-based climate solutions, biosphere-atmosphere interaction, and related themes.
 
 Responsibilities and tasks

   	
• Carry out independent research projects under the PI’s supervision and in close collaboration with the other PostDocs and researchers within the MycoForest project. 	
• Report and disseminate the periodic progress and results 	
• Take part in relevant teaching activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at relevant journals 	
• Actively take part in the research environments at the departments, sections and within the project.   
 We are looking for the following further qualifications:

   	
• Strong ability to interpret data and think analytically, critically, and conceptually. 	
• Strong social competence including interpersonal skills, teamwork and networking ability, and presentation skills 	
• Strong personal competence including autonomy, goal-oriented mind-set, planning/organizing/prioritizing, perseverance, problem-solving skills 	
• General personal leadership skills including ability to translate long-term goals to daily work situations (strategic time managing); be flexible to adjust one’s own behavior and thinking according to the (relevant/local) context so as to attain the desired goals (learning ability) 	
• Good language skills and fluency in English   
 Terms of employment
 Employment is full-time and for 2 years.
 
 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.
 
 Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.
 
 Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.
 
 You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).
 
 Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and indicate which of the 3 positions you are applying for.
 
 The application is submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.
 
 Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) – please relate how the above required abilities are represented in your past work experiences 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor’s or master’s and PhD and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list 	
• Reference letters (if available)   
 Application deadline:
 The deadline for applications is 29 October 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.
 
 The further process
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.
 
 The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.
 
 Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in week 49-50 2026.
 
 Applicants must be prepared for further security screening related to international research collaborations as part of the recruitment process, when UCPH considers it appropriate from a holistic consideration
 
 Questions
 For specific information about the Postdoc position, please contact the principal supervisor.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Sustainable Indoor Solar Cells for Ambient Light Energy Harvesting in IoT Applications - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
Are you interested in developing thin-film solar cells designed to operate efficiently under indoor lighting and thereby contributing to the green transition? 

At DTU Electro, you will have the opportunity to break new ground by harvesting energy from ambient light and help pave the way towards sustainable technologies.

The Thin-Film Photovoltaics Group at DTU Electro is seeking candidates for a PhD Scholarship focused on the development and characterization of highly efficient Sb₂S₃ solar cells. You will investigate materials, interfaces, and device architectures to understand and overcome the fundamental limitations of photovoltaic performance under low-light conditions.

The position is offered within the framework of DTU’s Alliances and Strategic Partnerships with Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech), Estonia. You will be part of an international research collaboration combining thin-film synthesis, solar-cell fabrication, advanced optoelectronic and defect characterization, and device testing under realistic illumination conditions. As part of the PhD project, you will undertake a research stay at TalTech and work closely with researchers from both universities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project focuses on developing high-efficiency Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells for indoor energy harvesting. The project will investigate how material properties, interfaces, and device architecture influence charge transport, recombination, and voltage losses under low-intensity illumination. The overall objective is to develop solar cells optimized for indoor light and demonstrate series-connected mini-modules capable of powering battery-free IoT devices.

Your primary responsibilities include:

• Develop and optimize Sb₂S₃ thin-film solar cells by engineering device architectures and interfaces to enhance charge collection while minimizing recombination and voltage losses under indoor illumination.
• Characterize solar cells under different LED spectra, light intensities, and illumination conditions relevant to realistic indoor environments.
• Investigate defect states, interface recombination, and open-circuit voltage losses, including advanced electrical characterization during a research stay at TalTech.
• Develop and characterize series-connected indoor photovoltaic mini-modules for battery-free IoT applications.
• Supervise and contribute to MSc/BSc student projects.
• Document and disseminate the research through scientific publications and international conference contributions
You should have a strong academic background in physics, chemistry, materials science, nanotechnology, or a related field. Prior knowledge of semiconductor physics and photovoltaics, and experience with thin-film materials, solar-cell fabrication, optoelectronic characterization, or indoor photovoltaics, would be particularly valuable.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the candidates will be made by Senior Researcher Stela Canulescu. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms. 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is the 1 February 2027. The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from the Senior Researcher Stela Canulescu, email stec@dtu.dk.

You can read more about the Department of Electrical and Photonics Engineering at www.electro.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Electro 
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.description:
A three-year position as a Postdoctoral researcher is now available at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. The Postdoc’s employment is expected to start on 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  About the Center

  You will be employed at the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, which aims to build a strong scientific foundation for understanding and acting on complex public-health challenges. The Center leverages multi-layered nationwide social and health data combined with an interdisciplinary fusion of methods spanning data science, epidemiology, ethnography, econometrics, and systems science. Our research focuses on the complex interplay of health, social, and environmental factors that shape individuals, families, and networks over time. We emphasise interdisciplinary collaboration, offering you an opportunity to actively engage as a collaborative partner in different projects depending on your interests and expertise. Learn more about the Center and our research, vision, and values here.

  About the Department 

  The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

  About the position 

  The position will be nested within the Child Health group at the Center, where we advance knowledge through a combination of research activities that leverage the Center’s data infrastructures and methodological expertise, and engagement with policymakers and practitioners. The Center has developed a strategic partnership with a Danish municipality – the Thriving Communities Lab – which offers a platform for connecting the scientific activities at the Center with real-world health promotion efforts. The focus of this partnership is to enhance the conditions for adolescents to thrive through a dynamic learning process that involves professionals across sectors in the municipality, the local government, and researchers, over a period of several years. One question we will explore is whether computational modelling can usefully bring together local knowledge, scientific evidence, the Center’s data resources, and insights emerging from practical interventions, and so strengthen this learning process. Your work as a postdoc will be anchored around this question. Our vision at the Center is to build on this experience to engage with more municipalities over time, addressing a variety of complex health challenges.

  As a Postdoc, your responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

   	
• Spearheading the development of a decision-support/scenario exploration tool that offers policymakers a way to visualize and simulate systemic effects of social investments and programmes, in close collaboration with our partners in the Thriving Communities Lab. 	
• Engaging with municipal collaborators within the Thriving Communities Lab to ensure a dynamic interplay between research activities and local efforts. 	
• Exploring multi-layered life-course data from the Danish Life Course Cohort (DANLIFE), augmented with local data from the municipal partner, to map the interrelated landscape of well-being among adolescents. 	
• Contributing to scientific publications and engage in the dissemination of research results related to these topics. 	
• Collaborating with researchers in the Center on interdisciplinary projects. 	
• Participating in research-based teaching at the Department of Public Health. 	
• Actively contributing to the development of organisational elements within the Center, such as network activities, website, outreach initiatives, social engagements, scientific meetings, and more.   Profile 

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic researcher with the following competences and experience:

   	
• You have a PhD degree in social science, economics, epidemiology, data science, complexity science, computational science, or other related sciences. 	
• You have experience with system dynamics modelling. Experience with agent-based modelling, social return on investment analysis or other analytical frameworks to model social and systemic impacts of social policies and programmes would also be an advantage. 	
• Experience working with Danish register data is an advantage. 	
• You are motivated to engage in participatory processes with practitioners and policymakers, and to collaborate with a variety of stakeholders to foster change. 	
• You have an active interest in complex-systems science applied to public health and epidemiology. 	
• You have proficient communication skills and a proven ability to work in interdisciplinary teams. 	
• You have excellent English skills, both written and spoken. 	
• Danish language skills are an advantage but not essential.   Place of employment

  The place of employment is the Copenhagen Health Complexity Center, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen, next to the Lakes in Central Copenhagen.

  Terms of employment 
 The average working hours are 37 hours per week. The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is February 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or another relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 35,000 DKK/approx. 4,700 EUR (October 2021 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 17.1 % to your pension fund. Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark for the past 10 years. The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Further information

  For specific information about the position, please contact the Associate professor Christopher Jamil de Montgomery: cmon@sund.ku.dk

  Applicants may find the following links useful:

   	
• Copenhagen Health Complexity Center: https://healthcomplex.dk/ 	
• University of Copenhagen: http://ku.dk/english/ 	
• Department of Public Health: http://publichealth.ku.dk/ 	
• International Staff Mobility: https://ism.ku.dk/   Application process

  Your application should be written in English and must include the following documents – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter of motivation (max 1 page). Please briefly describe your previous research experience and interests as well as what attracts you to the position. 	
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 	
• Certified/signed copies of
 	a) PhD certificate (if the PhD has not been completed, a written statement from the applicant’s supervisor will suffice)
 	b) Master of Science certificate. 	
• A research plan (max 2 pages) outlining your ideas for how a decision-support/scenario exploration tool could be developed, drawing on system dynamics modelling or other analytical frameworks suitable for modelling dynamic effects of social policies and programmes.   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. Only online applications will be considered.

  After the expiration of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager will select applicants for assessment based on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been advanced for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment has been completed, each applicant is given an opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant themselves.

  You can read more about the recruitment process here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  Application deadline 

  Deadline for applications: 31/10/2026 23.59pm CET 

  We reserve the right to reject material received after the deadline, and to reject applications that do not meet the abovementioned requirements.

  Interviews are expected to be held in week 47-48.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their personal background.

Millions of people wear Pandora to say something about themselves. Behind that sit two of the biggest levers on the company's results: a marketing investment among the largest in the industry, and the profitability of the jewellery itself.

You will build and run its engine keeping the Product and Marketing finance team connected to the financial heartbeat of the company: one planning calendar, one reporting standard, cost control across worldwide envelopes, and an automation toolchain that makes reporting produce itself. You are shaping how this team runs, and the role grows as the toolchain does. As we build the team capabilities, we continue delivering results every quarter, budget every autumn, and the value optimization discipline that funds our growth.

This is a role for someone who is a pace setter, taking real pride in a rhythm that builds credibility, and who wants to modernize how the work gets done.

What you will do

• Own the Product and Marketing financial planning calendar end to end: budget and long-range planning milestones, forecast cycles, month-end and performance review inputs, orchestrating and collaborating so that every corporate deadline is met reliably and consistently.

• Own the reporting catalogue with clear service levels, and build the automation toolchain that produces the recurring suite, retiring manual production as you go.

• Run the functional line into our Global Business Services team: process catalogue, quality, capacity, one blueprint.

• Run cost control for the CMO, CPO and Global Office envelopes as a trusted, independent service.

• Front the team's interface to FP&A and the CFO office, reconciling to one set of definitions.

What is needed to succeed

• 7-10 years in financial planning, reporting or control; you have run a planning calendar or close process end to end.

• Experience building or running a shared-services or offshore interface, with the catalogue and quality rhythm to show for it.

• At least one recurring reporting process you automated, with the manual version retired, and genuine energy for doing it again at scale.

• The independence to hold deadlines, definitions and spend hygiene, including with colleagues more senior than you.

Who you are

• A self-starter: you see the missing process and build it before anyone asks.

• You develop and defend your own point of view: the calendar and the definitions are yours, and you can say no and make it stick, respectfully.

• You believe finance is a strategic copilot to the business, and control done well, an essential guardrail to earn investors' and consumers' trust.

• You can have difficult conversations respectfully, and colleagues trust you more because of them.

• Consumer-centric at heart: you keep the numbers connected to the people who wear the jewellery.

• People-first and collaborator: you make a shared-services team feel like one team, across sites and time zones.

Reporting into the Sr Director, Global Product & Marketing Finance, you will be the backbone of a small, senior team with a mandate from the top of the company, and you contribute by making excellent work systematic.

Additional information

Global Career Band 4B - Manager.

Hybrid Working Flexibility – 3 days in office per week

Location Copenhagen; Global scope.

English is our working language; Danish is not required.

Did we get your attention?

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site www.pandoragroup.com.

Icing on the cake

You will be working out of our beautiful Head Office in Copenhagen V, established in 2016 and designed to unite and inspire our teams. Besides our beautiful interior design, we are also proud of our LEED Gold Certification for Energy and Environmental Design. This means that we use as few natural resources as possible and that we use them with respect. The result is a professional and dynamic space that is unique, comfortable and inspirational – and delivers a true Pandora experience to anyone who works here or comes to visit.

About Pandora

Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

At Pandora, we believe that creating an inclusive and diverse workplace and reflecting societal diversity in our customer engagement is essential to delivering on our company purpose: to give a voice to people’s loves. We dedicate ourselves to fostering, cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and diversity where everyone feels respected and valued.

Are you passionate about supply chain planning within a End-2-End perspective and motivated by making operational decisions that create value across the entire value chain? Do you thrive in a collaborative environment where customer focus, stakeholder management and data-driven decision-making go hand in hand? Then this could be the opportunity for you. We are looking for an Operational Network Planner for CBP Rødkærsbro cluster.

The position is based at our HQ Viby J, but expect visits to our sites in Rødkærsbro and Branderup.

“As part of the team, you will help plan the supply of mozzarella and pizza topping products for customers around the world, working closely with stakeholders across Supply Chain, Commercial and Production. If you are motivated by operational planning and making an impact in a global supply chain, you could be the candidate we’re looking for.” says Susanne Grundt Gotfredsen, Supply Chain Network Planning Manager.

Read more about Supply Chain at Arla here Inside Arla.

How you will make an impact

As an Operational Network Planner, you will play a key role within the Sales & Operations Execution (S&OE) horizon, ensuring that we deliver excellent service levels to customers while balancing production capacity, inventory levels and waste reduction across markets and warehouses.

You will join a highly collaborative planning team consisting of four Site Schedulers, two Operational Network Planners and one Component Planner, supporting two production sites. Working closely with colleagues across Supply Chain, Commercial and Production, you will help drive operational decisions that create value across the end-to-end supply chain.

Your key responsibilities will include

• Optimizing supply chain performance through root cause analysis and data-driven decisions.

• Monitoring relevant KPIs and implementing corrective actions to achieve targets.

• Conducting scenario planning to mitigate availability risks, reduce waste, and assess the impact of demand fluctuations on finished goods.

• Escalating unresolved short-term imbalances to global or local S&OE executive forums and key stakeholders.

• Leading proactive dialogue between Supply Chain and Commercial teams to solve complex issues.

• Identifying and contributing to optimization initiatives from an end-to-end perspective.

What will make you successful

You are an ambitious and structured professional with strong analytical skills and the ability to work across multiple functions. You thrive on collaboration and have a natural ability to engage with stakeholders from across the business.

You are motivated by change and actively contribute to the continuous improvement of ways of working and collaboration.

We imagine you

• Hold a relevant Bachelor's or Master's degree within Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Engineering, Business or a related field.

• Have 2-5 years of experience within supply chain planning, logistics or manufacturing, preferably working within S&OE or short-term planning horizons.

• Are comfortable analysing data and using insights to support operational decisions.

• Communicate clearly and confidently with stakeholders across different functions and organisational levels.

• Are curious, proactive and motivated by continuous improvement and optimisation.

What do we offer?

An inclusive corporate culture that creates job satisfaction is important to us, and we prioritize giving our employees good development opportunities. We are looking for you who want to grow with us at Arla Foods!

Arla Foods has a collective agreement and always offers good and competitive working conditions. In addition, we have a high priority on safety and the working environment.

About Arla

We are Arla – a European dairy cooperative with over 19,000 employees and around 8,600 farmers. Our cooperative model creates a unique closeness to our farmers – the owners of Arla – and motivates us every day to deliver the very best for our farmers, colleagues, our milk, our consumers, and our environment.

Would you like to join us?

Please apply as soon as possible. We process applications on a continuous basis and close the position once the right candidate has been found.

If you have any questions, please contact Supply Chain Network Planning Manager, Susanne Grundt Gotfredsen at +45 91 31 40 19.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

Who you are

Do you take pride in working in the early morning? If so, you are a good match as a forklift driver for our goods receiving department. When IKEA opens at 10 AM, it is important we have replenished the shelves so we are ready for our customers.

In addition we expect that you:

As a forklift driver you play an important part for IKEA’s customers and sales, because you and your team make sure our home furnishing solutions and accessories are always accessible for our customers. Every day is fast paced because we work with a sharp deadline at 10 AM, when the store opens.

Senior Hydraulic Engineer (Team Lead) – Heavy Industry Brake Systems

Location: Vejstrup, Denmark · Department: Engineering

Are you ready to lead innovation in hydraulic systems? Join the global leader in braking solutions and help shape high‑performance systems for wind, oil & gas, mining, and other demanding sectors. This is a hands‑on leadership role where you combine sound engineering judgment with practical execution—collaborating across teams and engaging directly with customers and suppliers.

Your impact

• Lead end‑to‑end hydraulic design and development for next‑generation brake systems.

• Translate customer needs into robust technical solutions that meet global standards and deliver measurable performance.

• Strengthen knowledge sharing and standardization to improve quality, speed, and efficiency across projects.

What you’ll do

• Serve as the subject‑matter expert for hydraulic systems—owning architecture, design calculations, and component selection.

• Prepare technical layouts, schematics, and proposals to support Sales and Marketing.

• Provide technical and commercial support (cost estimates, business cases) for bidding activities.

• Plan and execute system testing, inspection, and validation to ensure reliability and safety.

• Lead root‑cause analyses and support quality claims and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Act as technical liaison with customers and suppliers throughout project execution, including site visits.

• Drive development projects that advance our brake solutions and set new benchmarks.

• Capture, structure, and standardize technical knowledge to enhance processes and tools.

What you bring

• Experience: Solid background in hydraulic engineering within wind, oil & gas, mining, marine, or similar heavy industries (typically 10+ years; we welcome capable candidates with equivalent experience and growth potential).

• Skills: Strong theoretical foundation paired with practical, hands‑on problem solving.

• Tools & systems: Proficiency with MS Office; experience with ERP systems (we use AXAPTA, other platforms are welcome).

• Ways of working: Familiarity with stage‑gate project models; experience with Wrike or similar tools is an advantage.

• Mindset: Organized, proactive, and collaborative—able to work independently while enabling the team.

• Quality & safety: Experience in ISO‑certified environments and a safety‑first approach.

• Language & travel: Fluent in English (spoken and written); Danish is a plus. Willing to travel ~30 days per year.

Why join us

• Work on innovative, high‑impact projects shaping the future of hydraulic brake systems.

• Be part of a supportive, collaborative culture that values sharing knowledge and continuous improvement.

• Great opportunities for personal and professional growth through learning, mentoring, and responsibility.

• Competitive compensation and benefits: salary, pension plan, health insurance, and a great lunch program.

• A dynamic role with flexibility and diverse tasks—where your ideas can make a real difference.

Inclusion & equal opportunity

We value different perspectives and welcome applicants with varied career paths. If you’re excited about the role but don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply—your potential matters.

Want to know more?

Reach out to Technical Manager, Nikolaj Pave at +45 63 255 255 for more information.

Ready to apply?

Apply now and share your vision for the future of hydraulics, via the following link as soon as possible.

Learn more at www.svendborg-brakes.com.

Do you combine broad data and AI architecture expertise with hands-on engineering experience? Join Novo Nordisk to shape the architecture and build the foundations that enable secure, scalable data, analytics and AI solutions, including Generative AI (GenAI).

Your new role

You will set the architectural direction for data and AI platforms and solutions, connecting business priorities with a coherent target architecture and a practical technology roadmap. Working across a federated organisation, you will guide designs from data ingestion and modelling through analytics, machine learning and GenAI to integration with business applications. You will combine this breadth with hands-on technical leadership: validating key decisions through prototypes, reviewing code and helping engineers solve complex implementation challenges.

Your main responsibilities

• Shape the target architecture. Define architecture principles and the technology roadmap across data platforms, analytics and AI. Connect shared capabilities with business needs, plan transitions from existing solutions and balance global standards with local requirements.

• Design and build end-to-end solutions. Translate priority use cases into architectures spanning data ingestion, modelling, storage, APIs and AI deployment. Define integration patterns across cloud platforms and business applications, and implement key components alongside engineers.

• Engineer GenAI capabilities. Build reusable patterns for large language model integration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and tool-using agents, with evaluation, observability and appropriate human oversight.

• Take solutions into production. Guide implementation through code and design reviews, automated testing and CI/CD. Resolve reliability, performance and cost issues across data pipelines and AI services.

• Lead architecture decisions. Establish reference architectures and reusable patterns. Review solution designs with platform and product teams, assess build-versus-buy choices and test trade-offs in interoperability, scalability, security and cost through working prototypes.

• Embed security and controls. Work with security, governance and quality teams to implement access controls, data protection and AI guardrails, including validation and traceability where required.

• Lead across architecture and engineering. Coach architects and engineers, resolve design dependencies across teams and communicate technical choices to business and technology leaders. Turn architectural direction into clear implementation guidance.

Your skills and qualifications

• Degree in computer science, software engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Substantial experience spanning data and AI architecture and software or data engineering, with a track record defining target architectures and roadmaps and delivering production solutions.

• Recent, demonstrable hands-on experience in Python and SQL, APIs and data pipelines, supported by Git, automated testing and CI/CD. Ability to prototype critical designs, review code and troubleshoot implementation issues.

• Practical GenAI delivery experience, including LLM integration, RAG and evaluation. Experience with agent workflows and tool integration is an advantage.

• Architectural breadth across data modelling, integration, cloud data platforms, analytics, machine learning and GenAI, with implementation depth in at least one major cloud and modern data platform. Ability to assess interoperability, scalability, security and cost.

• Experience deploying and operating AI or machine learning services, with monitoring, versioning and troubleshooting across the application and data layers.

• Strong architecture judgement: translate business needs into technical designs, evaluate build-versus-buy options and guide distributed teams towards reusable solutions. Show your personal contribution to both architectural decisions and working implementations.

• Ability to influence business and technology stakeholders and align decisions across a federated organisation. Experience with regulated delivery, data governance and security, ideally in life sciences, is an advantage.

Do you want to use your skills in pioneering technology in a highly dynamic, ambitious environment with broad variety of exciting projects? In Welltec, cutting-edge technology and global development are high on the agenda, and we are looking for colleagues within mechanical engineering to take this journey to the next level.

A world-class company

Welltec® is an international oilfield service company and a leading specialist partner to the energy industry.

Our values are to be Pioneering, Visionary, Dedicated, and Agile.

We develop and manufacture precision-controlled technologies which provide the most unique and advanced Completion and Intervention solutions, which assist our clients in maximizing recovery from their assets.

We always look to the future, utilizing our intelligence, imagination and expertise to create new opportunities. We have won several industry awards for innovative thinking. We are enjoying constant growth worldwide through the wide adoption of our cutting-edge solutions.

Our policy is to hire locally and work globally. We therefore recruit where we are active and train our employees to operate our state-of-the-art technologies to provide services to our high-profile clients in the region.

The global dimension offers a range of opportunities for those who are motivated by a challenging and multicultural environment where employees come with very different backgrounds but with a common wish to collaborate and succeed.

The department

Welltec as a company is a truly global diverse team with over 60 nationalities in total. At Welltec, you will join our mechanical department situated in our Design & Engineering (D&E) function which currently consists of 33 colleagues with various educational backgrounds and nationalities. The D&E function also includes electronic and software engineers. In D&E we also work in smaller project groups – Mechanical-, Electrical- and Software Engineers together - in order to get a holistic approach to our products and tools and to benefit from each other’s knowledge and expertise. In D&E, the work environment is informal, creative and fun but at times it can be complex, challenging, and fast-paced.

The team that you will join is responsible for the development and maintenance of Welltec’s proprietary well intervention technologies, ranging from our Well Tractor with more than 20 years of service time to new and innovative technologies which we constantly introduce to the market through our global footprint.

The position

Your tasks will include:

• Develop new tools to solve cutting-edge problems.

• Work on technical projects through all development phases.

• Work in teams on development projects with both individual and shared responsibilities.

• Conceptualization and feasibility studies.

• Design reviews guided by DFM, FMEA principles and robust design thinking.

• 3D mechanical design.

• Plan, prepare and perform practical functional and verification testing of prototypes, tools and systems.

• Apply a structured and systematic approach to troubleshooting and root cause analysis during practical testing and development.

• Troubleshoot both existing solutions and new solutions under development, combining engineering analysis with hands-on testing.

• Provide guidance and input within your specific areas of expertise across the organization.

• Participate in project-related travel when required, including support for testing, troubleshooting, qualification activities and other project needs at Welltec locations, suppliers or customer sites.

The candidate

You are proactive in your daily tasks and have an analytical and critical approach to problem solving. You have a quick, creative mind with a natural understanding of complex concepts and systems.

The ideal candidate is someone who gets excited by technology, practical engineering and open-ended challenges. You are comfortable moving between engineering analysis, CAD design and hands-on testing, and you approach technical problems in a structured and systematic way.

In order to perform well in this role, you should have the following qualifications or similar competencies:

The preferred candidate has the following profile:

• Mechanical Engineer B.Sc., M.Sc. or similar background.

• Experience from the energy sector, hydraulics, precision mechanics, electromechanical systems, mechatronics, oilfield or similar.

• Possesses relevant deep technical knowledge and is able to apply it broadly with impact.

• Takes ownership of tasks and projects and enjoys broad responsibility.

• Strong hands-on engineering mindset with experience in practical functional testing, verification and systematic troubleshooting.

• Able to translate test observations and failures into root causes, design improvements and clear next actions.

• Agile Project Management skills.

• Knows when to supervise and delegate tasks to maximize efficiency and avoid bottlenecks.

• Experienced CAD user in CATIA or a similar system.

• Willing and able to travel as required to support project activities, testing and technical problem solving.

What we offer

Working with Welltec® means challenges and personal development in a demanding work environment. It is exciting and rewarding, and it is a varied place to work. Welltec® is an equal opportunity employer. We offer good career opportunities for the right candidate. Also, Welltec® has a competitive compensation package.

The process

If you are interested in the position submit your resume and cover letter online via the link below.

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply soon if you believe you fit the role.

This Specialist Professional role is a critical replacement to ensure business continuity within the Power and Grid Management team. These activities ensure that our digital products and solutions for the energy sector are robust, reliable, and meet all technical specifications before deployment. Given the focus on complex system verification, the ideal candidate will be a subject matter expert with extensive experience in verification engineering. This includes proven proficiency in test automation, scripting languages, and a deep understanding of the engineering design process, coupled with the ability to manage large projects and mentor junior professionals.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Analyze complex technical requirements and system designs for power and grid management solutions to define comprehensive verification strategies.

• Act as a subject matter expert, managing large-scale test projects and processes with limited oversight.
