• Identify, document, and meticulously track software defects and system anomalies through to resolution using workflow management tools.

• Conduct in-depth root cause analysis for difficult and complex problems, collaborating with development teams to find effective solutions.

• Generate detailed test summary reports and quality metrics to communicate findings and system readiness to stakeholders.

What You Bring

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Extensive experience, around 10 years, as a subject matter expert in verification engineering, software testing, or a similar role.

• Proven experience managing complex test projects or processes and mentoring other professionals.

• Demonstrated expertise in test automation, scripting, and testing complex software and hardware systems.

• Technical expertise in test automation, Python programming, scripting, Linux environments, simulations, and firmware development to support the design, testing, automation, and optimization of reliable and high‑quality technology solutions.

• Expertise in quality and process management, including test planning, quality assurance, engineering design processes, and workflow management to ensure efficient execution, high‑quality deliverables, and continuous improvement across engineering and development activities.

Can you own the platform and pipelines that EIVA’s software is built on?

EIVA is an equipment and software engineering company delivering solutions to the international maritime industry. You do not need to know the subsea domain to apply. Here, your product is the software itself, and your users are the other engineering teams who build and ship on the platform you own. What matters is curiosity – the ability to ask the right questions and translate what you hear into good technical decisions – and a collaborative, team-first mindset.

The position is based at EIVA’s Danish office in Stilling (just one minute from the E45, approximately 15 minutes from Aarhus by car and easily accessible by bus).

What's involved?

As Tech Lead – Infrastructure, you'll own the platform, pipelines and infrastructure that our NaviSuite software is built on.

Around 80% of the role is hands-on: working directly in the team's technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and tooling. The rest is technical leadership – owning architecture within the Infrastructure team, making the final call on anything inside the team's decision domain, and knowing when a question needs to go further, to our architects or to alignment with other teams. You'll also help keep that decision domain itself well defined: what the team can decide on its own, and where it needs external alignment.

There could be occasional travel – around one to two short trips a year.

Your responsibilities…

• Owning architecture in the team – ensuring platform and pipeline work aligns with EIVA's overall architecture, and explaining the interdependencies to the team

• Cross team alignment – representing the Infrastructure team's technical position and making sure its work fits with adjacent work elsewhere in the organisation

• Driving clarification with architects on technical questions that sit outside the team's decision domain

Also part of the role…

• Providing technical mentoring and sparring for the team's engineers

• Supporting the other development teams as users of the platform – helping with adoption, guidance and acting on their feedback

• Taking operational responsibility for the platform and pipelines

• Keeping the team's technical practices current – seeking out training, evaluating new tooling and sharing that knowledge internally

• Maintaining technical documentation for the platform, pipelines and environments

• Giving technical input to hiring and onboarding new engineers on the team

• Giving technical input to estimation and planning together with the Team Manager/Product Owner

The ideal candidate…

• Has a background in software engineering or computer science

• Has hands-on experience building and maintaining platforms, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code and internal tooling

• Has experience managing complex DevOps systems and workflows, and is comfortable making final technical calls within a defined decision domain

• Is familiar with tools such as Git/GitHub, artifact storage, Ansible and Terraform

• It's a bonus if you also have experience with licence management systems, but not a requirement.

Joining the EIVA crew

At EIVA, you'll join a team that values openness, informality and collaboration – while working with high-end, innovative technology in an inspiring environment. We appreciate personal responsibility and proactivity, and there is room to make your mark if you spot new opportunities. Work-life balance matters to us and is reflected in the 15th, 20th and even 25th work anniversaries commonly celebrated at EIVA. We offer…

ROLE DESCRIPTION

INVISIO is looking for a commercially minded and pragmatic Corporate Legal Counsel to support its global business. This is a broad legal generalist role with a strong commercial focus, where you will work closely with the business and provide legal support across a wide range of matters, with particular emphasis on international contracts, tenders, customer projects and other commercial legal matters.

As Corporate Legal Counsel, you will become part of a small legal team together with Signe Karstoft, Legal Director, to whom you will report. The role is based at INVISIO’s headquarters in Hvidovre, and the legal function is organisationally anchored within INVISIO’s Sales & Program function, which consists of approximately 50 employees globally, including around 25-30 in Denmark. You will primarily support the global sales organisation and work closely with colleagues across the business. Much of your work will involve large and complex customer contracts, tenders and projects.

You will provide legal support across INVISIO’s international business, including in relation to US contracts, such as contracts within the defence sector, and support sales teams across Europe and other markets. You will also support INVISIO in connection with major public tenders, including tenders involving ministries and defence organisations, providing legal support on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

As a technology company, intellectual property is an important part of INVISIO’s business. While dedicated specialists handle areas such as patents, you may also advise on IP-related matters as part of the broader commercial legal support. Experience with IP or from a technology or other IP-intensive business would therefore be an advantage.

In addition to the day-to-day legal support, you will contribute to developing and improving the way Legal supports the business. This includes driving legal improvement initiatives, maintaining and developing contract templates and legal guidelines, and conducting workshops and awareness activities for the business.

The role is highly international and outward-facing, with significant interaction with customers and stakeholders at all levels. You will have opportunities to join customer visits and negotiate contracts abroad, as well as participate in trade fairs in Denmark, Europe and the US.

The role is expected to involve approximately 25 travel days per year.

As INVISIO continues to grow rapidly, you will work in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, and no two days are the same.

AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

INVISIO is looking for an independent and commercially minded lawyer who takes ownership and enjoys working closely with customers and colleagues across the organisation. Your key responsibilities will include:

Commercial contracts and negotiations:

• 
Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of commercial contracts, including large international sales contracts, non-disclosure agreements, letters of intent, consulting agreements, tender-related contracts and distribution agreements.

• 
Take an active role in customer dialogue and contract negotiations and provide commercially focused legal advice, working closely with relevant stakeholders to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives.

• 
Provide pragmatic legal advice on contractual and other commercial matters arising in the day-to-day business.

**

Tenders and customer projects:**

• 
Provide legal support in connection with major public tenders, including reviewing tender documentation and advising on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

• 
Advise on legal and contractual aspects of tender structures, including which INVISIO entity should participate and any related intercompany arrangements.

• 
Support and, where relevant, take a coordinating role in customer projects and other commercial initiatives, including advising on contractual set-ups, priorities and how existing solutions can be applied in different markets etc.

**

IP and export control:**

• Ad hoc Advise on IP and export control matters, including IP considerations in commercial agreements and questions relating to export restrictions and requirements in connection with international sales and customer projects.

**

Legal development and business support:**

• 
Develop, maintain and improve contract templates, legal guidelines and other tools.

• 
Drive legal improvement initiatives and conduct workshops and legal awareness activities for the business, for example in relation to NDA’s.

• 
Provide ad hoc legal advice and support across INVISIO as required.

REPORTING AND TITLE

Reporting to: Signe Karstoft, Legal Director.

Title: Corporate Legal Counsel.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

Education: You hold a master’s degree in law (cand.jur. or cand.merc.jur.).

Work experience: You have approximately 3-6 years of relevant legal experience from an in-house role, for example in a technology or software company or another larger international industrial company.

Legal areas of specialisation: You have strong experience in drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements and are comfortable handling contractual matters independently. You also have experience supporting tender processes and advising on the legal and contractual matters that arise in this context.

In addition, you have a broad legal profile and are able to navigate a varied range of legal matters. Experience with IP-related matters, particularly from a technology or other IP-intensive business, would be an advantage. Knowledge of export control would also be beneficial.

Commercial: You have a strong commercial mindset and understand how legal advice fits into the broader business context.

You have experience working directly with customers and are comfortable collaborating with colleagues at all levels of the organisation. You are able to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives and provide pragmatic, solution-oriented advice.

Language skills: You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and verbal.

PERSONAL CAPABILITIES

Independent & proactive: You work independently, take ownership of your responsibilities and proactively drive matters forward.

Outgoing & interpersonal: You are outgoing and enjoy interacting with people with different backgrounds and at all levels, both internally and externally. You have strong interpersonal skills and are comfortable engaging with customers, colleagues and senior management.

Analytical & pragmatic: You have strong analytical skills and are able to understand complex legal and commercial matters while maintaining a pragmatic and solution-oriented approach.

Structured & able to prioritise: You work in a structured manner, maintain a good overview of your responsibilities and are able to prioritise effectively in a fast-paced environment where new and urgent matters frequently arise. You remain calm and focused when priorities change or deadlines are tight.

Stakeholder management & collaboration: You build strong relationships and collaborate effectively across functions and organisational levels. You are a team-oriented colleague who contributes to a strong sense of teamwork across the organisation and is able to influence stakeholders in a constructive manner.

Positive & constructive: You have a professional approach to your work and interact with others with maturity and integrity. You bring positive energy, are resilient when challenges arise and remain constructive in a busy environment.

INVISIO’S VALUE PROPOSITION TO YOU

INVISIO is a rapidly growing company with ambitious growth targets. The company achieves these ambitions through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts will be important to INVISIO’s continued success, and by joining the company, you will become part of an international headquarter with an informal working environment.

INVISIO offers a wide range of professional and social employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

ABOUT INVISIO

INVISIO is a global leader in communications technology for professionals working in mission-critical environments. Established in Denmark in 1999, the company develops and markets advanced, integrated communication systems for defence and public safety professionals, helping users communicate clearly and safely in demanding environments.

INVISIO’s modular and scalable portfolio includes headsets, control units, intercom systems, hubs and software designed to work together across dismounted, vehicle-based and command operations. The solutions are marketed under the INVISIO and Racal Acoustics brands.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, INVISIO has an international presence across Europe, North America and Asia. The company has approximately 330 employees globally, including around 215 in Denmark, and is growing rapidly. INVISIO is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (Large Cap).

INVISIO is characterised by a strong focus on innovation, close customer collaboration and an international working environment. Its core values are Passion, Innovation, Teamwork and Customer First.

You can learn more about INVISIO here: www.invisio.com.

APPLICATION AND CONTACT

If you believe this position is a good fit for you, we look forward to receiving your application. Please attach your CV and any relevant documentation. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please don’t hesitate to contact Camilla Krogh at (+45 51261264) or Mikkel Falkenberg at (+45 29993065) from the team at RESOLVA.

Built on a stack of

We imagine that you

• Experience with geospatial systems, financial modelling or the energy sector is an advantage Comfortable using modern AI coding tools as part of everyday engineering and interested in how AI changes software development itself - not just in adding LLM features to products

Working at Aegir Insights

Joining Aegir Insights means joining an international and dedicated team that moves with strategic intent on new ideas and enjoys learning new things. We encourage innovative and lateral thinking to achieve our goals.

We offer a respectful, diverse, and international working environment (our company language is English).

We have high ambitions, and you will take part in our growth journey by actively helping shape our culture and technical direction.

We offer a competitive remuneration package:

We are located in the heart of Copenhagen at Havnegade 27 st, 1058 Copenhagen.

About Aegir Insights

Aegir Insights is a technology-driven company offering decision-making software, data and intelligence products for the renewable energy sector. We combine data science and deep industry experience to help developers, investors, suppliers and governments make decisions.

Would you like to help accelerate the world's transformation to renewable energy?

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception by 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  The position is a fixed-term position for 30 months/2.5 years.
 
 Introduction
 The postdoc will be part of a project entitled "Mapping Experience of Action: Redefining Theories of Consciousness" funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The project is headed by Professor Thor Grünbaum and Associate Professor in Cognitive Psychology Mark Schram Christensen Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

  This interdisciplinary project develops a novel scientific approach to the study of consciousness by investigating conscious experiences of movement. Combining psychophysical experiments, computational modelling, and philosophical analysis, it examines how bodily and neural signals contribute to movement awareness. The project aims to advance our understanding of consciousness and critically evaluate leading neuroscientific theories of conscious experience.

  Applicants are asked to develop a short project description for the postdoc. It is critical that applicants are able to situate their project and research plan within the framework of the overall project. It is a requirement that applicants request from Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen (markc@psy.ku.dk) the original project proposal prior to submitting the application.

  Candidates with various background may be considered for the position. Examples of relevant backgrounds are PhDs in cognitive (neuro)science, computational neuroscience, cognitive modelling, biomedical engineering, sports science with a focus on behavioural neuroscience, or similar. The candidates are expected to have strong skills in cognitive modelling, experimental design, data handling and data analysis documented in relevant scientific publications.

  The postdoc will be working in close collaboration with the other project members which has academic backgrounds in cognitive neuroscience and philosophy, and student assistants with background in Cognitive Data Science.  The position will be placed in the Cognition, Intention and Action research group, part of the Section for Cognition and Brain Sciences, Department of Psychology.  It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and take part in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.
 
 Duties and Responsibilities
 The primary focus of the postdoctoral position will be on research within the main project. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.
 
 Qualification Requirements 
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  Strong skills in data handling and analysis are crucial, and experience with cognitive/computational modelling within human behavioural science or neuroscience is key to the content of the project. 

  You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.
 
 Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

  Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change.

  Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better.

  Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.

  For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.
 
 Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall project described above.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement.
 
 Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter including the preferred starting date (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc.
 		  	 	 	
• You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3.
 	  	
• A short project description (max. 2 pages). 	 		
• The description should outline your ideas for the postdoc project situated in the state-of-the-art research in the field of the project. It should include your proposals for specific types of experimental and modelling approaches that you envision to contribute with to the project. The description must not exceed 2 standard pages, corresponding to approx. 4,800 characters (including title, punctuation, figures, footnotes and references, but excluding bibliography). A substantial breach of this will result in the application being excluded from consideration.
 		  	 	 	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages) 	 		
• The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of planned research contribution over the coming years. This may include specific references to the project proposals funded by Independent Research Foundation Denmark, and how the candidate expect to contribute to the project at large. 	 	   
 Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,000/approximately EUR 5,100 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.
 
 Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.
 
 International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.
 
 Contact Information
 For additional information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen at email markc@psy.ku.dk or phone +45-3532 2448.

  For more Information about the recruitment process, please contact HR South at hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2675/26-2I

  The application deadline is 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

•

We hope to see that you are:

•

Your new team

Working closely with commercial, trading, marketing, product, technology, and analytics stakeholders, you will help shape the future of eCommerce analytics at Pandora and ensure insights play a central role in how we grow and evolve our digital business.

Additional information

Did we get your attention?

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible. You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site: www.pandoragroup.com.

jobs.occupation: Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for byggeri og Bygni
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Civil and Architectural Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
Informed comfort: natural-language interaction with home heating and cooling

Research area and project description
Predictive control can reduce energy costs and CO2 emissions of heating and cooling homes. However, its performance depends on knowing when residents are home and what they find comfortable.

You will develop a natural-language interface, based on a large language model, between residents and a predictive controller. Residents can then tell the controller, when they are away, report how the rooms feel, or ask for a warmer bathroom etc. In return, the controller explains what it did and why, shows what the next hours cost in money and CO2, and suggests alternatives that residents can accept or decline. The comfort limits are thus set by the residents; with the information they need.

This dialogue can save energy in three ways. Knowing when people are home and which rooms they use enables occupancy-based control, heating only where and when needed. Reports on how the rooms feel train personal comfort models, so setpoints match each household. The third, and least explored, is energy sufficiency: residents knowingly accept less heating or cooling, for example 20 °C instead of 21.5 °C on an expensive evening, while remaining free to say no. A central question is whether explaining alternative control actions and their cost changes how residents judge the same indoor conditions (their thermal acceptability), and whether the change lasts. All three look the same on the energy meter, so the project must separate them.

Few people want a system that talks all the time. Residents differ in how much information they want, in what form, and whether the system should take the initiative or only respond when asked (proactive versus on-demand interaction). Engagement may also fade as the novelty wears off. The project will study these differences and design for them.

You will:
• couple the language model to the controller, so that residents' requests become control actions within safe limits
• run a climate chamber experiment on whether explanations change thermal acceptability
• carry out a field study in occupied Danish homes through a winter and a summer, covering heating and overheating
Project description
For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

Qualifications and specific competences
Applicants to the PhD position must hold a M.Sc. in engineering, computer science, building science or a related technical field. Applicants with a B.Sc. and at least one year of master's studies can apply through the 4+4 programme.

You should be able to program, preferably in Python, and be comfortable analysing data. Experience with one or more of the following is an advantage: model predictive control or optimisation, large language models, statistics and the design of experiments with people, and field measurements in buildings. Nobody will have all of these, and you should be willing to learn what you lack.

The field study involves installing equipment in people's homes and talking with the residents, so you should be comfortable working with people. Danish is an advantage for the field work but not a requirement.

Applicants from neighbouring fields with relevant technical skills and a clear motivation for the topic are encouraged to apply.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Arhus C., Denmark.

Contacts

• Massimo Fiorentini, massimo@cae.au.dk (co-supervisor)

The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

jobs.occupation: Lead Consultant – Vulnerability Management; DK - Fredericia, Ballerup
jobs.description:
Can you translate complex technical security requirements into something the business understands and acts on - and challenge where necessary?

Energinet is seeking a highly skilled cyber security professional to join our Attack Surface Management team within the Group Cyber and Information Security unit. You will be the link between the department's technical specialists and the rest of Energinet and ensure that security requirements are both understood, prioritised and complied with.

You combine solid technical insight with clear communication and business understanding. You present innovative ideas with confidence, along with the presence and authority to guide decisions. 

Key Responsibilities

• Oversee the operation and continual improvement of enterprise vulnerability management capabilities across IT, cloud, and hybrid environments.
• Build, maintain, and optimize vulnerability scanning infrastructure, configurations, policies, and workflows.
• Develop scalable vulnerability assessment processes covering infrastructure, endpoints, servers, applications, cloud workloads, containers, and identities.
• Ensure accurate asset discovery, coverage validation, and vulnerability visibility across the enterprise.
• Manage lifecycle vulnerability processes from detection through validation, prioritization, remediation, and closure.
• Establish metrics and performance indicators to measure remediation effectiveness and risk reduction outcomes.
• Analyze attack paths, exposure chains, and security control weaknesses that could contribute to organizational risk.
• Develop risk-based methodologies for prioritizing exposures based on exploitability, business criticality, threat intelligence, and operational impact.
• Support continuous assessment of the organization's security posture through exposure analytics and attack surface monitoring.
• Serve as the technical owner and subject matter expert for vulnerability and exposure management platforms.

“We offer a job with a high level of professionalism and great societal significance, where you help protect Denmark's critical energy infrastructure. You will have skilled colleagues, good opportunities for professional development and flexibility in everyday life – in an organization that is growing and where cyber security is a high priority.” – Arpan Roy, Director, Attack Surface Management.

We expect you to

• Have a solid technical understanding in cyber and information security and can go in-depth with technical solutions.
• Have CISSP or an equivalent certification (e.g. CISM) - or are close to earning it.
• Is an effective communicator who can communicate complex requirements clearly to both technicians, project managers and management.
• Works in a structured way and projects professional authority.
• Have business understanding and the ability to question constructively and create progress.
• Be fluent in English at a high level in writing and speech. Danish proficiency is an advantage but not mandatory. 
About the department

At our office in Ballerup or Fredericia, you will be part of Attack Surface Management - a new department under the Group Cyber and Information Security unit. The department is responsible for the technical protection layers that reduce Energinet's attack surface. 

Together with the other departments in Cyber and Information Security, we are responsible for developing and operating the organizational processes and technologies within cyber and information security in Energinet and for coordinating the IT preparedness in the electricity, gas and hydrogen sectors. 

Want to know more?

If you have any questions about the job, you are very welcome to contact Arpan Roy at arroy@energinet.dk or on tel. +45 5161 2898. We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send us your motivated cv as soon as possible.

Special conditions: As Energinet performs tasks critical to society, we carry out background checks prior to employment. Employment is conditional upon your background check being compatible with employment at Energinet. The background check is also carried out once a year.

The position also requires that you are able to obtain and maintain security clearance. On PET's website, you can read more about security clearance.

We see diversity as a strength and encourage all qualified people, regardless of background, to apply for the job. We work actively and determinedly with diversity in Energinet and therefore encourage you to exclude information about age, marital status, etc. to minimise outage biases in the process. You can read more about our diversity policy here.

Energinet is an independent public company that reprecents society's interests when supplying Denmark with electricity and gas and that the energy system is converted to green energy. Our culture is closely linked to our social responsibility, and we work actively with the UN's global goals on sustainable energy, climate action, partnerships for action as well as industry, innovation, and infrastructure. By leading the way in the green transition, we can help to solve the global climate challenge. New solutions require us to be able to see problems from many different angles, and diversity is therefore a keyword in our culture. We strive to listen to, involve and share our knowledge. Based on the values of courage and trust, we focus on constantly developing ourselves as an organisation and as people. Read more at our website www.energinet.dk.

Vetaphone is the Danish company behind the invention of corona treatment back in 1951, and for more than seven decades the family-owned business has continued to set the standard within corona and plasma surface treatment technology. From its headquarters in Kolding, Vetaphone develops advanced, reliable systems that ensure optimal adhesion, print quality and production efficiency for customers in the print, packaging, converting and extrusion industries – and today the company is represented in more than 60 countries around the world. To strengthen the international sales organisation, we are now looking for a technically strong and commercially minded:

Technical and commercial sales support with close customer dialogue

As Technical Sales Manager, you become one of the key technical and commercial support behind Vetaphone’s global sales team, working closely with Area Sales Managers and agents to solve real production challenges where surface treatment performance impacts efficiency, quality and compliance. You get a broad and technically demanding role, where you guide projects from the very first customer dialogue and solution design through to quotation, negotiation and handover to the internal project department.

It is natural for you to drive technically complex, project-based sales to OEMs and end customers, and to step in as technical sales lead on selected projects in close cooperation with Area Sales Managers, agents and internal specialists. You analyse customer applications, production processes and requirements to define the optimal surface treatment solution, and you prepare and present technical and commercial proposals that communicate value, performance and compliance in a way customers understand and trust.

You support OEM customers with system integration, specification and application know-how, and build long-term customer relationships based on trust, expertise and results. At the same time, you contribute to knowledge sharing and capability building across the sales organisation and agent network, and you stay on top of market trends, customer needs and competitive developments – with regular international travel to customers, OEM partners and key industry events.

In the selection process, we will particularly emphasise:

• A solid technical background, preferably within mechanical and/or electrical engineering

• Proven experience with consultative, project-based B2B sales of technical systems or solutions

• The ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear customer value propositions

• A structured and self-driven approach, combined with strong stakeholder management skills

• Comfort working independently in an international, matrix-based organisation

• Fluent in Danish and excellent communication skills in English

• Willingness to travel internationally approx. 50-70 days per year

The ideal candidate has a solid technical foundation combined with a genuine sales flair, and thrives in a role where every project brings a new technical puzzle to solve. Maybe you already work in a similar technical sales role today, or you come from an engineering or application background and are ready to take the step into a more commercial, customer-facing career.

In return, you become part of a global technology leader with a strong market position, working closely with experienced technical and commercial colleagues on high-value international projects – with good opportunities for professional development within a specialised, knowledge-driven organisation.

The role is based at Vetaphone’s headquarters in Kolding, Denmark, combined with the international travel the role calls for.

Interested?

Sounds like the job for you? Then send your application and CV as soon as possible by using the “apply” function.

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Selectors® Partner Lars Mikkelsen at 2219 4930 or Selectors® on 7210 0030.

About Unilabs A/S

Unilabs A/S is part of Unilabs Pharma Solutions, a leading provider of laboratory services and innovative solutions for the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries. We support drug development through high-quality bioanalytical testing, helping to ensure that new treatments are developed efficiently, accurately, and in compliance with regulatory standards.

Do you thrive in a laboratory environment where high-quality analytical work is at the center of your daily responsibilities?

On behalf of Unilabs Pharma Solutions, we are seeking an experienced Biomedical Laboratory Scientist/ Bioanalyst to join a highly skilled bioanalytical team in a commercial laboratory providing solutions for the pharmaceutical industry. This role is ideal for a laboratory professional who enjoys performing analytical testing in a regulated pharmaceutical environment while contributing to method improvements, validation activities, and the maintenance of quality standards.

About the Role

The primary focus of this position is the execution of bioanalytical testing supporting pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients throughout drug development programs. You will be responsible for generating high-quality analytical data while ensuring full compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and quality systems.

You will join a collaborative laboratory team where analytical excellence, scientific rigor, and meticulous documentation are essential to success.

Analytical Testing (Primary Focus)

• Perform routine and non-routine bioanalytical testing according to approved methods, SOPs, and study protocols.

• Execute ELISA-based assays and other bioanalytical methods with a high degree of accuracy and consistency.

• Ensure timely delivery of analytical results while maintaining the highest quality standards.

• Review analytical data and documentation for completeness, accuracy, and compliance.

• Perform sample receipt, registration, processing, and analysis activities.

Key Responsibilities

• Maintain, calibrate, troubleshoot, and verify the performance of laboratory equipment, while supporting efficient laboratory workflows and ensuring laboratories remain inspection-ready.

• Participate in method development, optimization, validation, transfer, and continuous improvement of analytical methods and laboratory processes.

• Contribute to the qualification, implementation, and ongoing operation of laboratory equipment, technologies, assays, and designated operational areas.

• Perform all activities in compliance with GxP principles, including GCP, GCLP, GMP, ISO 15189, and pharmaceutical industry standards.

• Maintain accurate, complete, and traceable laboratory documentation, including support for SOP development and revision.

• Support deviation investigations, change controls, CAPAs, audit readiness activities, and participate in regulatory inspections and client audits as required.

• Support the training and qualification of laboratory colleagues and contribute to knowledge sharing across the team.

Who we Are Looking For

We are seeking a hands-on laboratory professional with a strong analytical mindset and experience working within a regulated pharmaceutical or biotech environment.

Qualifications

• Degree as a Biomedical Laboratory Scientist, Laboratory Technologist, Research Laboratory Technician, or equivalent scientific qualification.

• Minimum 2-5 years of experience in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO, or regulated laboratory industry.

• Practical experience performing bioanalytical testing in a GxP-regulated environment.

• Hands-on experience with ELISA assays is required.

• Strong understanding of laboratory documentation practices, data integrity, and compliance requirements.

• Experience following and working according to SOPs, validation protocols, and quality management systems.

• Fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

To succeed in this role, you are:

• Detail-oriented and quality-focused.

• Comfortable performing repetitive analytical work while maintaining accuracy and consistency.

• Structured and disciplined in your documentation practices.

• Proactive and able to work independently within established procedures.

• A collaborative team player who enjoys working in an international laboratory environment.

What Unilabs Offers

An exciting opportunity to work on pharmaceutical development projects with direct impact on patient care.

A modern laboratory environment in central Copenhagen.

Strong focus on scientific development and professional growth.

A collaborative team culture with experienced colleagues and a high level of technical expertise.

The opportunity to work with advanced bioanalytical methods in a regulated setting.

This role will particularly suit candidates who enjoy spending the majority of their time conducting laboratory analyses and generating high-quality data, while also contributing to validation, compliance, documentation, and continuous improvement activities.

Søg jobbet

Har ovenstående fanget din interesse, søger du stillingen ved at vedhæfte et opdateret cv og en motiveret ansøgning. Du kan også skrive en kort tekst om dig selv i ansøgningsteksten ovenfor. Temp-Team A/S varetager denne rekruttering og al henvendelse skal gå gennem Temp-Team.

Grundet GDPR modtager vi ikke cv og ansøgning via e-mail.

Temp-Team

Temp-Team A/S er et landsdækkende rekrutterings- og vikarbureau med lokale afdelinger i Danmark. Vi har 45 års erfaring inden for bemandingsløsninger og dækker et bredt udsnit af brancher. Vi yder altid en service af høj kvalitet og har tæt, personlig kontakt til både vores kandidater og kunder.

Vi er en del af JuhlerGroup – en international koncern.

Retire the ERP.

Light exists to replace factory-era ERPs with software that feels alive. Our Smart Financial Platform gives modern, global companies superpowers—automated accounting, real-time reporting, and financial flows that move at the speed of the business.

We build with our customers, ship fast, and obsess over craft. In a short time, Light has gone from idea to the operating core for leading companies like Lovable, Legora, and Keyshot. People don't just use Light—they enjoy it.

We're an early team defining a new software category. Think engineers who love debits and credits, designers who care about reconciliation states, and operators who treat finance as a product. If you're excited to modernize how the world runs money—one workflow at a time—you're in the right place.

Backed by world-class investors and advised by industry titans, we're building category-defining products with the freedom to ship ambitiously and own outcomes. Come help us make Light the global default for next-gen finance.

This Integrations Engineer role

Light is only as powerful as the systems it connects to. Money doesn't move because we say so—it moves because we speak the language of the bank, the e-invoicing network, and the planning tool on the other side, correctly, every time, for every customer entity. This role owns that layer: the interaction surface between Light and the rest of the financial world.

You'll build and operate the integrations that let Light plug into multi-tenant banking APIs (J.P. Morgan, HSBC, and peers), global e-invoicing networks, and tax platforms and more. This is backend-heavy, data-integrity-critical work where a dropped message or a silent reconciliation mismatch is not an acceptable outcome. You'll design the abstractions that turn a dozen incompatible partner APIs into one coherent internal model, and you'll keep those abstractions honest as partners change their specs underneath you.

What you'll work on:

• 
Bank connectivity. Build against corporate banking and payments APIs—account information, payment initiation, status reporting, FX—across providers like J.P. Morgan Payments and HSBC. Handle the realities of bank integrations: certificate-based and mTLS auth, OAuth flows, ISO 20022 (pain/pacs/camt) and legacy MT formats, sandbox-to-production parity, and rate limits that assume you're a bank, not a startup.

• 
Multi-tenancy done right. Our customers are many legal entities operating in many countries. You'll design integrations where credentials, configuration, and data are isolated per tenant, where onboarding a new entity is a workflow rather than a code change, and where one customer's failure never leaks into another's.

• 
Global e-invoicing. Connect Light to e-invoicing networks and country-specific mandates (Peppol and the growing set of national clearance and reporting regimes). Map between formats, manage compliance-driven edge cases, and keep delivery auditable.

• 
Tax platforms for statutory filing, US sales tax and much more.

• 
Reliability and reconciliation. Idempotency, retries, webhook and polling strategies, dead-letter handling, and end-to-end reconciliation so that what we think happened and what actually happened always agree.

Your qualifications

4-6 years of experience ideally, plus…

You build things. Not prototypes, not demos. Working software in production, doing something real for real users. This is the non-negotiable.

You've built integrations against unforgiving external systems. APIs you don't control, that fail in ways the docs don't mention, where correctness is contractual. You know how to defend a system against a partner that returns a 200 with an error in the body.

You know banking and payments APIs. Direct, hands-on experience with corporate banking, treasury, or payments APIs is what sets the strongest candidates apart. Experience integrating J.P. Morgan or HSBC specifically—their developer platforms, auth models, and payment and reporting APIs—is highly valuable and a genuine differentiator for this role. Familiarity with ISO 20022, SWIFT, virtual accounts, or open banking is a strong signal.

You are excited about AI. You use AI tooling efficiently to improve your work. At Light, a lot of code is written with AI, which means the hard part is increasingly the thinking: deciding what to build, reviewing what comes back, and catching where the model is confidently wrong. You know when AI speeds you up, when it's likely to mislead you, and how to lean on it while staying fully responsible for what ships.

You're comfortable across the stack. You don't need to be a specialist in everything, but you can't have a lane you refuse to leave. Our stack is Kotlin and React, and this role leans backend. If you're strong on the backend and curious about the rest, that works.

You care about data integrity. You think about the person on the other end and the money moving between them. You notice when a flow is correct but fragile, and you act on it.

You ship early and often. Small batches. Learn. Go again. You'd rather put something real in front of a customer than spend another week perfecting it in isolation.

Bonus points

• 
Experience in fintech or systems where data integrity is non-negotiable

• 
Familiarity with accounting concepts: debits, credits, reconciliation

• 
Experience with e-invoicing standards or country-specific compliance regimes

• 
Background in high-growth startups where everything was still being figured out

Our Tech Stack

We build on AWS, with a Kotlin backend, a React frontend, and infrastructure managed in Terraform. It's a real production system that global finance teams depend on every day. The integration layer you'll own sits squarely in the Kotlin backend, talking to a long list of external partners. You don't need to have used every piece of it. You do need to be comfortable in this kind of environment: real scale, real customers, real stakes.

The good stuff

In addition to being part of a great team and working in a really fun and innovative environment, we offer:

• 
A competitive salary + potential stock options

• 
25 days of annual leave + public holidays in the country where you are based

• 
Regular socials and company off-sites

• 
A huge opportunity for career growth as you'll help shape a market-defining product

The famous last words

Working at Light means you're embarking on an exciting journey to reshape the future of multinational financial operations. Our cheat-code is that we've built something like this before—and are now doing it again, only better. Our goal is to make global finance effortless and empower companies to make informed decisions.

Join the rocket ship while it's taking off.

Working at

Light

Light is the new way to run multinational finances for modern technology companies. Run AR, AP, expenses, bookkeeping, and financial reporting automatically across all your entities — without the chaos of multiple systems. Crafted and built by the designers and engineers behind world-class companies like Spotify, X, AWS, Klarna, Google and Shopify, we empower multinational finances with a joyful user experience like no other.

Ready for a career that's challenging, fun, and ever changing?

Working at Terotech

We're 50+ people based in Esbjerg, working in Denmark and internationally. Oil & gas, energy, manufacturing - all industries where downtime isn't an option. You learn fast, solve real problems, and see results immediately.

A Place You'll Want to Stay

Considering a career in Terotech?
