Hos Viking Gulvservice kommer du til at arbejde med række forskellige tømreropgave, bl.a. opbygning af gulvkonstruktioner, montering af gipsplader, opbygning af lettere trækonstruktioner m.m.

Du vil blive tilknyttet en kollega, så I altid er to om opgaverne, ved små opgaver må man forvente at arbejde selvstændigt. Som makkerpar får I stillet en firmabil til rådighed med de nødvendige maskiner og værktøj.

Vi forventer, at du:

1.       Har minimum 1 års erfaring indenfor tømrerfaget

2.       Har kørekort B

3.       Er pligtopfyldende og letforståelig på engelsk eller dansk

4.       Afslutter en opgave ryddelig og kvalitetsbevidst

Vi tilbyder:

1.       Attraktiv løn

2.       Arbejdstid i tidsrummet 07:00-15:00

3.       Kollegaer du kan sparrer med

4.       Spændende og alsidige opgave

 

Lyder stillingen interessant, eller har du spørgsmål? Så er du meget velkommen til at kontakte os på mail gm@vikinggulvservice.dk

Vi ser frem til din ansøgning og cv.

Samtaler afholdes løbende med ansættelse hurtigst muligt.

ENGLISH:

Viking Gulvservice is a well-established company located in Ballerup. Over the years, we have provided professional painting services to a wide range of customers. In addition to flooring services, we also offer painting and carpentry services.

We are currently looking for 1–2 experienced colleagues to join our carpentry team and help us handle our growing portfolio of projects.

If you have experience as a carpenter and are passionate about your work, we can offer you an attractive workplace with a positive and friendly atmosphere.

 

About the job

At Viking Gulvservice, you will work on a variety of carpentry tasks, including building floor structures, installing plasterboard/drywall, constructing light timber structures, and other related carpentry work.

You will normally work together with a colleague, so there will usually be two of you assigned to each project. For smaller jobs, however, you should be comfortable working independently.

As a team, you will have access to a company vehicle equipped with the necessary machinery and tools.

We expect you to:

1.       Have at least 1 year of experience working as a carpenter

2.       Hold a valid Category B driving licence

3.       Be reliable, responsible and able to communicate in English or Danish

4.       Take pride in completing your work to a high standard and leaving the work area clean and tidy

We offer:

1.       Attractive salary

2.       Working hours between 07:00 and 15:00

3.       Supportive and experienced colleagues you can exchange knowledge with

4.       Exciting and varied carpentry projects

 

Does the position sound interesting, or do you have any questions?

You are very welcome to contact us by email at gm@vikinggulvservice.dk.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV.

Interviews will be held on an ongoing basis, and we are looking for someone who can start as soon as possible.

ristorante Amarone is looking for a skilled, reliable, and dedicated Cook to join our team.

We are looking for someone who:

• 
Has relevant experience working as a cook

• 
Is skilled and passionate about preparing high-quality food

• 
Is reliable, responsible, and committed to their work

• 
Can work independently as well as part of a team

• 
Is flexible and able to work in a busy environment

We offer a full-time position in a professional and friendly workplace.

If you are an experienced and motivated cook looking for a new opportunity, we would be happy to hear from you.

The Impact You'll Make

As our Power Electronics Architect, you’ll play a key role in shaping the next generation of variable speed drive solutions within our HVAC and Water Drives business. By defining and driving the power electronics architecture of our frequency converters, you will develop more energy-efficient, reliable, and sustainable motor control solutions.

Your impact? You will define the technical direction of future drive platforms, ensuring optimal performance, cost competitiveness, reliability, and scalability. Your work will directly support our customers' efforts to improve energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact while accelerating the transition toward electrification. You’ll collaborate closely with experts across hardware, software, systems, mechanical engineering, supply chain, and procurement while taking ownership of the power electronics architecture and design principles that help us build innovative products for a more sustainable future.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Define and own the power electronics system architecture for next-generation variable speed drive products

• Drive technical decisions and trade-offs across performance, cost, manufacturability, and reliability

• Lead concept development and evaluation of emerging technologies ex. Silicon Carbide (SiC)

• Collaborate across hardware, software, systems, and mechanical teams to ensure alignment with product and customer requirements

• Mentor engineers, promote best practices, and contribute to platform development and long-term innovation initiatives

What We're Looking For

• Master's degree in Power Electronics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

• Extensive experience designing power electronic systems for frequency converters, drives, inverters, or similar applications

• Strong knowledge of converter topologies, power semiconductor technologies, and system-level architecture development

• Experience with simulation and modeling tools such as PLECS, MATLAB/Simulink, or equivalent tools

• Strong analytical, communication, and collaboration skills, combined with the ability to influence technical direction across multidisciplinary teams

• A team-oriented mindset and a genuine interest in contributing to a positive, supportive, and trust-based working environment where collaboration, well-being, and strong collegial relationships are valued

What You'll Get from Us

• We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.

• You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected, and valued for who they are.

• You’ll receive benefits like 13th salary, annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re pretty great.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

Information at a Glance

Apply now

Brand

Danfoss engineers solutions that increase machine productivity, reduce emissions, lower energy consumption, and enable electrification.

Our solutions are used in areas such as refrigeration, air conditioning, heating, power conversion, motor control, industrial machinery, marine, and on- and off-highway equipment. We also provide solutions for data centers, renewable energy, energy storage, heat recovery, as well as contribute to district energy solutions for cities.

Our innovative engineering dates back to 1933. Danfoss is family-owned and employs over 39,000 people. We create long-term value for our customers in more than 100 countries with a global footprint of around 100 factories.

Are you passionate about Michelin and luxury service? Do you want to be part of a motivated team with high ambitions in a privileged environment where you will develop and nurture successful working relationships, both with our guests and within your workplace? Then you might be the on-call waiter we are looking for to support our restaurant Marchal.

WE OFFER

An exciting working day in an international environment in our Michelin awarded restaurant Marchal. We are a young and dynamic team, who together delivers a personal, stylish and elegant service of the highest international standard. Through our internal d’Anglecademy you will be trained in various programs to give you best possible circumstances for growth and success.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an on call waiter at Marchal, you will elevate our guests by creating unforgettable experiences through a high level of service and your expertise within wines and Michelin cuisine. You will work closely with our team of dedicated waiters and chefs to ensure a flawless service at a Michelin level. You must maintain high guest loyalty throughout high guest satisfaction and ensure that all guests receive a unique and magical experience.

WE EXPECT

That you have similar experience as waiter in a Michelin star or a luxury establishment. You are detail-oriented and able to keep the grand overview, while being sincerely passionate and engaged with both guests and employees. You are a visible and active team member and ensure a good cooperation with the rest of the hotel. We are Playdead, an independent game company based in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. We have made two critically acclaimed titles, LIMBO and INSIDE. Our current project is a 3rd-person science fiction adventure set in a remote corner of the universe.

We are seeking an experienced Level Architect with strong artistic skills to join our team in Copenhagen. As our process is very visually driven, we expect layout artists to have a strong eye for visual composition and broad experience in the creation of 3D environments.

Your responsibility as our new colleague will be in designing, blocking out, and in some cases modeling locations for a third-person, open-world game. At Playdead, locations are often designed with a combination of grey-boxing and more detailed, modeled elements. You will work in coordination with the other designers and artists on the team with a focus on how the player will flow within the level and betweens spaces.

We are a close-knit group of developers, and working within that group requires an ability to adapt to the existing visual style and methods while contributing your own ideas to the whole. We are particularly looking for a candidate who enjoys setting their own goals and taking responsibility for their own schedule. More than anything, we are looking for someone who is excited about all facets of game development, as well as being passionate about gaming overall.

You should be willing to work at the Playdead office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Keywords for position

layout - level design - composition -3D - modelling - iteration

What will you be doing?

• Level layout, spatial design and composition using primitive blockouts and 3D assets to produce believable locations within a large, open world.

• Taking a basic brief and mocking up a grey box design to set the foundation for further development and visual storytelling.

• Detailed, untextured 3D modeling

• Iterating on existing location designs based on feedback and testing.

• Collaborating with other artists and designers to support level design and construction.

If you wish to apply, please consider the following general requirements

• You have worked on the development of at least one released 3D game.

• A link to an online portfolio of previous work showcasing a knowledge of composition, layout, lighting, colour and visual storytelling.

• Experience with a game engine such as Unity, Unreal etc. or an internal engine is a must.

• Experience with 3D packages such as Blender, Maya, 3dsMax, etc. is a strong advantage.

Desired skills

• Experience with world creation tools such as World Machine, Quadspinner Gaea, or similar is a plus.

Who We Are

We are a team of more than 100 creative professionals. We experiment and collaborate with a focus on creating new experiences, and as such we are looking for people who can help us achieve them.

Our approach to development does not include crunching towards arbitrary deadlines - instead, we particularly look for talented people who enjoy managing their own schedule and thrive on working within a friendly, collaborative environment.

We love to make carefully crafted games with obsessive attention to detail and are always on the lookout for others who share that passion.

We work with leading payment providers (Nets, Worldline, Softpay, Swedpay, Verifone, and MobilePay) - operating at the heart of the Nordic payments ecosystem. We're growing fast, and we're looking for a relentless hustler who wants to grow with us.

The best Customer Success Manager isn't the one who answers the most support calls. It's the one who ensures customers rarely need to call - and consistently helps them get more value from our platform.

The Role

Understanding their business well enough to spot problems before they become support calls

• 
Reaching out proactively with relevant features, improvements, or ways to get more from the platform

• 
Handling support issues when they come up, but treating them as the exception, not the job

• 
Feeding what you learn from merchants back into the product

Success in this role = customers who rarely need to call, and who wouldn't consider switching providers.

What we're looking for

• 
Fluent written and spoken Danish (additional languages a plus)

• 
Comfortable having commercial conversations that feel like advice, not sales

• 
Able to work independently (this role has real autonomy and not a lot of hand-holding)

Curious about technology and interested in fintech/payments

Some experience in customer success, account management, or a similar client-facing role

What you get

• 
Direct exposure to Nordic fintech: daily collaboration with Nets, Worldline, Softpay, Swedpay, Verifone, and MobilePay

• 
Real ownership: your customers, your calls, measured on outcomes rather than process

• 
Room to grow: we're early-stage and growing quickly, so responsibility comes fast

A small, senior team: direct access to the people building the product, including a founding team with 50+ years of combined experience at major companies

Job Description

Are you passionate about data and driven by the opportunity to make a real impact by helping companies turn facts into actionable insights? Do you thrive in dynamic environments where you work with some of the most complex and modern data solutions? If so, you might be our next colleague.

Responsibilities & technologies

In Data Management, you will become part of a team that contributes to enabling our customers to develop and manage their business based on data and knowledge.

You will work in the intersection of technology and business. Information and data are at the core of our work, and we can see that our analyses, advice, and final solutions create value for our customers. The work involves developing technical solutions to collect, process, model, analyze, and visualize data.

To provide the best possible advice and support to our customers, we place great importance on staying up to date with the latest trends and technologies in data management. You will work with a broad range of market-leading technologies, including: Azure SQL Server, Snowflake, dbt, Microsoft SQL Server, and others.

Your tasks are highly varied and depend on your skills and the direction you wish to develop.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Design, modeling, and building of data structures such as databases.

• Structuring and collection of data from various sources.

• Implementation of business logic on data for use in reporting.

• Customer advisory, strategy work, and business analysis in collaboration with our customers.

• Development of reports for business users with a focus on front-end.

About you

You are newly graduated or have up to a couple of years of relevant professional experience within data management. Through your education, you have gained a solid professional foundation and a logical approach to handling complex data and challenges. You thrive in a development-oriented environment with a focus on collaboration and continuous personal and professional development.

To succeed in this role, you have experience with or the interest to learn:

• ETL and Database technologies.

• Languages such as various versions of SQL, Python, and R.

• Business Intelligence tools: Power BI, Tableau, and others.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will guide you through your development and help you achieve your goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague helps ensure the well-being of each employee and provides you with concrete insights into the many different career opportunities as you build your experience.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars on everything from technologies to customer management. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills, preparing you for various tasks and continuously improving your expertise throughout your career with us.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. As a Crane Mechanic Apprentice, you will work with the construction, installation, troubleshooting and repair of truck-mounted cranes and truck chassis.

The Crane Mechanic programme takes 4 years and combines school-based training with practical apprenticeship training in a company.

At the end of the programme, you complete your final trade examination and become a qualified Crane Mechanic.

We are looking for someone who:

jobs.occupation: Backend Developer, Data Collection and Infrastructure
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. The collection is the hard part, and it is most of this job. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry.

On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

What you will work on

• The collection and ingestion pipeline behind those numbers, together with the engineers who run it today.

• Add coverage for new search surfaces as they appear, and fix the ones we already cover when they change shape.

• Write and tune queries against very large time series data, across columnar and relational stores.

• Start with scoped changes to existing services, and grow into owning services yourself, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

What you bring

Must have:

• Solid programming fundamentals. You write clear code and can reason about what it costs at runtime.

• Code of yours running somewhere real. A production system at work, a service you host yourself, or a side project with actual users.

• Comfort in Linux. You can read logs, follow a request through a system, and find out why something is slow.

• Ownership. You take a problem, decide how to attack it, ask when you are stuck, and follow through.

Good to have:

• Distributed systems fundamentals. Queues, workers, backpressure, etc.

• Python and its common frameworks (Django, Celery, pandas/polars). Our stack runs mostly on Python, but it is not a must if the fundamentals are strong.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store.

• The network layer. Connection lifecycle, timeouts and retries, TLS, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3.

• Web scraping or browser automation.

• AI agents. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Kafka.

All of it can be learned here.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You want to own a feature end to end, from idea to production. The problems we hand you will be scoped at first, and less so over time, and a month after something ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a database, debug a proxy network, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a narrow technical scope or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will get real responsibility earlier than most places give it. The senior engineers sit next to you, and asking them is part of the job.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English. A link to something you have built counts for a lot.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.

jobs.occupation: Senior Network Specialist – Core Infrastructure Platforms
jobs.description:
Senior Network Specialist – Core Infrastructure Platforms

We are moving our entire network and firewall estate to an automated, code-driven operating model, and we need someone who can help lead that shift. If Ansible, Terraform and Git workflows excite you more than console access, this role is built for you.

**The job

**

You will help design, build and operate the automation platform behind our entire network and firewall estate, moving us from manual, device-by-device changes to a version-controlled, peer-reviewed, GitOps-style way of working. As a technical anchor in Core Infrastructure Platforms, you will shape how the whole Infrastructure department approaches network automation.

In short, you can look forward to:

•    Driving network automation – help architecting, building and maintaining network automation for our Cisco and Palo Alto estate, replacing manual configuration with automated deployments.

•    Owning our network Source of Truth – building and operating the authoritative, version-controlled model of our intended network state (think Nautobot or Infrahub).

•    Designing CI/CD and Git – setting up pull requests, automated checks and review-gated deployments, and running the platforms

•    Running core network and SDN infrastructure – owning and optimising our datacenter and enterprise network, including Software-Defined Networking

**Joining the team

**

You will join our Infrastructure department, a small team coving everything infrastructure related.  We are in the beginning   of an ambitious shift from manual device configuration to a Source of Truth-driven, GitOps-style operating model, and you will have real influence over the architecture, tooling and practices we adopt next.

You will also act as a sparring partner and mentor to colleagues across Infrastructure, sharing what you build through documentation and peer review so good ideas do not stay with just one person.

**Your qualifications

**

You have a solid networking foundation combined with hands-on experience in modern network automation. You are comfortable working across Cisco and Palo Alto platforms, treating infrastructure as code with tools such as Ansible or Terraform, building CI/CD pipelines and using Git. We are interested in the strengths you bring across the areas below. Your most important skills are:

•    Solid networking fundamentals (L2/L3, BGP, OSPF, EVPN, VXLAN) with hands-on experience in Cisco (IOS/NX-OS) and Palo Alto/Panorama, plus exposure to SDN paradigms such as Cisco ACI.

•    Hands-on experience with Ansible or Terraform applied to network infrastructure.

•    Experience designing or operating CI/CD pipelines and using Git

•    Scripting skills in Python or Jinja2, with comfort working with APIs.

On a personal level, you are a proactive team player who shares what you build, a problem solver with an eye for detail, and someone who would rather automate a problem away than solve it the same way twice.

Professional proficiency in English is required; Danish is an advantage.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years, as we work with security-classified projects.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Jesper Hougaard Andersen, Senior Manager, Core Infrastructure Platforms.

In Rewards, we are responsible for the design, governance and continuous development of our global reward programmes and frameworks. You will be a key partner to the Senior Director Global Rewards & People Analytics on Executive Rewards, supporting analyses, market insights, presentations, remuneration governance and the development of future reward solutions.

“We are an ambitious and engaged team focused on developing solutions that are relevant, engaging and aligned with business needs, while ensuring successful implementation across the organisation”, says Wandunia Pontoppidan, Senior Director, Global Rewards.

The job

In preparation for our Remuneration Committee meetings, you will partner closely with Senior Director, Global Rewards & People Analytics on executive remuneration and the ongoing evolution of our variable pay programmes. You will analyse current practices, assess market trends and alternative approaches, and develop recommendations that help ensure our reward programmes remain competitive, effective and aligned with our strategic priorities.

In close collaboration with Reward colleagues, people partners and business leaders, you will be responsible for:

•    Supporting Remuneration Committee activities, including benchmarking, analytics, presentation materials and recommendations related to executive remuneration.

•    Supporting annual Executive Leadership Team reward reviews and reporting activities.

•    Reviewing and designing short and long-term incentive programmes, including implementation planning and change communications.

•    Partnering with leaders and people partners on position evaluations and salary recommendations for new hires and promotions at ‘Director’ level and above.

•    Conducting organisational and remuneration reviews and contributing to projects that strengthen our reward offerings across geographies.

•    Contributing to country benchmarking and annual salary review activities, including salary range development and budgeting during peak periods.

You will work with senior stakeholders and translate complex information into clear decision-making material. You will challenge the status quo and balance thorough analysis with pragmatic solutions. Drawing on data, market insights and external trends, you will help shape reward solutions that support both business priorities and the employee experience.

What you bring

We are looking for someone who can build credibility and influence through strong relationships, sound judgement and thoughtful communication. You are confident in your expertise, while remaining curious, open to feedback and keen to learn from others. You are ambitious and always strive for great results together with your team and colleagues, and you know how to balance high quality with timely deliveries.

You understand the critical link between reward design, people data and technology. You are comfortable working with people data structures, governance and system implications, ensuring that reward frameworks can be translated into practical, compliant and efficient solutions across platforms.

Given the nature of the role, you handle sensitive information with discretion and sound judgement, and confidentiality is a natural part of how you work.

Qualifications and personality

We expect that you:

•    Hold a relevant Masters’ degree

•    Have +5 years of experience working in Rewards in a global context.

•    Have experience working with executive remuneration and various long-term incentive instruments.

•    Possess strong stakeholder relations and collaboration skills

•    Have a curious and analytical mindset, and the ability to comprehend complex data sets.

•    Can convert data into findings and recommendations through simple and appealing visuals.

•    Are structured, organised and have a strong eye for detail

•    Are strong in Excel and PowerPoint and can apply AI

•    Communicate fluently in English, both verbally and in writing

This position offers a global perspective, with collaboration across our 42 countries. The role combines analytical depth with stakeholder engagement, translating complex data into insights and decision materials for senior stakeholders.

jobs.occupation: Senior Backend Developer, Product and Data
jobs.description:
What we are building

Someone researching a purchase might start in ChatGPT, compare options in Perplexity, run a Google search, then go back to an AI assistant to decide. The companies being compared have little idea where they show up in that chain or what gets said about them, and very few can measure it today.

We build the infrastructure that measures it. Every platform we track changes under us, and none of them offers a feed, so we collect the data ourselves. Three products run on it:

• AccuRanker is the rank tracking and SEO analytics platform. Rankings, competitor movement, keyword research, dashboards, forecasting.

• AccuLLM tracks brand visibility inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overview, and AI Mode.

• AccuSERP is a search data API we sell to other companies in the industry. On a normal day that means 27 billion rows inserted, 85 million web requests collected, 80 million background jobs run, and 64 million analytical queries served. Eight people build and run all of it.

This job is on the product side: the backend, the data models, and the query paths that run on top of what we collect.

What you will work on

• Build features across AccuRanker and AccuLLM: Django APIs, background jobs, and the data models behind them.

• Design ClickHouse schemas and query paths, and keep the 64 million daily analytical queries fast as the data grows.

• Work across Postgres and ClickHouse, and decide what lives where.

• Own services end to end, from design through deployment to how they behave in production.

• Take features into the React frontend if you want to. Fullstack is welcome, not required.

What you bring

Must have:

• Python and a major web framework (we run Django and Celery), or equivalent depth in another stack.

• Database and API design. Schemas, indexes, migrations, and APIs that hold up under load.

• Comfort in Linux and close to production. Debugging incidents, understanding system behavior, improving observability, making services more reliable.

• Ownership and initiative. You take a problem, you decide how to solve it, and you follow through.

Good to have:

• React and TypeScript, for the optional frontend part of the job.

• ClickHouse or another columnar store at scale.

• Kafka.

• AI agents in production. Tool and context design, structured output and evals.

• Data infrastructure at scale. The ingestion, storage, and query-performance problems our numbers imply.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You own a feature end to end, from idea to production. You can make progress while the problem is still half defined, and a month after it ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety, and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a query, ship a customer-facing feature, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a roadmap handed to you, a narrow technical scope, or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will often be the person deciding both what to build and what “done” means.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.

• Large scale web scraping or browser automation.

• Kafka.

• Python and its common frameworks (Django, Celery, pandas/polars). Our stack runs mostly on Python, but it is not a must if the fundamentals are strong.

• Data infrastructure at scale. The ingestion, storage, and query-performance problems our numbers imply.

Who does well here

People who set a high standard for their own work, and who care about performance, reliability, cost, and operational simplicity.

You own a feature end to end, from idea to production. You can make progress while the problem is still half defined, and a month after it ships, you are still the one who cares about it.

You move fast when speed is what the problem needs, and you know when stability, safety and maintainability matter more.

This field moves fast right now. We expect you to read, try things, and form your own view of what is worth using, without waiting to be told what is new.

The job is wide. In one week you might tune a database, debug a proxy network, and design an agent.

This role is not for you if you want a roadmap handed to you, a narrow technical scope, or a large team around you. We are small, the problems change, and you will often be the person deciding both what to build and what “done” means.

AI at AccuRanker

AI is a big part of the product and of how we build it. AccuLLM sends queries to LLMs all day, customers use our MCP server, and agents and tool design are real engineering problems here.

Being effective with coding agents is becoming a core engineering skill, and it is part of this job. You should be good at giving agents the right context, breaking work into pieces they can execute well, reviewing what they produce, and knowing when to take over yourself. The bar is more high-quality engineering done without outsourcing your understanding and judgment, which is a different thing from using AI a lot.

How we work

• You own services, not tickets. You decide how to solve the problem, make the tradeoffs, and deploy it yourself.

• We ship many times a day. A change can go from idea to production the same day.

• We argue about designs, in writing and in the room. Correctness, cost, and latency are worth arguing about out loud.

• We share what we know and help each other own unfamiliar parts of the system.

What we offer

• Salary set individually on skills and experience.

• Pension, health insurance, flexible working hours, and paid parental leave.

• Hardware of your choosing.

• Office in central Aarhus on Åboulevarden, top floors, panoramic views over the city. The role is on-site, with hybrid options planned for later this year.

• Great lunch.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note to pet@accuranker.com, in Danish or English.

We review applications as they come in and hire as soon as we find the right person, so send yours when it is ready.

Questions about the role are welcome. Call our CTO, Peter Emil Tybirk, on +45 61 41 77 41.

About us:

Founded in Copenhagen, Denmark, in 2014, Templafy’s success is built by our 60+ employee nationalities found at offices around the world. We believe that when people feel valued, heard, and empowered, they perform at their best—creating a win for all. About the role and company:

I'm using AI to write the job posting, and I asked Codex to use the Slack connector to collect some "cultural proof points" about what it's like working at Templafy. This is what it came up with:

Templafy engineering culture comes across as pragmatic, product-close, technically opinionated, and unusually open about trade-offs.

· Engineers are expected to think like product builders, not just implementers. Threads often connect technical work to customer demos, pilots, product quality, adoption, and user feedback

· Pragmatism is a real value. There’s repeated language around simple/explicit code, logical PR chunks, avoiding feature creep, solving the 80% case first, building MVPs, and getting something testable into users’ hands quickly

· Quality matters, but in a practical way. Tests, E2E coverage, evals, pipeline health, flaky tests, feature-flag cleanup, and technical health all show up as shared concerns

· Engineers are candid and trusted to challenge scope. I saw people questioning whether work should be bugs vs feature requests, whether backlog items are clutter, when to pause work, and when a “quick fix” is acceptable

· Cross-functional collaboration is very present. PMs, design, solutions, support, security, platform, and product engineering are all in the same threads negotiating quality bars, customer urgency, UX, risk, and ownership

· AI/tooling curiosity is strong, but not naive. The AI guild and engineering channels show people experimenting with code review agents, AGENTS.md, evals, Codex/Claude workflows, guardrails, and agentic SDLC, while also worrying about learning, friction, false positives, security, and long-term maintainability

· There’s a bias toward async feedback and shared learning. Moving sprint review-style updates into short videos and Slack feedback is a good culture signal: fewer meetings, more continuous visibility

· Ownership is distributed. People jump in to unblock, sanity-check, investigate, create PRs, clean up flags, or hand over work when someone is away. The tone is informal but accountable

Small caution: I would avoid selling the culture as “perfectly polished.” The honest version is stronger: Templafy looks like a place where engineers have real agency, real product context, and real technical messes to improve.

The rest of this job posting is probably more like what you'd expect.

What You’ll Do

You will:

• 
Collaborate with Product and Design to turn ambiguous problems into usable solutions

Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully as part of your everyday engineering workflow

• 
Make technical decisions within your area and contribute to broader architecture discussions

Write reliable, maintainable code that fits existing patterns and systems

• 
Use tests and fast feedback loops to support confident delivery

• 
Build early versions of ideas to evaluate real behavior instead of debating hypotheticals

• 
Help simplify product paths, remove complexity, and make features easier to test and maintain

• 
Debug issues, improve performance, and support production systems

• 
Help the team balance delivery speed, technical quality, and customer impact

• 
Contribute to engineering practices, code reviews, and technical discussions

What We’re Looking For

We’re looking for someone who enjoys product context and wants to be part of shaping what gets built, not only how it gets built.

You probably have:

• 
Strong experience building production software in a product engineering team

• 
Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools in real development work

• 
The judgment to use AI tools without outsourcing your understanding of the system

Good technical judgment and the ability to make pragmatic trade-offs

Experience with modern web application development

The ability to challenge scope constructively and keep work focused

Nice To Have

Experience with cloud platforms, CI/CD, observability, distributed systems

Experience building AI-enabled products, agentic workflows, evals, or prompt/tooling systems

• 
Interest in improving developer experience, technical health, and team practices

What You’ll Join

You’ll join a product engineering team that cares about building useful software, learning quickly, and keeping the systems healthy enough that we can keep moving. We value people who can ask good questions, make things simpler, and help the team find the right trade-off when there is no perfect answer.

This is a good role for someone who wants meaningful product ownership, close collaboration with non-engineering colleagues, and enough technical complexity to make simplification genuinely valuable. We are looking for someone who can move fast, but who also knows that the fastest teams are usually the ones that keep their systems understandable.

Role Summary

Working closely with our production technicians, quality specialists, and engineering teams, you will ensure every robot leaving our facility meets strict performance, safety, and reliability standards.

Key Responsibilities

Mechatronic Assembly & Integration

•

**Qualifications & Competencies

Preferred / Nice-to-Have

Knowledge of ESD-sensitive electronics handling and clean-assembly practices.

Basic understanding or conversational ability in Danish.

**Who you are

• 
Team Player: You enjoy working in a collaborative, international environment where team members support each other to meet production targets.

**What we offer

Application Process

jobs.description:
With more than 3,000 employees, Deloitte is the largest audit and consultancy firm in Denmark. We tailor solutions across Audit, Tax, Financial Advisory Services, Enterprise Risk Services, Technology and Transformations.

Deloitte Technology & Transformation is seeking an ambitious Analyst/Consultant with a passion for strategic people-centred management consulting and digital transformation. If you’re ready to apply your expertise and make an impact, we’d love to hear from you!

About the team

Who will you be working with?

You will join Deloitte’s evolving HR Strategy & Technology practice within Deloitte Consulting (Technology & Transformation) as an analyst or consultant (level dependent on experience).

You will be part of our strategy and operations community where we focus on the advisory side of HR transformation. We help clients reimagine their HR functions and operating models by combining strategic thinking with operational excellence. From leading complex end-to-end HR transformations to advising on the latest human capital trends and best practices, our consultants collaborate closely with senior HR professionals to align organizations with strategic goals, optimize HR processes, and gain a competitive edge.

If you're passionate about making a difference on the people side of strategy in a collaborative, international environment, seize this opportunity to apply for a full-time position with Deloitte's HR Strategy & Technology team.

Job Description

What work will you be doing?

Emphasizing growth and impact, our team cultivates a supportive culture where everyone can thrive. Through social activities and collaboration within our team and across Deloitte, we prioritize delivering results for our clients while fostering a supportive environment. As an Analyst/Consultant, you will collaborate closely with experienced consultants on client projects, contributing to HR strategy and transformation initiatives for multinational corporations. Additionally, you will support business development efforts and contribute to internal initiatives such as employer branding and learning programs based on your interests and background.

In this role, you will make an impact by:

• Approach each engagement as a collaborative case — diagnosing client needs through stakeholder interviews and organizational analysis, leveraging AI and data-driven insights, and co-creating solutions with HR leaders and business stakeholders.

• Develop comprehensive HR strategies aligned with organisational goals and objectives, collaborating closely with clients, management teams, and stakeholders through meetings and and workshops.

• Conducting research, data collection, and analysis to provide valuable insights to clients,

• Collaborating with project teams to develop high-quality deliverables, including documents and presentations, for client projects.

Qualifications

Who we are looking for?

We’re looking for a curious and analytical thinker who enjoys crafting creative solutions to complex challenges. You communicate your ideas clearly and confidently, helping others understand and embrace your advice. You value close collaboration with clients and enjoy working in fast-paced, diverse, and multidisciplinary teams.

You have the following skills and experience:

• A Master’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Strategy, IT, or a related field.

• Good interpersonal skills, workshop facilitation, and a collaborative approach to teamwork

• A genuine interest in human capital strategies and strategic organisational development.

We are particularly interested in candidates who also bring:

• Outstanding academic achievement.

• Experience within HR transformation and HR life-cycle processes.

• Experience from the consulting industry.

Even if you do not see yourself in all the bullets above, we encourage you to apply if you believe your skills can contribute to our team’s success**.

Additional Information

We're looking for someone who can start as soon as possible. If you're ready to make an impact immediately, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply, please upload your resume, bachelor's and master's degree transcripts, and any other relevant documents through our application portal.

Instead of a traditional cover letter, we request that you respond to the following two questions, with each answer limited to a maximum of 200 words. These responses will provide us with a deeper understanding of your qualifications and interest in the role:

• What interests and motivates you about pursuing a career in HR Strategy & Technology consulting, and what unique contributions do you envision bringing to this role?

• How have your educational and/or professional experiences prepared you to work as an Analyst/Consultant at Deloitte?

We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

jobs.occupation: PhD Student in Computational Molecular Design - DTU Chemical Engineering
jobs.description:
If you are interested about establishing your career in an interdisciplinary area related to chemical engineering, novel materials design and advanced computational methods and you are looking for the best possible foundation for fulfilling your dreams and ambitions, then you should consider this opportunity.

We invite you to apply for a PhD position on a newly established project at the Center of Energy Resources Engineering, DTU Chemical Engineering.

You will be involved in the development, parameterization and validation of new coarse-grained molecular models and the development and implementation of systematic molecular simulation methods for novel polymers, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and other advanced complex materials and composites that are promising for industrial sustainable technologies. Molecular simulation output will be used for the training of machine learning models and prediction of properties for materials not synthesized in the lab, yet. In parallel, you will be part of a project that brings together experimental and computational research groups from DTU Chemical Engineering and DTU Energy. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to contribute to the development of a powerful computational platform based on multi-scale methodologies for the design of novel materials to be used for various sustainable energy technologies, such as CO2 capture, H2 storage and others. You will work with other PhD students and post-docs with similar expertise and passion for Molecular Thermodynamics, Molecular Simulation, and/or Machine Learning. You will collaborate with researchers from other groups involved in the project. A successful candidate for this position should have strong knowledge of the fundamentals in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science or closely related discipline.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Development and validation of new molecular models at the atomistic or coarse-grained level,
• Development of new, and implementation and extension of existing simulation methodologies aiming to improve efficiency and accuracy,
• Use of these computational methods to study properties of various advanced materials,
• Dissemination of research achievements through peer-reviewed publications in top rated journals and highly prestigious international conferences,
• Successfully completion of PhD courses and pursue of teaching assistant work as part of the DTU PhD program,
• Supervision of BSc and MSc student projects.
We are looking for highly motivated and academically strong candidates who have: 

• Strong programming skills, 
• Proven research experience in molecular thermodynamics, molecular simulation and/or physics inspired-machine learning,
• Hands-on experience with one of the widely used molecular simulation platforms such as GROMACS, LAMMPS, RASPA, or similar, 
• Ability to work and think independently while contributing to successful completion of collaborative research projects,
• Good written and oral communication skills in English. 
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Professors Ioannis Economou, Xiaodong Liang, Georgios Kontogeorgis and possibly other members of CERE based on the application documents, alignment of the candidates with the qualifications mentioned above, and the impressions during the interview. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years. 

Starting date is 1 February 2027 (or close to this, according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Ioannis Economou at ioannis.economou@qatar.tamu.edu or Georgios Kontogeorgis at gk@kt.dtu.dk 

You can read more about DTU Chemical Engineering at kt.dtu.dk and about CERE at https://www.cere.dtu.dk/ 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 31 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter),
• Curriculum vitae, 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale,
• 3 names with contact details of individuals who can provide input regarding the academic competence and research experience of the candidate. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Center for Energy Resources Engineering at DTU pursues research excellence in applied thermodynamics and biothermodynamics, carbon capture utilization and storage, resources valorization, scientific computing and other related areas. It facilitates a safe and secure transition to sustainable energy. It contributes to engineering research education and supplies excellent engineers to our industrial partners and to society at large. 

The Department of Chemical and Biochemical Engineering at DTU is a leader in innovative teaching and research, built on core technical subjects and engineering scientific disciplines. Teaching and research cover separation processes, reaction engineering, dynamics and process regulation, process and facility planning, unit operations, heat transmission, fluid mechanics and applied thermodynamics. The Department enjoys very close relations with international partners, including a wide range of industrial companies.  

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.occupation: Marie Skłodowska-Curie PhD fellowship in Learning and Optimization Algorithms for Carbon-Aware Datacenter Fleets - DTU Compute
jobs.description:
A Marie Skłodowska-Curie PhD fellowship is available in the Embedded Systems Engineering (ESE) section at DTU Compute. You will be one of the 15 Doctoral Candidates (DCs) of the MSCA Doctoral Network AEGIS, Adaptive Grid-Interactive Edge Datacenter Fleets, which Prof. Paul Pop, DTU, coordinates together with 10 partners across Europe.

This is a software and algorithms project. You will design algorithms and build software that decide where AI workloads run and when datacenter sites change their power use, so that hundreds of separate sites act as one carbon-efficient grid resource. The project does not involve electronics, FPGAs, or low-level embedded development, and it does not require prior knowledge of datacenters or energy systems: with a strong background in algorithms and data structures, you can learn the optimization methods and the domain during the PhD.

Marie Skłodowska-Curie fellowships are among the most respected and best-paid PhD positions in Europe. AEGIS sits where two fast-growing fields meet: datacenters and AI infrastructure on one side, energy and power systems on the other. Few people can work across both, so the skills you build here are scarce and in high demand. Our graduates will be ready for roles at cloud and datacenter operators, energy companies, grid operators, telecom companies, and in academia.

As an MSCA Doctoral Candidate, you will receive: (i) a competitive salary and employment conditions in accordance with the applicable Danish collective agreement and MSCA rules; (ii) two funded secondments, at TU Berlin and at Center Denmark; and (iii) a network-wide training program. The MSCA mobility and, where applicable, family contributions form part of the total employment remuneration and are not necessarily paid as separate supplements.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD project is DC13, Fleet-Level Workload Shaping with Live Grid Signals. You will build the central orchestration engine of the AEGIS fleet: reacting to live grid signals, it decides where to place, pause, or move workloads, and which sites should change their power use with batteries, cooling, and adaptable compute. You will be responsible for:

• Designing a multi-agent orchestrator that can handle multiple datacenter sites.
• Implementing multi-timescale control, from sub-second to hourly decisions.
• Developing learning-based decision methods, such as contextual bandits with bounded-regret guarantees.
• Building a counterfactual analysis toolkit that estimates the carbon savings of different orchestration policies.
• Publishing and disseminating research in international conferences and journals.
• Collaborating with the academic and industrial partners in AEGIS, and contributing to the department with service work, including being a Teaching Assistant.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

We expect that you have:

• Strong algorithms and data structures, and solid programming skills.
• A background in one or more of: machine learning, reinforcement learning, combinatorial optimization, operations research, or distributed systems.
• Curiosity, initiative, and the drive to own a problem end to end.
• Good spoken and written English.
The standard MSCA eligibility criteria also apply:

• No doctoral degree. At the date of recruitment you must not yet hold a PhD.
• Mobility rule. You must not have lived or done your main activity (work or studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months just before you are recruited. Short stays such as holidays do not count.
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of applicants will be based on academic qualifications, strength in algorithms and programming, motivation and initiative, and fit with the research area. The assessment will be carried out by an academic assessment committee.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

At DTU Compute, we have a large focus on creating a good working environment. Our work with diversity and inclusion is an essential part of that. We believe that having a good working environment is a necessary foundation to provide excellent research, teaching, supervision and innovation.

At DTU Compute, we have about 140 PhD students. We offer several events and activities for all our PhD students such as annual PhD Bazaar, onboarding course where you will meet other PhD students, and you can join our PhD Club that organizes BBQs, board games events, lunches etc. 

You can read more about DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is full-time.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Prof. Paul Pop (paupo@dtu.dk). You can read more about the AEGIS network at aegis-dn.eu, the DC13 project page at aegis-dn.eu/positions/dc13, DTU Compute at www.compute.dtu.dk, and about Paul Pop. More details on relevant research problems are available from Paul Pop's Google Scholar page.

Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

jobs.occupation: L&S Category Specialist - Material Handling Equipment Procurement
jobs.description:
Please note: This is a full-time office-based role (5 days/week)

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark

Opportunity

Are you curious, driven by impact, and excited by the idea of shaping how a global logistics leader manages its assets in the AI era?

We are looking for a Category Specialist to join our Material Handling Equipment (MHE) category team at a pivotal moment: Maersk is building an AI-powered asset platform (AssetIQ) that is transforming how we plan, source, and manage assets across their full lifecycle.

In this role, you will bring your live, real-world category and supplier experience directly into that transformation — partnering closely with the product team behind our new AI-guided workflows to solve real category problems without delay, so our processes develop, scale, and deliver Procurement and Asset Management Excellence from day one.

Alongside this, you will support and drive core category work — sourcing, supplier performance, and asset lifecycle optimization for our global MHE fleet — translating data and insight into decisions that create measurable value across our operations.

What We Offer

At Maersk, you will join a global team responsible for a strategically important category with significant spend and business impact — and you will do so at a moment when the category itself is being reinvented. You will work hand-in-hand with our inhouse platform development team as their category partner, helping shape live, AI-guided processes rather than inheriting a finished system. Alongside this, you will gain exposure to global stakeholders, supplier negotiations, category strategy development, and operational improvement initiatives, building deep expertise in logistics, material handling equipment, and AI-enabled asset management.

Category Management & Procurement

• Support and drive execution of category strategies for Material Handling Equipment (MHE).

• Coordinate sourcing activities including RFQs, tenders, negotiations, and contracting.

• Collaborate with regional procurement teams to consolidate demand and maximize value creation.

• Support supplier relationship management and performance improvement initiatives.

• Contribute to commercial discussions and negotiations with key suppliers.

Data, AI & Business Excellence

• Analyze spend, supplier, contract, and asset data — using our AI-powered asset platform — to identify optimization opportunities.

• Surface and personally resolve real category and supplier challenges from sourcing and asset management, turning your hands-on expertise into streamlined data enabled workflows.

• Take new AI-guided processes from concept to category-wide standard: co-creating workflows with the digital team, pressure-testing them in live sourcing situations, and scaling what works.

• Support and drive reporting, category performance tracking, and business case development.

Who We Are Looking For

• Experience within logistics, procurement, category management, supply chain, warehousing operations, or a related field.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to partner effectively across business and supplier teams.

• Applied analytical skills and the ability to translate data into business insights.

• Commercial mindset with an understanding of supplier management and negotiations.

• Genuinely passionate about how AI and digital platforms can transform established ways of working.

• Curious, proactive, and motivated to drive improvements and challenge the status quo.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Engineering, Business, Economics, or a related field.

• Experience within logistics, warehousing, or handling equipment environments.

• Exposure to sourcing, category management, supplier relationship management, or procurement analytics.

• Familiarity with Agentic AI Platforms, procurement systems, reporting tools, or data analysis platforms.

Success in This Role

You will thrive in this role if you are intrinsically motivated by impact — energized by combining procurement, stakeholder engagement, analytics, and problem-solving to create meaningful business value, and genuinely curious about how AI can reshape the way we work. You are comfortable working across functions, building strong supplier and stakeholder relationships, and partnering with our AssetIQ team to turn real category challenges into scalable digital solutions — helping to lift Procurement and Asset Management Excellence at Maersk to the next level.

Join us and help shape how we source, manage, and optimize assets at Maersk — where category expertise meets AI-driven transformation.

Maersk is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we embrace different styles of thinking. Maersk is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applicants without regard to race, colour, gender, sex, age, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy or parental leave, veteran status, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with all legal requirements.
